procedures.procedure: Review all transactions in the five days around quarter-ends and test whether genuine derecognition criteria are met
Confirm repo balances and terms with counterparties, including any affiliated funds
Test collateral valuation and haircut calculations against current market prices and the desk's risk policy
Review the disclosures of secured financing under IFRS 7 including the nature of collateral

scenarios.line_item: Fund NAV and unit capital (mutual fund)
scenarios.client_context: The fund administrator (an outsourced service provider) calculates the daily NAV. This quarter the administrator migrated to a new accounting platform and several corporate-action batches (a stock split and two dividends) failed to process, leaving prices in the NAV wrong for a week before detection. The management company charges the fund a performance fee calculated on the quarter's NAV growth.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Failed corporate-action batches make NAVs wrong — investors traded at incorrect prices.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The performance fee is computed from possibly erroneous NAVs, directly transferring value to the manager.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Migration-period transactions may be lost between old and new platforms.

procedures.procedure: Obtain a service organization report (SOC 1 / ISAE 3402) on the administrator, read it, and evaluate the migration-period control exceptions
Reperform the NAV for one day: independently price holdings, rebook the stock split and dividends, and compare to the published NAV
Recalculate the performance fee from corrected NAVs and assess whether the fee and compensating payments to investors are correctly recorded
Confirm holdings with the fund's custodian and reconcile to the administrator's positions

scenarios.client_context: Management fees are calculated monthly on average assets under management pulled from the transfer agent. One institutional client negotiated a fee holiday for the first quarter, but the billing system kept charging full fees until May before the credit notes were raised in bulk. A new fund launched in December is being charged fees based on committed capital, not the contract's 'invested capital' definition.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Fee basis (committed vs invested capital) and the unprocessed fee holiday drive systematic overbilling.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Bulk credit notes raised in May against Q1 charges create a cut-off problem in the income statement.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate a sample of monthly fees against each fund's fee schedule and AUM data, including the holiday period and the new fund
Trace the credit notes to the client's fee agreement and the rebilling approval, and assess period allocation
Reconcile AUM used for billing to the transfer agent's register and the custody records
Compare fee income per fund to budget and investigate significant variances

scenarios.client_context: The insurer implemented IFRS 17 this year. Premium revenue is still recognized at policy inception (the old IFRS 4 habit) for the large annual motor portfolio, while the service expense is spread over the coverage period. Commissions to aggregators and comparison sites are capitalized... some of them, inconsistently. The actuarial team's coverage-unit pattern in the model differs from the policy term data.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Revenue at inception with expenses over time front-loads profit — a direct breach of IFRS 17's coverage-units model.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Inconsistent commission capitalization is a transition trap; the standard requires a consistent approach.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Annual policies spanning the year-end need allocation of premiums over coverage periods.

procedures.procedure: Reperform the IFRS 17 revenue recognition for a sample of policies: coverage units, allocation and the earned pattern versus the old IFRS 4 outcome
Review the policy for acquisition costs and test a sample of aggregator commissions for consistent capitalization and amortization
Reconcile policy counts and premium data from the policy admin system to the IFRS 17 model
Confirm annual premium income with a sample of policyholders
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirming premiums received tests that the policy exists and was paid — but the actual risk here is the timing and pattern of recognition under IFRS 17, not whether the cash arrived. The procedure looks substantive but misses the real assertion.

scenarios.client_context: The ceding insurer recovers part of its claims from reinsurers. Recoverables are booked gross at claim amounts without any loss allowance, even though one major reinsurer was downgraded to junk during the year. Retrocession commissions (commissions received from reinsurers) were netted against claims expense rather than deferred and amortized over the reinsurance coverage.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A junk-rated reinsurer's recoverable needs an ECL-style impairment assessment; booking gross is indefensible.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Netting retro commissions against claims distorts both line items and the presentation of the reinsurance result.

procedures.procedure: Confirm recoverables with reinsurers and obtain their financial strength ratings after year-end
Assess the loss allowance on the downgraded reinsurer's recoverable against IFRS 9
Recalculate the deferred retro commission amortization and verify claims expense is presented gross
Review the risk-transfer test documentation for the main quota-share treaty

scenarios.client_context: The bank reports its Liquidity Coverage Ratio to the regulator monthly. The treasury system classifies all retail deposits above 250k as 'stable' funding, and a large single corporate deposit known to be withdrawn after year-end is included in available liquidity at 100%. The LCR fell below 100% in two internal months, which are not reflected in the year-end regulatory submission.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Misclassifying deposit stability and applying no outflow assumption to a known withdrawal overstates the LCR.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Regulatory returns that do not reconcile to the accounting records create ISA 250 regulatory-frame exposure.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Months below 100% must be part of the regulatory dialogue and the accounts' risk disclosures.

procedures.procedure: Reconcile the regulatory LCR submission to the accounting records and the treasury system, category by category
Test the deposit stability classifications against the regulator's criteria, focusing on large retail deposits
Review the outflow assumptions for the corporate deposit with the ALM committee minutes and the client's notice of withdrawal
Assess whether the below-100% months were reported to the regulator and reflected in the liquidity risk disclosure in the notes

scenarios.line_item: Payment float and customer balances (payment institution)
scenarios.client_context: The payment institution holds customer funds in safeguarded accounts. Customer balances are tracked in a separate ledger reconciled to the safeguarding account quarterly. Between reconciliations, incoming payments are matched to customers by reference, but 5% of inflows have no reference and sit in a suspense account — some for over a year. The institution is close to breaching its safeguarding balance requirement.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Unmatched inflows in suspense may include customer balances that never reach the customers' ledger.
assertions_high_risk.rights_and_obligations: Safeguarding balances must at least equal customer payables at all times; a shortfall is a regulatory breach.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: A quarterly reconciliation means the monthly positions in between are unverified.

procedures.procedure: Perform an independent reconciliation of the safeguarding accounts to the aggregate customer ledger at year-end, and reperform the suspense account matching
Review aged suspense items, trace a sample back to originating payers, and assess whether they belong to customers
Obtain confirmations of safeguarding balances from the banks holding the accounts
Review the monthly safeguarding calculations and the correspondence with the regulator on any breaches

scenarios.client_context: The BNPL provider records installment receivables and an ECL provision using default curves from its first two years of data. It launched in a new country mid-year with a different consumer profile, but the same curves are applied. Receivables are often repaid early, and the revenue model records merchant fees and late fees — the late fee income has tripled while complaints about misleading checkout disclosure pile up.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Default curves from a different market and early repayments make ECL and interest income projections unreliable.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Tripled late fee income amid complaints raises the question of whether fees are valid and enforceable — and ISA 250 regulatory risk.

procedures.procedure: Compare default curves for the new country against local early experience data and recompute ECL
Test a sample of late fee charges to the consumer agreement in force at checkout and review regulator correspondence
Confirm a sample of installment balances with consumers via the app provider's records
Perform a completeness check of merchant fee revenue by reconciling transaction volumes from the merchant portal to the billing engine

scenarios.line_item: Client assets held by a broker (custody)
scenarios.client_context: The broker holds client shares and cash in omnibus accounts at a custodian bank. Client records are maintained in-house. During the year a system glitch duplicated 200 client holdings, and stock lending of client securities to the broker's own market-making desk was authorized by a clause in the fine print of the client agreement that legal counsel has never reviewed.

assertions_high_risk.existence: Duplicated holdings mean records exceed what actually exists — the opposite of the usual direction.
assertions_high_risk.rights_and_obligations: Lending client securities to an affiliated desk may breach custody rules; clients may not have validly consented.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Omnibus accounts can conceal that client assets are insufficient to cover client entitlements.

procedures.procedure: Reconcile the in-house client records to the omnibus custodian statements at the individual security level
Trace the duplication incident to change logs, verify correction, and confirm no client was overcharged fees on phantom holdings
Obtain legal counsel's opinion on the stock-lending clause and the client consent, and evaluate the broker's compliance with client asset rules
Confirm holdings with a sample of clients directly

scenarios.line_item: Derivative positions (commodity hedges by an airline)
scenarios.client_context: The airline hedges jet fuel with oil swaps and options, designating them as cash flow hedges. The hedge documentation for a new tranche references 'fuel cost exposure' but the derivatives are written on crude oil — with no documented assessment of the crude-to-jet fuel correlation. During the year the airline stopped hedging for six months while keeping the derivatives open, and the deferred hedge reserve is large.

assertions_high_risk.existence: Basis risk between crude oil derivatives and jet fuel exposure means hedge accounting may not qualify — the reserve should flow to P&L.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The large deferred reserve parked in equity may conceal losses that belong in income.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: All open derivatives including the de-designated period must be captured in the hedge records.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate hedge effectiveness qualification, including the documented crude-to-jet-fuel relationship and the six-month non-hedged period
Independently value a sample of derivatives using market curves and verify the split between the hedge reserve and P&L
Confirm derivative positions and terms with the counterparties
Review the disclosure of hedge risk and the amounts in the cash flow hedge reserve including the six-month de-designation

scenarios.client_context: Due to an economic downturn the bank restructured a fifth of its SME portfolio: payment holidays, extended terms, interest-only periods. Half of the restructurings were processed by branch staff with a spreadsheet override of the core system's staging rules, keeping the loans in Stage 1 instead of moving to Stage 2 (significant increase in credit risk). The restructuring policy requires 'evidence of viability' that branches documented with one-page self-assessments.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Forbearance without a genuine viability assessment masks credit deterioration — Stage 1 staging understates ECL.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Spreadsheet overrides bypassing the system's staging engine create both error and override risk.

procedures.procedure: Test a sample of restructured loans against IFRS 9's restructuring guidance: viability assessment quality, revised terms and the 12-month vs lifetime ECL staging
Review all staging overrides, reperform the system's own stage calculation, and quantify the ECL impact of differences
Compare post-restructuring payment performance with the viability assumptions
Assess whether modified terms and forbearance disclosures are made in the notes

scenarios.line_item: Pension scheme assets held in pooled vehicles (level 2/3 mix)
scenarios.client_context: The scheme's assets are held via pooled investment vehicles priced by external administrators. A property fund within the pool suspended dealing after a wave of redemption requests, and its administrator continues to publish the pre-suspension price. The scheme's own records still show the suspended fund as a Level 2 asset with the stale price. Contributions received in the final week of December were allocated to units in January.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A stale price on a suspended fund no longer reflects an exit-price fair value and the level classification is wrong.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Late-December contributions must be recognized as scheme assets and liabilities in the right period.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Units in a suspended vehicle may not be realizable — the 'asset' is effectively a claim in a queue.

procedures.procedure: Obtain confirmation of unit holdings from the pool's administrator and the dealing status of the suspended property fund
Independently assess the fair value of the suspended fund units, including manager commentary and redemption queue position, and challenge the Level 2 classification
Trace December contribution schedules to unit allocations and bank records, testing the cut-off
Recalculate the scheme's funding position disclosures using corrected asset values

scenarios.line_item: Premium receivables and unearned premium (life insurer)
scenarios.client_context: The life insurer's agents collect monthly premiums in cash in some regions. Premium income is recorded when the agent remits to head office, not when collected. The unearned premium reserve is calculated on written premiums with a 1/12 pattern even though several flagship products are single-premium with multi-year coverage. One agent has remittances outstanding for three months.

assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Cash-collected premiums recorded on remittance lag the collection date — income is recorded too late.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A 1/12 unearned pattern is wrong for single-premium multi-year products; the reserve is understated.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Unremitted agent cash may never reach head office — a classic misappropriation window.

procedures.procedure: Test remittance cut-off: compare collection dates on agents' receipts books with recorded premium income around year-end
Investigate the agent with three months of unremitted cash: confirm outstanding amounts and verify physical cash and receipts
Recalculate the unearned premium reserve for single-premium products using actual coverage periods
Confirm premium payment records for a sample of policyholders directly

scenarios.line_item: Provision for regulatory fines and remediation (conduct costs)
scenarios.client_context: The regulator is investigating the bank's sales practices for a fee-charging packaged account. The bank's own review, completed in November, found systematic mis-selling to 40,000 customers. No provision has been recognized — the CFO argues the regulator has not yet set the fine amount. Remediation project costs are capitalized as 'intangible - customer relationship restoration'. Prior-year comparatives show similar conduct issues that were resolved at 5x the initial estimate.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: A constructive obligation to remediate 40,000 customers exists regardless of the regulator's decision — no provision is a completeness failure.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Prior conduct history at 5x initial estimates is strong evidence the outflow estimate needs careful challenge.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Capitalizing remediation costs as intangibles is wrong — they are expenses.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the internal mis-selling review, customer complaint data and the board's response to assess whether a constructive obligation exists under IAS 37
Benchmark the remediation estimate against the bank's own prior conduct cases and external industry outcomes
Review the accounting policy for remediation costs and reverse the inappropriate capitalization
Correspond with the regulator via the client, and review legal counsel's assessment of the likely range of outcomes

scenarios.client_context: Campus administrative staff order supplies from a catalogue without purchase approval limits. The finance clerk is the wife of the operations manager, and the same monthly amount has been charged for the last eight months. No goods-received checks are performed.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Absence of purchase approvals and goods-received checks means expenses could be recorded for goods never received.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Flat monthly charges suggest estimates rather than actual invoices, risking misstated amounts.

procedures.procedure: Vouch a sample of office supply expense entries to supplier invoices and evidence of receipt by campus departments
Review the supplier master file for duplicate or similar vendor names and check who approved their creation
Scan the expense ledger for round-sum recurring monthly entries and enquire into their basis
Confirm year-end supplier balances with the office supplies vendor directly
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirming payables balances addresses completeness of liabilities, not whether the recorded expenses actually occurred; the flagged risk is fictitious or estimated expense, which needs vouching to invoices and receipts.

procedures.procedure: Trace a sample of catalogue purchase orders raised in the last week of the year to the expense ledger
procedures.trap_explanation: The scenario flags occurrence and accuracy of recurring flat amounts; period-boundary cut-off was not identified as a risk, and purchases do not become expense until goods are received, so this procedure tests a low-risk assertion here.

scenarios.client_context: Sixty delivery vans collect cash-on-delivery payments; drivers hand in cash weekly and a float of EUR 300 per depot is maintained in a lockable box. The depot supervisor counts the cash alone and records it in a spreadsheet. Two depots show identical cash counts three months running.

assertions_high_risk.existence: Cash held in depots is a theft-prone asset counted by one person with no independent witness, and identical repeated counts suggest the balance is not really being verified.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Cash collected by drivers before year-end may still be in transit or unrecorded when the ledger is struck.

procedures.procedure: Attend surprise cash counts at a sample of depots and reconcile counts to the spreadsheet and general ledger
Trace driver collection records for the final week of the year to cash banked and to the cash ledger
procedures.trap_explanation: Cut_off is not among the assertions flagged as risky, and for the completeness risk the useful part of this procedure is tracing collections to the ledger; the year-end boundary emphasis is misdirected.

procedures.procedure: Obtain a bank confirmation for each depot bank account showing balances and transactions in the final month
Review the spreadsheet change log and interview two drivers about the hand-in routine
Recalculate the float reimbursement top-up entries to the petty cash account
procedures.trap_explanation: Recalculating top-ups tests arithmetic accuracy of a control account, but the risk is physical existence of cash and one-person counts; the procedure does not address whether the cash is actually there.

scenarios.client_context: A 12-screen cinema sells about 70% of tickets at the door for cash. The till system produces a daily Z-report, but the manager can edit reported totals before they are posted to the ledger. Concessions income is recorded in the same account as ticket sales.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: High-volume cash sales with manager-editable till reports create a classic skimming risk: cash takings can be removed before they ever reach the ledger.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Manual editing of Z-reports before posting means reported sales may not match till readings.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Mixing ticket and concession income in one account misclassifies revenue streams.

procedures.procedure: For a sample of days, compare the ledger's daily sales posting to the unedited system log of till transactions
Observe the cash count and bank deposit preparation at two cinemas and reconcile deposits to daily takings
Compare admissions recorded by the system with ticket stock issued to the box office for the same period
Perform analytical review of tickets sold per film against distributor royalty statements
Review the ticket refunds listing and match refunds to original sales transactions
procedures.trap_explanation: Testing refunds addresses whether recorded revenue was reversed appropriately — an occurrence-side concern for recorded sales — but the flagged risk is cash skimming before recording (completeness); refund testing cannot detect sales that never entered the ledger.

scenarios.client_context: The group accrues monthly electricity and gas usage for 14 restaurants using 3% of prior-year winter costs. Two new sites opened in November, and the energy supplier changed billing systems in December, with December invoices not expected until February.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: The supplier's billing-system changeover means December usage may never be invoiced, so an accrual based only on received invoices would miss the liability.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The 3%-of-prior-year rule ignores two new sites, so the accrual is understated for the expanded estate.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate the year-end accrual using meter readings or smart-meter data for each site, including the new restaurants
Inspect January and February supplier invoices when received and reconcile usage straddling the year-end to the accrual
Enquire of management about the supplier's billing transition and review correspondence confirming unbilled periods
Confirm the final settled December invoice directly with the energy supplier
procedures.trap_explanation: Direct confirmation is fine for recorded balances, but the stated risk is that no December invoice exists yet; confirming what the supplier has billed only captures items the supplier managed to invoice and may miss usage unbilled due to the system changeover. It also tests the wrong direction if used alone — the accrual must be built from usage data, not from invoices.

scenarios.client_context: Members buy 12-month contracts billed annually in advance; the January renewal wave accounts for 60% of annual fees. The billing system posts fees on the contract start date, but some members argue for a pro-rata start. Freezing of memberships during the year is handled by manual credit notes approved by branch managers.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Freeze credit notes approved by branch managers, who also face churn targets, may be incorrectly applied, understating receivables and revenue.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Annual advance billing concentrated in one month increases the risk that recorded receivables include non-existent or cancelled members.

procedures.procedure: Sample January-billed memberships and agree contract start dates and fee amounts to signed agreements
Inspect freeze credit notes approved after year-end and assess whether freezing criteria were met and timing was appropriate
Compare the number of billed memberships per branch to monthly door-access system counts
Age the receivables ledger and review the allowance against historic collection patterns of January-billed members
Send positive confirmations to a sample of members for their annual fee balance
procedures.trap_explanation: Member confirmations may evidence the balance, but the flagged risks are manager-approved credit notes and billing of possibly cancelled members; confirmation responses are unreliable for testing credit-note appropriateness and slow for a churn-driven population. Testing the credit notes themselves addresses the risk directly.

scenarios.client_context: The company receives roughly 400 supplier invoices a week, keyed into the ledger by one clerk. A flood of year-end deliveries for the holiday season sits in the goods-in yard; delivery notes are matched to invoices only when the supplier chases payment. No goods-received-not-invoiced (GRNI) report exists.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Payables are recorded from supplier invoices, not receipts, and invoices are only matched on demand — goods received before year-end without invoices will be omitted.

procedures.procedure: Perform a search for unrecorded liabilities: inspect January and February payments and supplier statements for December-dated supplies
Compare goods-received notes for the final two weeks to invoices recorded in the payables ledger
Obtain supplier statements for the largest 20 vendors and reconcile them to ledger balances, investigating reconciling items
Vouch a sample of recorded payables to purchase orders and goods-received notes
procedures.trap_explanation: Vouching tests existence of recorded liabilities, but completeness is the flagged risk; the danger here is payables that are missing, which vouching cannot detect.

procedures.procedure: Review the finance clerk's open item listing for debit balances and confirm netting arrangements with suppliers
procedures.trap_explanation: Netting reviews address classification between payables and receivables, which is not the flagged risk; the context points entirely to omitted liabilities due to invoice-driven recording.

scenarios.client_context: Cellar stock of kegs, bottles and casks is counted quarterly by pub managers who also earn a bonus tied to venue profit. The brewery's trade receivable from inter-pub stock transfers is growing. Keg deposits payable to the brewery are tracked in a separate register.

assertions_high_risk.existence: Manager counts, driven by profit bonuses, may overstate stock or record stock not physically present.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Stock delivered in trade between pubs may bypass the standard receipts process and be omitted from counts of receiving venues.

procedures.procedure: Attend cellar counts at a sample of pubs on an unannounced basis, performing own counts and comparing to manager sheets
Review inter-pub transfer notes for the year and trace quantities to both sending and receiving venue stock records
Age slow-moving bottled lines and assess whether selling price has fallen below cost for obsolete stock
Reconcile keg deposit liabilities to kegs physically observed at the pubs
Enquire of pub managers whether they hold any consignment stock on behalf of third-party brands and inspect agreements
procedures.trap_explanation: Enquiries about consignment are relevant when inclusion of third-party stock is a risk; here the flagged risks are bonus-driven overstatement and missed transfers, and oral enquiries alone are weak evidence for either.

scenarios.client_context: The cooperative's balance sheet carries 22 field parcels at cost from decades ago. Last year the board commissioned a valuation for insurance purposes at current market prices, which is double the carrying amount. Adjacent parcels were recently rezoned for residential development.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The insurance valuation and rezoning create a temptation to substitute a market value in the financial statements even though the revaluation model would require a whole-class, regularly reviewed approach.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: If a revaluation is applied piecemeal, the measurement basis disclosure may become misleading.

procedures.procedure: Inspect title deeds or land registry extracts for a sample of parcels and confirm registered ownership by the cooperative
Evaluate whether the revaluation model, if adopted for land, is applied to the entire class with consistent policy and competent valuer support
Confirm that the insurance valuation is not used directly as carrying value under a cost model and recalculate depreciation-free carrying amounts
Recalculate the year's insurance premium expense allocation across the cooperative's members
procedures.trap_explanation: Insurance premium allocation is an income-statement accuracy test on a different line item; it says nothing about land measurement, ownership or disclosure, which are the flagged assertions.

procedures.procedure: Physically visit five parcels and observe boundaries against the cooperative's field register
procedures.trap_explanation: Inspection may support existence of land, but the flagged risks are valuation and disclosure of measurement basis; walking boundaries is a low-value procedure when title deeds already establish existence — the risk direction is measurement, not physical presence.

scenarios.client_context: The company prepaid an agency EUR 1.8m in October for an influencer campaign running from November to August next year. The prepaid balance at year-end equals the full payment less one month amortized. The campaign underperformed in its first month and the contract allows partial refunds if milestones are missed.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Underperformance and refund clauses mean part of the prepayment may not be recoverable through future services; only one month was amortized.
assertions_high_risk.existence: The large prepayment is a single ledger entry; its existence and link to the underlying contract need verification.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the agency contract and payment evidence, and recalculate amortization from campaign commencement to year-end
Compare campaign milestone reports from the agency to contractual service milestones to assess whether remaining services will be delivered
Assess whether any refund claim is warranted and whether recoverability of the remaining prepayment is supported
Discuss with management and, if necessary, the agency's account manager the status of unperformed services
Vouch the October payment through the bank statement to the supplier's remittance advice
procedures.trap_explanation: Vouching the cash payment confirms the payment occurred, but existence of a prepayment asset also depends on the entitlement to future services; with refund clauses and underperformance, the real risk is valuation of the remaining balance, not the payment trail.

scenarios.client_context: Partners approve their own travel expense claims in the system. Client entertainment is charged to project codes to keep utilization margins looking strong. A new policy doubled entertainment limits mid-year, and one project's entertainment spend rose sixfold after the change.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Self-approval by partners with an increased limit creates a risk that personal or non-business costs are claimed.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Charging entertainment to project codes misclassifies expenses and distorts project profitability reporting.

procedures.procedure: Select a sample of partner-approved claims above the new limit and vouch to receipts, itineraries and business purpose evidence
Analyse entertainment spend by project code before and after the policy change and investigate outliers
Review the expense system configuration to verify whether self-approval is blocked and whether limits are system-enforced
Recalculate per-diem amounts against the standard rate table
Confirm a sample of employees' expenses with the corporate card provider statement
procedures.trap_explanation: Card statements evidence card spending but not that costs were business-incurred, and they do not address classification across project codes; matching statements to claims can even look complete while personal spend passes as business.

scenarios.client_context: Annual tuition of EUR 12k per pupil is invoiced at the start of the school year in September, with instalment plans available. Mid-year withdrawals trigger refund calculations under the enrolment contract. The school launched a sibling discount and a bursary scheme this year, both processed as manual invoices by the registrar.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Manual invoices for discounts and bursaries, alongside instalment plans, raise the risk of miscalculated fee amounts and refunds.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: The academic year straddles the reporting year, so revenue recognition must follow the delivery of teaching rather than invoice or receipt dates.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Refund calculations for withdrawals may be applied to boost or smooth reported revenue.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate a sample of manual discount and bursary invoices against the published policy and verify approvals
Trace withdrawals from the pupil register to refund credit notes and recompute refundable amounts under the enrolment contract
Agree the revenue recognition pattern to the contractual obligation to provide teaching across the year and recalculate deferred balances
Reconcile pupils on the attendance register to pupils billed for the year
Confirm outstanding instalment balances with parents of a sample of pupils
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirming receivable balances tests a balance-sheet existence assertion on instalments; the flagged risks are manual pricing errors, refund abuse and recognition timing on the income statement.

scenarios.client_context: During the year the holding company transferred a subsidiary to a new shareholder at book value, appropriated retained earnings to a non-distributable reserve, and revalued a warehouse. The ledger has a single 'reserves' control account maintained in a spreadsheet by one accountant.

assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Distributable versus non-distributable reserves may be mixed, so disclosed amounts available for dividends could be overstated.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The spreadsheet-based single control account raises the risk that movements in the year — transfer, appropriation, revaluation — are posted incorrectly or to the wrong reserve.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate the reserves roll-forward for each reserve category, tracing movements to board minutes and accounting records
Review the accounting policy and note disclosures distinguishing distributable from non-distributable reserves
Confirm the subsidiary transfer was effected at properly authorized book value and trace the entry to the equity register
Agree the warehouse revaluation surplus and related deferred tax to the valuer's report
Confirm dividends paid in the year with the bank and the shareholder register
procedures.trap_explanation: Dividend payment confirmation tests the payments themselves; the flagged risks are misallocation within reserves and distributability disclosure, for which the roll-forward and reserve categorization are the relevant procedures.

scenarios.line_item: Bank charges and overdraft interest expense
scenarios.client_context: The chain runs overdrafts at three banks; interest and fees are accrued monthly by extrapolating last quarter's charge. One bank migrated accounts mid-year and some statements were unavailable. The finance team reconciles statements only quarterly because of staffing shortages.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Missing statements from the bank migration plus quarterly-only reconciliations mean bank charges could be omitted from the ledger.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Extrapolated accruals, rather than actual charges, risk inaccurate expense recognition.

procedures.procedure: Obtain full-year statements from all three banks, including reconstructed statements from the migrated bank, and reconcile charges to the expense ledger
Recalculate interest on the overdraft using average daily balances and the facility margin, comparing to the accrual
Inspect January-February charges on year-end overdraft balances for items relating to the pre-year-end period
Obtain bank confirmations of facility terms, interest rates and fees charged
Vouch a sample of accrued charge entries to the bank's fee invoices
procedures.trap_explanation: The context flags omission (completeness) and extrapolation error (accuracy) on charges; vouching recorded accruals to invoices tests whether recorded items exist, the opposite direction from the risk that some charges are missing entirely.

scenarios.client_context: The group acquired 80% of a homeware chain nine months before year-end. The purchase price was a multiple of the target's EBITDA, which the seller computed. The acquisition-date fair values were produced by the group's own finance team in a spreadsheet; the finance director was previously the target's CFO. Goodwill of EUR 40m arose.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Internally produced fair values in a spreadsheet, prepared under a director with a conflict of interest, create bias risk in the PPA and thus in goodwill.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Contingent consideration, acquisition costs or assumed liabilities may be left out of the PPA because the exercise was done in-house without a checklist.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Purchase-price allocation disclosures may lack required detail given the informal process.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the competence and independence of those who produced the acquisition-date fair values and the methods used for major asset classes
Compare the PPA schedule to the sale agreement to confirm all components — consideration, assumed liabilities, contingent payments — are captured
Review the disclosure note against the required acquisition disclosure elements for the year
Confirm the purchase consideration paid with the group's bank and the seller's solicitors
procedures.trap_explanation: Payment confirmation shows consideration was transferred, but the flagged risks are biased fair values and an incomplete PPA; the cash trail does not test what was allocated to assets and liabilities at acquisition.

procedures.procedure: Vouch a sample of the subsidiary's post-acquisition revenue to customer invoices
procedures.trap_explanation: Post-acquisition revenue testing addresses the subsidiary's own income recognition, not the group's consolidation of the business combination; the risk sits in the acquisition-date PPA prepared by a conflicted team.

scenarios.client_context: The group holds 70% of an Asian joint venture; the local partner holds 30%. The JV made a loss this year while the group's other subsidiaries were profitable. Allocations to NCI are computed on the group's standard consolidation spreadsheet, which still uses the ownership percentage from before the group bought a further 5% last year.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: An outdated ownership percentage in the consolidation spreadsheet misallocates losses between the group and the NCI.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: NCI attribution of comprehensive income and of losses exceeding the NCI's carrying balance must be separately disclosed; the spreadsheet may not distinguish these.

procedures.procedure: Trace the current ownership percentages to share registers and the share purchase agreement for the additional 5% stake
Recalculate profit and loss and OCI allocations to NCI using verified percentages, including treatment of losses in excess of the NCI balance
Review the consolidation spreadsheet change controls and who can edit percentage assumptions
Inspect the NCI note for separate presentation of opening balances, comprehensive income attribution and distributions
Confirm the NCI partner's view of the JV's loss at a meeting with its finance representative
procedures.trap_explanation: Discussing the loss with the minority partner may corroborate the loss figure, but the flagged risk is the allocation mathematics driven by an outdated percentage; the partner's view does not test the group's consolidation entries.

scenarios.client_context: Revenue is generated from billions of call-data records rated by a legacy billing engine. Three months ago a new tariff plan was added and applied retroactively to some subscribers. Roaming partner settlements are received up to two months in arrears. Revenue analysts can manually adjust rated records, and one analyst made 40% of all manual adjustments this year.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: A new tariff plan applied retroactively, processed by a legacy rating engine, risks mis-rating of calls and credits.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Roaming revenue settled in arrears may be omitted, and manual adjustment patterns suggest records could be suppressed.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: The two-month roaming settlement lag concentrates boundary risk around year-end.

procedures.procedure: Re-perform rating on a sample of call-data records under the old and new tariff plans, including retroactively applied subscribers
Analyse manual adjustments by analyst and reason code, and vouch a sample of the high-volume analyst's entries to support
Reconcile roaming partner settlement files received after year-end to the accrued roaming revenue
Obtain an IT audit specialist's report on the billing engine's rating configuration changes and access controls
Confirm year-end balances with the largest roaming partners
procedures.trap_explanation: Partner confirmations address balances receivable or payable; the flagged risks are mis-rating, suppressed records and arrears completeness on revenue itself, which confirmations of balances do not address.

scenarios.client_context: Enterprise contracts are billed monthly in arrears from usage data. Unbilled revenue is estimated at month-end by a bespoke spreadsheet that extrapolates the last posted month. The division's head receives a bonus based on divisional profit, and unbilled revenue grew 35% while billed revenue grew 4%.

assertions_high_risk.existence: Rapid unbilled growth against flat billed revenue suggests the asset may contain amounts not supported by underlying usage or contract entitlement.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Spreadsheet extrapolation, under a profit-bonused division head, creates estimation bias risk in the month-end estimate.

procedures.procedure: Reconcile the unbilled estimate to actual invoices raised in the following period and investigate systematic over/under-estimation
Trace a sample of unbilled amounts to underlying usage data and contract terms permitting arrears billing
Review the spreadsheet's formula logic and version history, and test who can change estimation assumptions
Perform retrospective review of prior-year unbilled estimates against final invoices to quantify bias
Confirm unbilled balances with a sample of enterprise customers
procedures.trap_explanation: Customers cannot confirm amounts they have not yet been billed; the assertion risk is whether the estimate is supported by usage data and is unbiased, which is tested through subsequent invoice reconciliation, not customer confirmation.

scenarios.client_context: The brand works with five media agencies on net-60 payment terms. Marketing accruals at each quarter-end are based on agency estimates emailed as PDFs, not reconciled to delivered media plans. The marketing director is leaving next quarter, and the accrual for the largest agency has been rolled forward unchanged for three quarters.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Agency invoices lag delivery by up to 60 days, and accruals based on emailed estimates may omit campaigns delivered near year-end.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: An accrual rolled forward unchanged for three quarters, as a director exits, is unlikely to reflect actual delivered services.

procedures.procedure: Reconcile year-end marketing accruals per agency to delivered media plans and campaign tracking reports
Inspect agency invoices received after year-end for services delivered before year-end and check inclusion in the accrual
Recalculate the accrual for the largest agency from its campaign delivery data rather than the rolled-forward estimate
Confirm balances and open engagements directly with the five agencies
procedures.trap_explanation: Agency confirmation of recorded balances does not detect omitted accruals for services delivered but not yet invoiced — the flagged risk; confirmations cover what is already on the ledger, the wrong direction for a completeness concern.

procedures.procedure: Analyse marketing expense as a percentage of sales by quarter and investigate anomalies in the final quarter

scenarios.client_context: Finished goods of chilled ready meals carry a 12-day shelf life. A supermarket delisted two product lines in November, and stock of those lines equals six weeks of current demand. NRV is computed by the production manager in a spreadsheet that uses list prices rather than net of retailer promotional discounts.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Delisted lines with six weeks of supply, valued at list prices ignoring promotional discounts, are at clear NRV write-down risk.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Short shelf-life stock may include expired or spoiled items not yet scrapped.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate NRV for delisted lines using expected selling prices net of promotion and disposal costs, and compare write-downs to the ledger
During count attendance, inspect expiry dates on sampled chilled stock and observe segregation of expired items
Compare post-year-end sales prices achieved for delisted lines to the NRV assumptions
Review the spreadsheet pricing assumptions and who approves updates to list price data
Confirm stock held at the delisted supermarket's regional distribution centre with the retailer
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirming consignment stock with the retailer addresses whether that stock belongs in inventory; the flagged risks are NRV write-downs on the company's own stock and expired items — measurement and existence of own holdings, not third-party title.

scenarios.client_context: The founder's son owns a components supplier that provides 15% of the company's raw materials. Purchase prices are set annually by the founder without benchmarks. Two supplier invoices a month are approved by the son himself as acting purchasing manager. The audit committee does not exist; oversight is by the founder alone.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Prices set by the founder without market benchmarks may not be at arm's length, overstating cost and understating profit.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Self-approved invoices from an owner-affiliated supplier raise the risk of purchases that never occurred or duplicate billing.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Related-party transactions require disclosure of nature, amounts and terms; a governance-light company may omit them.

procedures.procedure: Benchmark component prices to quoted market prices or independent supplier quotes and quantify differences
Vouch a sample of self-approved invoices to goods-received notes and production consumption records
Review the related-party disclosure note against the identified transactions for completeness of nature, amount and terms
Scan the supplier master file and payment runs for other entities connected to the family
Compare gross margin by month and investigate months following the annual price reset
procedures.trap_explanation: Monthly margin analysis is indirect and confounded by volume and production variances; the direct risk — non-arm's-length pricing set by the founder — is tested by benchmarking prices, not by margins.

scenarios.client_context: Annual passes sold in waves around the summer peak are recognized over 12 months from sale. The park introduced a free-months promotion in the discount period, and some passes were sold by third-party resellers who retain a commission. The revenue team defers income in a spreadsheet keyed by sale date, not by first-visit entitlement.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Free-month promotions and reseller commissions change the transaction price and the deferral period; a spreadsheet keyed only by sale date misallocates revenue between periods.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Deferred income supported only by spreadsheet rows may include refunded or expired passes with no remaining obligation.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Sales concentrated around the summer peak create period-boundary allocation risk.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate the deferred income balance for a sample of promotions and reseller sales using contract price net of commission and the correct service period
Reconcile deferred income to the season-pass database, checking for refunded, expired or upgraded passes
Trace a sample of December and January pass sales to recognition start dates in the ledger
Compare pass usage data to the straight-line recognition assumption to assess whether the obligation is delivered evenly
Observe turnstile footfall counts on a sample of days and compare to ticketing system entries
procedures.trap_explanation: Footfall observation addresses completeness of gate revenue for daily admissions; the flagged risks concern the deferred income balance — existence of remaining obligations and allocation of promotional pricing — which turnstile counts do not address.

scenarios.client_context: A government innovation agency funds a drug-discovery programme with milestone payments as candidate selection criteria are met. The company recognized the full awarded amount at year-end, claiming the milestones were 'virtually certain'. One milestone — candidate selection — is still pending, and the lead scientist on the milestone committee is the same person who reports grant progress to the agency.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Recognizing grant income before the milestone conditions were met books income for an event that has not yet occurred.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The amount recognized at a point versus matched to qualifying expenditure over time may be mismeasured.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Conditions and unmet milestones attached to grant funding require clear disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Read the grant agreement and confirm the status of candidate selection milestone evidence at year-end
Recalculate grant income recognition against qualifying expenditure incurred in the year and the milestone schedule
Corroborate milestone status with lab records and independent stage-gate reports rather than the scientist's own progress report
Inspect the grant income and conditions disclosures for completeness
Perform analytical review of total R&D expense against prior year
procedures.trap_explanation: Analysing R&D expense speaks to the cost side and completeness of expenditure; the flagged risks are premature recognition and measurement of grant income, which expense analysis does not address.

scenarios.client_context: The annual bonus pool accrual is computed by HR from a scorecard model; the group CEO approves his own scorecard weighting. This year the accrual fell 20% despite record profits, and the CEO's disclosed single-figure remuneration is close to the contractual maximum that triggers shareholder re-approval above it. Deferred bonuses were reclassified from liabilities to equity instruments.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Self-approved scorecard weightings with a profit trend contradicting the accrual suggest estimation bias in the pool.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Deferred bonus reclassification between liabilities and equity affects both the accrual and equity balances.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Remuneration disclosure caps and deferral policy must align with the statutory remuneration report.

procedures.procedure: Recompute the bonus pool from the scorecard formula using independently evidenced performance measures
Compare the accrual trend to profit and headcount trends and challenge management on the divergence
Review the terms of the deferral plan and evaluate whether reclassification to equity is supported by the instrument's substance
Agree the disclosed single figure and bonus split to the approved remuneration policy limits
Confirm bonus accrual balances with the pension trustee
procedures.trap_explanation: The trustee has no role in the bonus pool accrual; the risk is estimation bias and instrument classification, not third-party custody of the liability.

scenarios.client_context: The provision for platform decommissioning was set up when the field started producing 20 years ago and rolls forward annually using an inflation index and a fixed discount rate. New legislation on seabed restoration came into force last year, and a rival operator's recent decommissioning in the same basin cost 40% more per tonne of structure than the company's estimate.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Rolling forward an old estimate with a fixed discount rate ignores changed discount rates and recent cost benchmarks, so the provision is likely misstated.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: New seabed restoration obligations may not be captured in the obligation's scope.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the provision measurement model — cost estimates, inflation, discount rate — against current market evidence including the rival operator's outturn costs
Assess whether the new seabed restoration legislation creates additional components of the obligation and test inclusion in the provision
Obtain an engineering specialist's review of the decommissioning cost estimate and methodology
Recompute the unwinding of the discount for the year and its classification as a finance cost
Confirm the provision balance with the regulator's decommissioning cost estimate letter
procedures.trap_explanation: A regulator letter may indicate security amounts, but the obligation is the company's own estimate under accounting standards; treating the regulator's figure as confirmation of the carrying amount substitutes a third-party number for evidence about the company's estimation process.

scenarios.client_context: The agency pays 4,000 staff on a shared-service payroll run from a neighbouring municipality. Employer social security contributions are calculated by an interface between two systems; the interface mapping table was updated mid-year when contribution rates changed. Internal audit found three months where the interface rejected unmatched records and they were parked in a suspense file.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Rejected interface records parked in a suspense file mean some employees' contributions may never have reached the payable ledger.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The mid-year rate change through a manual mapping-table update risks wrong contribution rates on many records.

procedures.procedure: Reconcile the suspense file contents to the payable ledger and confirm disposition of every rejected record
Recompute employer contributions for samples of employees before and after the rate change using the statutory rates
Reconcile amounts remitted to the social security institution to the payable ledger movements
Obtain an IT report of all interface mapping-table changes, who made them and their approval
Confirm payable balances with the social security institution directly
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirmation of recorded balances tests existence, but the flagged risks are records lost in a suspense file (completeness) and wrong rates (accuracy); the institution can only confirm what was reported to it, not what the agency failed to report.

scenarios.client_context: The company revalued its flagship office tower for the first time, creating a EUR 30m surplus transferred to a revaluation reserve. The tax manager computed deferred tax on the surplus at the company's historical tax rate of 30%, but the enacted rate for the following years is 25%. Separately, the group revalued only this one property while carrying others at cost.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Using the superseded 30% rate for deferred tax on the revaluation surplus overstates the deferred tax liability.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Revaluing a single property within a class while others remain at cost may breach the requirement for consistent treatment within a class and requires clear measurement-basis disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate deferred tax on the revaluation surplus using enacted rates for the expected recovery periods
Review the accounting policy for property classes and evaluate whether revaluing one property in a cost class is appropriate
Inspect the valuer's report and assess whether the fair value evidence supports the surplus and the expected disposal manner
Check that the revaluation surplus and related deferred tax are presented within equity, not through profit or loss
Vouch the property's insurance cover note to verify the reinstatement value used in tax computations
procedures.trap_explanation: Insurance reinstatement value is a different measurement basis from fair value or tax base; it cannot support deferred tax measurement, which depends on accounting carrying value versus tax base at enacted rates.

scenarios.client_context: The company raised EUR 120m in a rights issue in March, incurring underwriting, legal and listing fees of EUR 7m. The ledger initially charged all fees to profit or loss; the group then reversed EUR 5m to equity in October without documentation of the fee-by-fee analysis. The share premium account also absorbed a non-underwriting marketing campaign.

assertions_high_risk.classification: Costs that are directly attributable to the equity issue must be deducted from equity, while unrelated marketing spend belongs in profit or loss; the undocumented reversal and campaign absorption blur this boundary.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The EUR 5m October reversal without supporting analysis risks an arbitrary split between equity and expense.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Campaign costs routed through share premium may include costs not connected to the issue at all.

procedures.procedure: Obtain the fee-by-fee analysis of the EUR 7m costs and evaluate the equity-versus-expense split against the nature of each cost
Inspect the marketing campaign invoices and contracts to determine whether they are directly attributable to the share issue
Agree the rights issue proceeds to the share register, prospectus and bank receipts
Trace the October journal to its preparer and approver and assess whether the reversal was a year-end cosmetic adjustment
Confirm the share capital movement with the registrar and CSD records
procedures.trap_explanation: Registrar confirmation of share counts addresses the completeness of issued capital; the flagged risks are the cost classification split and undocumented reversal — measurement and classification issues the registrar cannot speak to.

scenarios.client_context: The operator pays hoteliers in USD and collects from customers in EUR. Forward contracts hedge about half the exposure, but the hedge relationship was never documented. The local currency of key supplier countries depreciated 18% in the second half. FX gains and losses are booked to a 'hedging reserve' regardless of whether the item is hedged.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Closing rates on unhedged USD payables after an 18% swing will drive material revaluation differences; spreadsheet rate tables may be stale.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Routing all FX differences to a hedging reserve misclassifies what should hit profit or loss, since no hedge relationship is documented.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Undocumented hedges do not qualify for hedge accounting, so presenting them as hedged is misleading.

procedures.procedure: Re-translate USD monetary balances at verified closing rates and agree differences to the ledger
Review the FX gain/loss posting logic and confirm only qualifying hedge effects are in equity, with the rest in profit or loss
Inspect whether hedge documentation designating the forward contracts exists and assess hedge-accounting eligibility
Confirm year-end forward contract values with the bank and agree to the derivative valuation
Vouch a sample of hotel payments to remittance advices
procedures.trap_explanation: Payment vouching addresses whether payments occurred, but the flagged risks are translation at correct closing rates and misrouting of FX differences; the payment trail says nothing about period-end measurement.

scenarios.client_context: Clients withhold 5% retention from each milestone certificate on stadium works, releasable on practical completion plus a defects period. The receivable ledger is maintained per project in a spreadsheet. Two projects delayed completion into next year, and one client has entered administration since year-end.

assertions_high_risk.existence: Retention releasable only on completion may not qualify for immediate payment; recording it gross as an ordinary receivable may overstate the asset.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The client administration is a post-year-end event pointing to impairment of retention due from that client, and the deficiencies-period condition affects expected recoverability.

procedures.procedure: Agree the retention ledger per project to client-signed milestone certificates and contract terms
procedures.trap_explanation: Accuracy is not flagged as a high-risk assertion here and the certificate check primarily evidences existence of retention rights; including a misdirected assertion pairing weakens the procedure mapping.

procedures.procedure: Assess the effect of the client's administration on the retention due and test impairment against expected recovery scenarios
For delayed projects, confirm the completion and defects-period conditions and evaluate whether the retention presentation matches its contractual timing
Review post-year-end cash receipts on retention releases and compare to expectations
Inspect the ageing of retention balances by client and concentration of credit risk

scenarios.client_context: The group holds film-rights vehicles in which outside investors hold most of the capital but the group controls distribution decisions. Consolidation scope is decided by the group FD; three vehicles holding EUR 60m of film rights were excluded this year on the grounds that ownership is below 50%. A new vehicle formed in December holds advances from the group routed through an intercompany account.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Control-based consolidation, not ownership percentage, determines scope; excluding control vehicles with outside capital may omit assets, liabilities and NCI from the statements.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Unconsolidated structured entities require disclosure of interests and risks, which the ownership-percentage rationale suggests is missing.

procedures.procedure: Analyse the governance terms of the three excluded vehicles — decision rights, veto rights, exposure to variability — against control criteria
Trace the December vehicle's formation documents and intercompany advances to confirm its treatment in consolidation scope
Evaluate disclosures of interests in unconsolidated structured entities for nature and risks
Recalculate the effect on group assets, liabilities and equity if controlled vehicles were consolidated, to quantify the misstatement direction
Confirm bank balances of the excluded vehicles directly with their banks
procedures.trap_explanation: Bank confirmation on excluded vehicles tests their own balances, but the flagged risk is whether those vehicles belong in the consolidated group at all; confirming balances presumes the consolidation answer rather than testing it.

scenarios.client_context: The group reports two segments — 'Products' and 'Services' — but internal monthly management reports used by the executive committee show five operating units. Two loss-making units in the Products segment were aggregated this year after the segment measure was changed to exclude 'non-core' central costs. The new measure is not reconciled in the segment note.

assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The reported segmentation diverges from the internal management structure, and the unreconciled measure change undermines comparability and required reconciliation.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Aggregating loss-making units may hide material segment information required to be separately reported.

procedures.procedure: Compare the internal management reporting package to the segment note and evaluate whether reported segments reflect how the CODM reviews the business
Assess the rationale and documentation for aggregating the two loss-making units against aggregation criteria
Verify that the segment measure is measured consistently with group policy and reconciled to consolidated totals line by line
Enquire of the CODM about the information actually used, corroborated with meeting packs and dashboards
Vouch a sample of segment revenue to customer invoices
procedures.trap_explanation: Underlying revenue vouching is a SoPL assertion test; the flagged risk concerns how revenue is presented and reconciled in the segment note, not whether recorded invoices exist.

scenarios.client_context: Donors restrict 55% of income to specific country programmes. Fund allocations between restricted and unrestricted reserves are performed in a spreadsheet maintained by the head of programmes, whose country budgets depend on allocations. A major donor's grant terms were renegotiated mid-year to broaden permitted use, but the funds accounting was not updated.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Allocations driven by someone whose budgets depend on the outcome create bias risk in fund splits.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The mid-year grant renegotiation changes fund restrictions, so the disclosed purposes of restricted funds may be outdated.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Grant terms across dozens of donors make omission of a restriction condition a realistic risk.

procedures.procedure: Trace fund allocations for a sample of donations to grant letters and donor conditions at year-end, including the renegotiated grant
Review the spreadsheet's allocation logic, change history and whether anyone independent of programmes signs off splits
Reconcile movements in each restricted fund to project expenditure reports certified for the donor
Inspect the reserves and funds note for purposes, restrictions and any unspent balances per project
Observe a stock count of relief supplies at a country warehouse
procedures.trap_explanation: Physical stock observation tests existence of inventories; the flagged risks are allocation of funds between reserves and outdated restriction disclosures, which a warehouse count does not address.

scenarios.line_item: Income tax expense and effective rate reconciliation
scenarios.client_context: The group operates in 12 countries through a combination of branches and subsidiaries. The tax provision is computed centrally by a group tax team whose leader is bonused on cash tax savings. This year a new 'royalty' charged by an IP subsidiary cut the effective rate from 24% to 17%, and the tax note's reconciliation was re-presented with combined 'other' items of EUR 9m.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: An intra-group royalty that conveniently cuts the effective rate, designed by a bonused tax leader, may not reflect real transfers of function or IP.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Centralized computations across 12 jurisdictions create arithmetic and rate errors, and the 'other' bucket may conceal misstatements.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: A re-presented reconciliation obscuring EUR 9m of items undermines the required clarity of the rate reconciliation.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the IP subsidiary's functions, staff and contracts to corroborate that the royalty reflects substance before using it in the provision
Recalculate the current and deferred tax charge per jurisdiction using enacted rates and statutory adjustments
Break down the EUR 9m 'other' reconciling items and substantiate each component
Review transfer-pricing documentation and correspondence with tax authorities for the royalty arrangements
Confirm tax balances with the tax authorities in the two largest jurisdictions
procedures.trap_explanation: Authority confirmations address recorded liabilities' existence; the flagged risks are an unsubstantiated royalty affecting the charge and an obscured reconciliation — measurement and disclosure issues that balances confirmation cannot detect.

scenarios.client_context: A leveraged facility contains a net-leverage covenant tested semi-annually. After a fuel-cost spike, September's test passed with 3% headroom. In November management reclassified EUR 20m of operating leases as short-term, lowering the covenant measure. The covenant definition in the facility agreement references the audited accounts, and the year-end retest is due six weeks after the audit report date.

assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: If covenants are or may be breached, disclosure of the breach, waivers and lender negotiations is required; the retest timing pushes this against the audit deadline.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Reclassifying leases to flatter the covenant measure may be a misclassification made for covenant rather than substance reasons.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Borrowings classified as long-term may need re-presentation as current if the covenant breach is probable.

procedures.procedure: Read the facility agreement's covenant definitions and test the November lease reclassification against them and lease accounting criteria
Recompute the covenant measure at year-end on audited figures and assess breach probability and required re-presentation of borrowings
Obtain management's post-year-end covenant retest when available and evaluate disclosure of breach or waiver status
Review correspondence with lenders about the fuel-cost impact and any amendments or waivers
Vouch November interest payments to bank statements
procedures.trap_explanation: Payment vouching tests that payments occurred, but the flagged risks are covenant-driven reclassification and breach disclosure; the cash trail does not test either the lease reclassification or lender-negotiation status.

scenarios.client_context: The company introduced an AI tool that classifies usage into subscription tiers and drafts upgrade invoices. There is no human review of the tool's output for upgrades above EUR 10k; the tool was trained on historical data from before a pricing-model change, and the sales VP who owns the tool's business rules also owns the upsell revenue target.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: AI-drafted upgrade invoices reviewed by no one, under a target-owning executive, may include charges customers never agreed to.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The tool was trained on pre-pricing-change data, so tier classification and amounts may be systematically wrong.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Tier misclassification between subscription types distorts both revenue lines and deferred income.

procedures.procedure: Vouch a sample of AI-drafted upgrade invoices above EUR 10k to customer acceptance evidence — orders, accepted change orders or written confirmation
Test the AI tool's tier-classification logic against the current pricing model using a test set of usage records with known correct tiers
Compare upgrade invoice volumes and values before and after the tool's go-live and investigate anomalies by customer segment
Review refund and dispute logs for AI-invoiced upgrades and trace resolutions
Send confirmation requests to a sample of customers confirming their subscription tier
procedures.trap_explanation: Customer confirmation of tier status is weak evidence for the flagged risks — wrong-tier pricing and unagreed upgrades — because customers confirm what they believe they are in, which is exactly what the mispriced invoice also claims; testing the tool's logic and acceptance evidence is the direct route.

scenarios.client_context: The company guaranteed a EUR 150m facility of a 50:50 joint venture that is building a battery park. The JV failed a milestone test in December; under the JV agreement, that failure converts part of the partner's equity into a loan. The guarantee liability was measured at EUR 0 at inception on the grounds that default was 'unlikely'. The group accounts for the JV using the equity method, and the partner asked the group to waive the milestone breach.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A financial guarantee must be measured at the higher of the expected-loss amount and the initial recognition amount; an 'unlikely default' rationale of EUR 0 is not a valid measurement basis, and the milestone breach changes the expected-loss assessment.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Whether a present obligation exists at year-end depends on the JV's compliance status and the waiver decision, which was still pending.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Contingent and recognized portions of the guarantee, plus the control relationship with the JV, require disclosure; the waiver request suggests management may prefer contingent-liability presentation.

procedures.procedure: Read the guarantee instrument and JV agreement to establish the trigger events, subrogation rights and effect of the milestone failure
Recalculate the guarantee liability at the higher of expected-loss measurement and the initial amount, using the JV's updated financial condition
Review the cash covenant and facility headroom of the JV to corroborate default likelihood
Assess the disclosure of the recognized guarantee, contingent portions, and the equity-method JV's standing including the pending waiver
Confirm the JV's facility balance directly with the lender bank
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirming the JV's loan balance evidences the underlying facility but not the group's guarantee liability; the group-side assertion is about the obligation it issued and its measurement, which the lender's records of the JV debt do not establish.

scenarios.client_context: Falling crude prices forced a year-end impairment test of a producing field. Management's test used a year-end oil price of USD 85 per barrel for ten years, contrary to the group's price-deck policy of reverting to long-term prices of USD 65 after year two. The test passed with 4% headroom. A decommissioning cost estimate revision announced after year-end raised the cash outflow profile.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A year-end price of USD 85 contradicting the group's own USD 65 price deck creates management-bias risk in the headroom, which is only 4%.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Impairment testing assumptions and sensitivity disclosure must reflect the estimation uncertainty, and the post-year-end decommissioning revision may be an adjusting event.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate recoverable amount using the group's approved price-deck policy and quantify the headroom effect
Evaluate the technical basis of the production profile and cost assumptions against the reservoir engineer's report
Assess whether the post-year-end decommissioning cost revision is an adjusting event affecting the year-end recoverable amount
Review the sensitivity and estimation-uncertainty disclosures for the field's carrying value
Vouch the field's cumulative production statistics to the regulator's production database
procedures.trap_explanation: Production data verification supports the existence of the asset's output history, but the flagged risk is the measurement of recoverable amount under biased price assumptions; historical production is an input the model already agrees on.

scenarios.client_context: The insurer adopted the new insurance contracts standard this year. The CSM and loss-component balances now drive temporary differences, and the deferred tax computation maps them using a spreadsheet built by the tax department with input from a consultant who also implements the group's IFRS 17 system. Two subsidiaries in the group use the modified retrospective approach while one uses the fair-value approach, and the tax effects of the transition adjustments were pushed through opening equity with minimal review.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Spreadsheet mapping of new balance-sheet components to tax bases, prepared by the same consultant who built the system, creates bias and error risk in the deferred tax amounts.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Different transition approaches across subsidiaries raise the risk that some temporary differences — for example loss components — were never mapped to the computation.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Deferred tax on items recognized outside profit or loss must be traced to the same equity component; transition adjustments in opening equity need clear disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate deferred tax on the CSM and loss component per subsidiary, tracing tax bases from transition workings
Obtain a completeness mapping from every new IFRS 17 balance to the deferred tax model and challenge unmapped lines
Check that deferred tax on transition adjustments is booked against the same opening equity components rather than profit or loss
Inspect the deferred tax and IFRS 17 transition disclosures, including tax effects of components recognized outside profit or loss
Confirm tax losses carried forward with the local tax authority for the three subsidiaries
procedures.trap_explanation: Authority confirmation of tax losses addresses whether losses exist, but the flagged risks are the mapping of new IFRS 17 temporary differences and the equity classification of the tax effects; confirming losses does not test the transition computation.

scenarios.client_context: The trustee moved to a new actuarial firm this year.
