The new actuary lowered the discount rate by 30 basis points while the company's own investment committee was simultaneously negotiating a buy-in for part of the scheme. The previous firm had flagged longevity improvements among production staff that the new report does not mention. The CFO approved the actuarial report in one day.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A change of actuary coinciding with a buy-in negotiation creates incentive for assumptions that move the reported obligation toward a negotiating position; the unaddressed longevity signal supports that concern.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Scheme assets, surplus or deficit components, and the effect of the buy-in on asset classification may be omitted or mis-scoped in the report.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Assumption changes, sensitivities and the multi-employer scheme's characteristics require full disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Obtain the actuarial report and evaluate the discount rate against year-end high-quality corporate bond yields and the prior actuary's basis
Recalculate the obligation's sensitivity to the omitted longevity improvement and assess whether it is material to the deficit
Evaluate the buy-in's accounting effect — asset classification, income recognition and disclosure of the transaction
Trace the key population data — active members, pensioners, salaries — to the scheme administrator's records
Confirm the scheme's asset holdings with the custodian bank
procedures.trap_explanation: Custodian confirmation verifies the scheme's assets exist, but the flagged risks are the actuarial assumptions driving the obligation and disclosure of assumption changes; confirming holdings does not test the liability's measurement.

scenarios.client_context: The flagship fund holds stakes of 25-40% in eight underlying hedge funds. The manager concluded none are consolidated or equity-accounted because the fund is 'passive'. For two underlying funds, the manager also serves as director and receives performance fees. The fund's NAV feeds the fee calculation of the management company, and valuations of illiquid underlying positions are provided by the manager's own valuation team.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Self-produced valuations of illiquid underlying positions, feeding the fee calculation, create direct bias risk in the NAV.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Whether the stakes exist at year-end, in the size recorded, needs verification against the registers of illiquid, thinly-administered vehicles.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Significant influence through directorships may require equity-method presentation, and valuation methodology and fee-conflict disclosures must be complete.

procedures.procedure: Re-perform valuations of the illiquid underlying positions using observable market evidence and independent pricing sources
Confirm holdings with the underlying funds' administrators and registers of unitholders
Evaluate the directorship positions for evidence of significant influence and the resulting presentation conclusion
Review the valuation policy disclosures and fee-conflict disclosures against the reality of the manager's valuation role
Confirm the management company's fee calculation with the fund board
procedures.trap_explanation: Fee calculation confirmation tests the arithmetic of the manager's fee, but the flagged risks are the NAV inputs (biased level-3 valuations) and consolidation conclusion; the fee board cannot validate the valuations feeding the NAV.

scenarios.client_context: In October the board approved a plan to sell a loss-making copper mine and announced it to the market. A buyer is yet to be found, and brokers value the mine below carrying value. The company reclassified the mine to held-for-sale, kept measuring the asset pool at carrying value, and continues to recognize depletion and site overheads in the asset pool. An auction process is being run by the CFO's brother-in-law's boutique advisory firm.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A sale-likely-below-carrying-value situation requires measurement at the lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell; continuing depletion in the pool suggests measurement errors.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Held-for-sale classification requires the asset to be available for immediate sale and sale highly probable; without a buyer after months, the classification may be premature.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Disposal group details, impairment, and related-party involvement of the adviser require disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the held-for-sale criteria — board approval, active marketing, buyer interest, expected completion — at year-end given no buyer after months
Recalculate measurement of the disposal group at the lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell, using broker and market evidence
Review the treatment of depletion and site overheads charged after the reclassification date and correct the pool's carrying computation
Inspect the advisory engagement and assess disclosure of the related-party relationship and fee arrangement
Physically inspect the mine site and observe its operational status
procedures.trap_explanation: Site observation evidences the mine exists and its state of activity, but the flagged risks are measurement of the disposal group and validity of the held-for-sale classification — presentation and measurement questions a site visit cannot address.

scenarios.line_item: Covenant breach after the reporting period
scenarios.client_context: The developer's leverage covenant was tested after year-end and breached due to apartment presales falling through. Management argues the breach is a non-adjusting event because the sales collapse happened in February. However, one major buyer's insolvency proceedings began in December, and the presale contracts' deposit-forfeiture conditions were known to be triggered before year-end. Negotiation with the bank is ongoing, and the draft accounts show the loan within non-current liabilities.

assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The breach and its circumstances require disclosure, and whether it existed at year-end determines its classification in the accounts.
assertions_high_risk.classification: If the breach arose from conditions present at year-end — the December insolvency — the borrowings should be presented as current, not non-current.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Expected renegotiation fees, penalty interest and onerous-condition effects need to be reflected in the measurement of the liability.

procedures.procedure: Inspect presale contracts, the buyer's insolvency filings, and deposit-forfeiture triggers to establish which conditions existed at year-end
Evaluate the classification of the loan as current or non-current based on the breach's origin and any waiver obtained before authorisation
Review bank correspondence for penalty terms, waiver conditions and fees and test their measurement
Assess the disclosure of the breach nature, financial effect and negotiation status
Confirm the loan balance and security with the lender
procedures.trap_explanation: Lender confirmation evidences the loan's existence and terms, but the flagged risks are period classification of the borrowings and disclosure of a breach rooted in pre-year-end conditions; confirmation does not decide those.

scenarios.client_context: The company has one advanced exploration project, eighteen months of cash left, and its funding plan relies on a strategic investor whose term sheet expired unsigned in November. The directors state the going concern basis is appropriate because the investor 'remains interested'. Management's cash-flow model assumes project construction spending continues despite the funding gap, and the model's downside scenario shows cash exhaustion in eight months. No alternative financing has been sought.

assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: A material uncertainty that is not properly disclosed — supported only by an expired term sheet — would make the accounts misleading.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: If the going concern basis is inappropriate, assets measured on a going concern basis, including capitalizable exploration costs, may be overstated.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Uncertainty about funding the next twelve months affects the current versus non-current classification of all balance sheet items.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the cash-flow forecast's assumptions — funding sources, construction spending, and timeline — against corroborated evidence including the expired term sheet
Corroborate the strategic investor's continued interest with direct correspondence or their representatives, not only management's assertion
Assess the disclosure of the material uncertainty, including the conditions and management's plans
Review the treatment of capitalized exploration costs if the going concern basis fails and whether write-downs would be required
Confirm the cash balance with the bank at year-end
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirming the cash balance verifies today's cash, but the going concern question is about cash at future dates and the credibility of the funding plan; the balance confirmation is an input the model already takes as given.

scenarios.client_context: The company publishes transition-plan disclosures claiming one plant will be converted to biomass by a stated date, while its capex approvals contain no budget for the conversion. A new carbon-pricing law was enacted just before year-end, effective from next year. The impairment test of the plant excludes any carbon price effect because management says the law's rates are 'not yet certain', and the sustainability report's emissions figures are prepared by the communications team from unaudited data feeds.

assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Transition-plan claims contradicted by capex budgets create misleading disclosure; carbon-law effects must be reflected or their absence explained.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Ignoring enacted carbon pricing in the plant's impairment model biases the recoverable amount upward.

procedures.procedure: Compare the disclosed conversion plan to board-approved capex budgets and challenge inconsistencies
Evaluate whether the enacted carbon-pricing law's rates are sufficiently certain to be incorporated in the impairment test and recompute the effect
Trace the emissions figures in the sustainability report to source data and assess consistency with financial statement disclosures
Review the disclosures of climate-related risks against the entity's actual regulatory position and plant economics
Confirm carbon allowance holdings with the national registry
procedures.trap_explanation: Registry confirmation verifies allowances exist, but the flagged risks are biased impairment assumptions and misleading transition disclosures; confirming holdings does not test the model inputs or the disclosure accuracy.

scenarios.client_context: The group's founder lent EUR 40m interest-free to a subsidiary 60%- owned by the group, with repayment subordinated to a bank facility. No interest has ever been imputed, and the loan is carried at face value. The founder also personally guaranteed the subsidiary's rent obligations. The subsidiary is loss-making, and a market-rate loan would carry roughly 9% interest.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: An interest-free, subordinated loan to a loss-making subsidiary carried at face value is likely overstated; expected credit loss and imputed-interest effects must be considered.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Related-party loan terms, the subordination and the founder's guarantee require full disclosure.
assertions_high_risk.classification: The loan's subordination to bank debt may make it quasi-equity in substance, affecting where it appears and how losses are allocated between holders.

procedures.procedure: Reassess the loan's recoverable amount given the subsidiary's losses and the subordination ranking, testing any expected credit loss model used
Evaluate the loan's substance — subordination, expected conversion or forgiveness — and whether quasi-equity presentation is more appropriate
Inspect the loan agreement, subordination deed and any side letters with the founder
Review the related-party note for terms of the loan and the founder's guarantee
Confirm the loan balance directly with the founder
procedures.trap_explanation: The founder is the counterparty who benefits from face-value presentation; confirmation from a related party is low-quality evidence, and the flagged risks are measurement and classification of the loan, which the founder's agreement cannot resolve.

scenarios.client_context: Two hotels were impaired during the pandemic; the write-downs were recognized as losses in those years. This year, post-pandemic occupancy has recovered, and management has reversed the impairments through profit or loss, restoring carrying values to pre-pandemic levels. However, the recoverable amounts supporting the reversal use stabilized year-round occupancy, while the recovery is driven by summer weekends booked through one aggregator platform, and the pandemic-era write-downs were based on a different cash-generating unit configuration.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A reversal may only restore the carrying amount to what it would have been absent the impairment, using amortized-cost logic, and the assumption of stabilized year-round occupancy may overstate recoverable amount.
assertions_high_risk.classification: If part of the rise in value reflects revaluation-type increases rather than reversal of previously recognized impairment, routing the whole amount through profit or loss misclassifies it.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The reversal's basis, the CGU configuration change and the assumption change need disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Recompute the maximum reversible carrying amount from the historical impairment workings and compare to the reversal booked
Challenge the stabilized occupancy assumption against month-by-month actuals and channel-mix data including aggregator dependence
Evaluate whether the CGU reconfiguration between the impairment and the reversal is legitimate or conveniently aggregates stronger assets with weaker ones
Assess whether any portion of the value increase should be presented as a revaluation or in equity rather than reversal through profit or loss
Obtain room-rate cards from the hotels' booking systems and agree to revenue records
procedures.trap_explanation: Agreeing rate cards to revenue records tests revenue occurrence, but the flagged risks are the measurement ceiling on the reversal and its classification; room-rate vouching is on a different line item and assertion.

scenarios.client_context: A public-sector client represents 62% of revenue; its contract was retendered with results due three months after year-end. The company also has a large receivable from this client, which disputes invoiced overtime billed under a legacy rate card. Management's forecast assumes contract renewal at current volumes. The receivable was reclassified mid-year from contract assets based on a legal opinion that the amounts qualify as unconditional.

assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The concentration and retender create a disclosure imperative covering dependence and risk; assuming renewal without disclosure would mislead.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The disputed overtime receivable may be overstated; recovery depends on the retender outcome and the rate-card dispute.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Overtime billed under a legacy rate card may include amounts the client never agreed to pay.

procedures.procedure: Assess disclosure of customer concentration, the retender status and management's renewal assumption against disclosure requirements
Inspect the retender correspondence and, after year-end, the outcome for evidence on renewal probability
Vouch disputed overtime billings to signed deployment records and the client's contractual rate basis
Review the legal opinion behind the contract-asset to receivable reclassification and test whether the unconditional-right criterion is met
Confirm the receivable balance directly with the public-sector client
procedures.trap_explanation: The client has already disputed the overtime billing, so its confirmation will simply restate the dispute; the flagged risks are recoverability and the concentration disclosure, which a balance confirmation cannot resolve.

scenarios.client_context: The company hedges cocoa purchases with futures. A sharp price drop made the hedge deeply in-the-money relative to physical purchase commitments, and management re-balanced the hedge ratio in October, doubling the volume of futures designated. Hedge documentation was updated retrospectively to describe the doubled ratio as the 'intended' ratio from inception. The treasury manager earns a bonus on hedging gains, and effectiveness testing is performed manually in a spreadsheet with a lookup-table error identified by internal audit in one column.

assertions_high_risk.classification: Retrospective designation of the doubled ratio to keep hedge accounting after prices moved may disqualify the hedge relationship, moving derivatives to fair-value-through-profit-or-loss.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The spreadsheet lookup error and bonus incentives create measurement bias risk in derivative valuation and effectiveness results.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Hedge relationship descriptions and risk-management intent disclosures must match the documented reality at inception, not the October amendment.

procedures.procedure: Compare the inception hedge documentation to the October amendment and assess whether re-balancing qualifies for prospective treatment rather than retrospective rewriting
Re-perform effectiveness testing with the lookup-table error corrected and evaluate both pre- and post-October ratios
Revalue the futures portfolio independently against exchange settlement prices
Inspect the hedge disclosure note for consistency of documented relationships, amounts and risk-management objective
Confirm the futures positions with the broker
procedures.trap_explanation: Broker confirmation verifies positions exist, but the flagged risks are hedge-accounting qualification and bias in effectiveness measurement; existence of the derivatives was never the concern.

scenarios.client_context: A reverse-factoring programme was extended this year: the bank pays suppliers early and the retailer repays the bank on extended terms of 120 days. The programme grew to cover 40% of supplier invoices, but the payables ledger's ageing now looks improved because supplier due dates were extended by the programme rather than by trade terms. Disclosure describes the arrangements only as 'invoice discounting services' without amounts or the change in terms. Interest on the bank liability is embedded in the supplier prices.

assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Describing reverse factoring merely as invoice discounting, without amounts, terms changes or bank involvement, obscures liquidity and concentration risks that users need.
assertions_high_risk.classification: If the programme's substance replaces trade payables with bank financing, presentation as trade payables misclassifies the liability.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Embedded interest within supplier prices and extended terms affects expense measurement and any liability measurement.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the programme agreements with the bank and compare terms to trade payables terms to determine the liability's substance
Evaluate the disclosure of programme size, key terms, bank involvement and changes in supplier payment terms
Recalculate the embedded financing cost in supplier prices and assess whether finance cost recognition is appropriate
Confirm the bank liability balances under the programme and their terms directly with the bank
Vouch a sample of supplier invoices in the programme to goods-received notes
procedures.trap_explanation: Invoice vouching tests whether recorded purchases occurred, but the flagged risks are classification and disclosure of the financing structure; the physical goods flow was never in question — the financing arrangement is.

scenarios.client_context: An acquisition three years ago included an earn-out based on the acquired unit's cumulative sales over four years. With nine months to run, the unit's sales have been boosted by a launch in a new territory — a launch explicitly excluded from the earn-out definition in the purchase agreement, but included by management in the fair value estimate this year. The earn-out is a cash payment, and the counterparty is the unit's former owners, who remain as senior executives of the unit making the sales forecasts.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Including excluded-territory sales in the earn-out model overstates the liability, and the forecast is prepared by the payees themselves.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Sales recorded by the unit feed the earn-out, so the unit's leadership has a direct incentive to overstate sales in the earn-out period.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Earn-out measurement changes, sensitivity and the conflict between payees and preparers need disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Read the earn-out definition in the purchase agreement and reconcile the sales measure used in the model to it, territory by territory
Vouch sales feeding the earn-out to third-party distribution data and customer invoices, focusing on the new territory
Assess whether the forecast prepared by the payees is corroborated by independent evidence — market data, pipeline, prescriptions
Evaluate disclosure of the measurement basis, remeasurement amounts and key assumptions
Confirm the remaining earn-out obligation with the former owners
procedures.trap_explanation: The former owners are the counterparties who receive the payment; their confirmation of the balance is inherently unreliable and cannot resolve the contractual-definition dispute that drives the misstatement.

scenarios.client_context: Walk-in repairs are recorded on paper job cards; the mechanic ticks off completed jobs at day-end and the owner types totals into the ledger. Cash payments are common, and the workshop bin contains job cards from prior weeks never entered. A new apprentice has been handling the day-end totals since last month.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Paper job cards sitting unentered in the workshop and a new apprentice running day-end totals mean completed work may never reach the ledger.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Manual totalling of handwritten cards invites arithmetic and keying errors.

procedures.procedure: Physically collect and list all job cards in the workshop and reconcile each to the ledger, identifying unentered cards
Recalculate day-end totals from the job cards for a sample of weeks, including the apprentice's first month
Trace a sample of banked cash deposits to the daily repair takings recorded
Vouch a sample of recorded repair invoices to customer signatures on job cards
Confirm year-end bank balance directly with the bank
procedures.trap_explanation: Bank confirmation verifies the cash balance, not whether repair takings were recorded; the flagged risks are unentered job cards and totalling errors on revenue.

scenarios.client_context: Forty station kiosks each hold a morning float and remit takings weekly. The till system compares expected cash to counted cash; variances under EUR 5 are auto-written off by a rule the area manager added, and one kiosk shows daily negative variances of exactly EUR 4.90 for two months.

assertions_high_risk.existence: Recurring variances just under the write-off threshold pattern-match employee theft; the declared cash may not all be present.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Weekly remittances from 40 kiosks may not all reach the ledger, and the auto-write-off rule suppresses the evidence.

procedures.procedure: Attend surprise till counts at a risk-weighted sample of kiosks and reconcile to the till system's expected cash
Obtain the variance report before write-offs, analyse variances by kiosk and threshold, and investigate the EUR 4.90 pattern
Review who configured the auto-write-off rule and whether it was approved
Reconcile all weekly remittance advices for the year to bank deposits per kiosk
Recalculate float reimbursement entries for a sample of kiosks
procedures.trap_explanation: Float reimbursement arithmetic is not where the risk sits; the pattern of threshold-adjacent variances points to existence of cash and suppression of variance records, which top-up recalculation cannot address.

scenarios.client_context: Suppliers offer 2% discounts for payment within 10 days. The ledger records payables gross and books discounts taken as a reduction of purchase cost when the early payment is made. Payments are batch-run weekly by the treasury clerk, who also reconciles the bank, and 30% of discount-eligible invoices were paid too late to qualify last quarter.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Late payments that lose the discount are still being reduced by the 2%, understating cost of purchases.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The one-person payment-and-reconciliation role creates the risk of payments to wrong beneficiaries or amounts not followed up.

procedures.procedure: For a sample of invoices paid after the discount window, recalculate whether the discount was deducted and quantify the error
Compare payment dates per bank statement to invoice discount terms for a month of payments
Review segregation between payment preparation and bank reconciliation, and test supervisor approvals on the batch run
Perform cut-off testing on goods-received notes in the last two weeks against recorded payables
Confirm payable balances with the ten largest suppliers
procedures.trap_explanation: Supplier confirmations address existence of recorded balances; the flagged risks are discount arithmetic errors and missing payables, so the direction of testing needs to be recalculation and cut-off, not confirmation of what is already recorded.

scenarios.client_context: The group pays staff monthly in arrears on the 28th, so 3-4 days of December service is unpaid at year-end. The accrual is calculated in the payroll system as the prior month's total times 4/30. December is the resort's peak season with overtime and seasonal staff bonuses, while November was shoulder season.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: A 4/30 formula based on quiet-season November understates peak-December service with overtime and bonuses.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Seasonal casual staff engaged directly by hotel managers off-system may never enter the payroll accrual.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate the year-end accrual from December rosters and timesheets including overtime and seasonal bonuses
Compare headcount on the HR system to duty rosters signed by hotel managers and investigate off-roster workers
Agree the January payroll actually paid to the December accrual and investigate differences
Analyse monthly payroll expense by property and challenge the November-based accrual for peak sites
Confirm December payroll tax filings with the tax authority
procedures.trap_explanation: Authority filings only capture on-system staff; the flagged risk includes off-system casuals never registered, so confirming filings would miss exactly the population at risk.

scenarios.client_context: The company subcontracts cleaning to a network of small firms owned largely by employees' relatives. Invoices are submitted monthly with no service-level evidence, and one supplier doubled its invoice value this year while the building footprint was unchanged. The operations manager approves all subcontractor invoices without limit.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Related-party suppliers with no service evidence and an unlimited approver create a fictitious-services risk.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The doubling of one supplier's billings without a driver suggests overbilling.

procedures.procedure: Vouch a sample of the doubled supplier's invoices to work orders, site logs or client sign-off sheets
Perform analytical comparison of expense per square metre across buildings and suppliers
Map subcontractor ownership to employee records to identify undisclosed related parties
Review whether any portion of the maintenance spend relates to capital improvements requiring capitalization
Obtain a management representation that all cleaning services were performed
procedures.trap_explanation: A representation is management's own assertion, not evidence; where related-party overbilling is the flagged risk, corroborating third-party or operational records are required.

scenarios.client_context: The company moved into a new office in September. Fit-out costs of EUR 400k were capitalized, including design consultancy, a party to launch the space, and monthly plant rental. The founder authorized all spend; no fixed asset register existed until the auditors requested one, built retrospectively from bank statements.

assertions_high_risk.classification: A launch party and recurring plant rental are operating costs; capitalizing them misclassifies expense into the asset.
assertions_high_risk.existence: A register rebuilt from bank statements may include payments for items that are not assets at all.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Without a register, depreciation start dates and useful lives are guesses.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the fit-out contract and supplier invoices and classify each cost component between capital and operating spend
Physically inspect the office and agree observed fixtures and furniture to the new fixed asset register
Recalculate depreciation from the asset register, checking start dates against the occupation date
Trace the register's items to bank payments and confirm none relate to consumables or events
Perform cut-off testing of repair expenses before the move
procedures.trap_explanation: Cut-off on prior premises repairs targets a timing assertion that is not flagged here; the risks are misclassification of operating spend into the asset and existence of register items.

scenarios.client_context: The chain replaced annual stocktakes with cycle counts: each store counts a rotating subset weekly, and the system adjusts book stock to count. Store managers' bonuses depend on stock accuracy. One region shows a pattern of upward adjustments only in the final week of each quarter, and no adjustments are ever downward.

assertions_high_risk.existence: Bonused managers performing their own counts, with one-way upward adjustments, suggest counts may be manipulated or stock may not exist.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Counting subsets means some lines are never verified, and systematic upward bias hides losses.

procedures.procedure: Attend independent counts at a sample of stores, prioritizing the region with quarter-end adjustment patterns
Extract all count adjustments by store, week and direction and analyse the quarter-end clustering statistically
Test whether the cycle-count rotation covers every SKU at least annually by reviewing the count schedule
Recalculate the margin effect of upward adjustments and compare to the bonus threshold
Observe the store's goods-in process for a day and trace receipts to the system
procedures.trap_explanation: Goods-in observation tests that receipts are recorded, but the flagged risk is the credibility of counts themselves; verifying inbound flow does not test whether stock on the shelf matches the book.

scenarios.client_context: The chain prepaid 18 months of rent on its flagship café to secure a discount. In month 11, the landlord was put into administration and the lease contains a break clause allowing the landlord to terminate on 3 months' notice. The company keeps amortizing the prepayment evenly and has made no adjustment.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The landlord's administration plus a landlord break clause means future occupancy is uncertain; the unamortized prepayment may not be recoverable through future benefit.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Whether the prepayment remains an asset or should be re-presented depends on the lease accounting outcome, not just the payment schedule.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the lease's break clause terms and obtain correspondence on the landlord administration and any administrator decisions on the lease
Evaluate whether continued occupancy for the full prepayment period is probable and whether an impairment or accelerated write-off is required
Recalculate amortization to date and reconcile the carrying balance to the lease schedule
Assess whether the right-of-use asset and prepayment are presented consistently with the lease accounting policy
Confirm the prepayment with the administrator's agent acting for the landlord
procedures.trap_explanation: The administrator's agent can confirm receipt of the payment but cannot confirm the company's entitlement to future occupancy — the flagged valuation risk; confirmations address a fact that is not in dispute.

scenarios.client_context: Fees are billed from timesheets at blended hourly rates. Two senior architects left mid-year and their unbilled time was written back to revenue. A large fixed-fee project ran over budget; the partner in charge billed it as time-based using the highest rate card. Timesheets are submitted monthly with no project-stage linkage.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Reclassifying a fixed-fee overrun to time-based billing at the top rate card misapplies the contract terms.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Timesheets without project-stage linkage allow billing time for work that did not occur.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: December timesheets are submitted in January, concentrating boundary risk on which period the effort belongs to.

procedures.procedure: For the fixed-fee project, read the engagement letter and recompute the contractual billing against time billed
Vouch a sample of billed hours to client-approved stage outputs or site instructions
Trace December and early-January timesheets to the period in which the work was performed and the invoice raised
Analyse revenue per architect before and after the departures, investigating the write-back of unbilled time
Confirm billed balances with the largest three clients
procedures.trap_explanation: Client confirmations of balances do not test whether billing followed the contract terms or whether timesheet hours were real work — the flagged risks are accuracy and occurrence of the fee build-up, not the receivable's existence.

scenarios.client_context: The board declared a dividend in November, recorded as a liability and a movement in retained earnings, payable in February. One shareholder died in December, and under the shareholders' agreement his shares carry a redemption right exercisable by his estate at a formula price; the estate has signalled it will redeem rather than take the dividend.

assertions_high_risk.classification: The redemption obligation is a financial liability that may need separate presentation from the dividend payable; mixing them misclassifies the amounts due to different holders.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The redemption formula price may exceed the declared dividend, and the amounts due may be misallocated between the two mechanisms.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The redemption right and its terms are material post-balance-sheet information requiring disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Read the shareholders' agreement's redemption clause and compute the estate's entitlement under the formula, comparing to the declared dividend
Inspect the board minute declaring the dividend and the payment schedule, and agree the liability to it
Evaluate whether the estate's redemption right requires separate financial liability presentation from the dividend payable
Review disclosures of the redemption right, the estate's position and expected settlement
Cut-off test the dividend declaration date against the reporting period
procedures.trap_explanation: The declaration was clearly in-period in November, so period cut-off is not the flagged risk; the substance lies in classification between the dividend and the redemption obligation.

scenarios.client_context: The charity holds funds across four call accounts and a 12-month term deposit opened in June at a fixed rate. Interest on the term deposit is paid at maturity and accrued manually by the part-time finance officer. Rates rose twice in the second half of the year, and the call accounts' rates changed each time.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Manual accrual of the term deposit and mid-year rate changes on call accounts invite outdated-rate errors.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Interest credited in January for December may never be posted by the part-time officer.

procedures.procedure: Obtain bank statements and rate advices for all accounts and recalculate interest for the final quarter at current rates
Inspect January statements for December-accrued interest credited and trace to the ledger
Recalculate the term deposit accrual from June to year-end at the contracted fixed rate
Perform a reasonableness test of total interest against average balances and blended rates
Confirm deposit balances with all four banks
procedures.trap_explanation: Balance confirmations verify principal amounts, not whether interest income was recorded at the right rates and periods — the flagged risks are accuracy and completeness of the income accrual.

scenarios.client_context: The operator leases floors, subleases desks, and receives one monthly electricity invoice per building covering both its own office and the sublet areas. The split is made by a fixed 60/40 ratio set two years ago; since then the operator doubled its own staff in the building and took on a 24-hour tenant on one floor.

assertions_high_risk.classification: The recoverable portion belonging to the sublet tenants should be matched against their rental income or recovered, not expensed; the stale 60/40 split misclassifies both directions.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The ratio no longer reflects usage patterns, misstating both the expense and the recovery.

procedures.procedure: Obtain sub-meter readings or area-based recalculations for a sample of months and compare to the 60/40 split
Review tenant lease terms on utility recovery and test that recoveries are matched against the correct expense portion
Vouch the total electricity invoice to the meter account and building usage data
Recalculate the expense split including the new 24-hour tenant floor
Confirm the utility account balance with the provider
procedures.trap_explanation: Provider confirmation evidences the amount owed, but the flagged risks are the internal split and classification between operator expense and tenant recovery — facts the provider cannot speak to.

scenarios.client_context: The sales director can raise credit notes without approval up to EUR 2,500. In the last week of December, 130 credit notes were raised against November sales — three times the weekly average — and the customers were rebilled in mid-January. The sales director's team missed its Q4 volume target by a small margin.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Credit-then-rebill patterns around a missed target suggest notes may reverse sales that genuinely occurred, or support fictitious side agreements.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Crediting December-recognized November sales and rebilling in January shifts revenue between periods.

procedures.procedure: Vouch a sample of December credit notes to customer returns evidence, complaints or pricing agreements and trace rebills
Compare weekly credit note volumes before and after year-end and analyse clustering
Recalculate Q4 sales including and excluding the credit-note cycle and assess the target effect
Review the credit note approval matrix and test system enforcement of the EUR 2,500 limit
Send confirmations to the customers involved in the December credit notes
procedures.trap_explanation: Customer confirmations of balances will reflect the post-credit-note position and cannot reveal whether the underlying sales were genuine or shifted; the flagged risks are occurrence and cut-off of the credit-rebill cycle.

scenarios.client_context: VAT returns are prepared quarterly by the head chef's spouse from till Z-reports, and the tax authority's pre-filled data shows higher card sales than the returns for two quarters. Daily takings include a small cash-only lunch counter added last year that never entered the Z-report feed.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: A cash-only counter excluded from the Z-report feed means output VAT on those sales was never declared.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The discrepancy between card-processor data and filed returns suggests arithmetic or mapping errors in the return preparation.

procedures.procedure: Reconcile the card processor's settlement data to declared card sales for the mismatched quarters and quantify the gap
Observe the lunch counter's takings process for two days and trace cash sales to the till feed and VAT workings
Recalculate output VAT on the counter's estimated sales from purchase records of counter ingredients
Review the preparer's competence and independence given the related-party role
Confirm the VAT payable balance with the tax authority
procedures.trap_explanation: The authority's records reflect what was filed; confirming them cannot detect undeclared counter sales — precisely the completeness risk — and would wrongly corroborate the understated balance.

scenarios.client_context: The platform sells ad slots partly for cash and partly contra: advertisers provide services in exchange for ad space. Contra deals grew to 20% of bookings this year. Revenue is recorded gross at rate-card prices for both cash and contra deals, while some contra services received are separately recorded as income. The sales team is bonused on gross bookings.

assertions_high_risk.classification: Contra arrangements must be assessed for whether separate sale and purchase transactions exist or a single net arrangement applies; gross rate-card recognition may double-count or misclassify barter revenue.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Rate-card pricing for non-cash deals may not reflect the transaction price, overstating revenue.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Bookings bonused before delivery create an incentive to record ads never run.

procedures.procedure: Inspect a sample of contra contracts and evaluate whether separate purchases and sales exist, or net presentation applies
Compare recognized revenue on contra deals to the fair value of services received or the cash price of equivalent ad slots
Vouch a sample of booked ads to ad-server delivery logs evidencing the ads actually ran
Test that services received under contra deals are not simultaneously recognized again as income
Analyse gross bookings versus delivered revenue by salesperson against the bonus plan
Confirm outstanding balances with advertisers
procedures.trap_explanation: Balance confirmations with advertisers address receivables existence; the flagged risks are the classification and measurement of contra revenue and whether booked ads ran — none of which a balance confirmation resolves.

scenarios.client_context: Franchisees self-report monthly room revenue and pay a 5% royalty, with 1% marketing levy. Three franchisees opened near competing brands and their reported occupancy is 20 points below the market benchmark; one franchisee is owned by the franchisor's regional director's family. Under-reporting carries only a EUR 500 contractual penalty, and the franchisor stopped site audits two years ago.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Self-reported royalties with weak penalties and no site audits create an under-reporting incentive, especially where occupancy beats benchmarks of competitors would suggest higher revenue.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Royalty computation from self-reported figures may apply wrong rates or exclude the marketing levy.

procedures.procedure: Benchmark each franchisee's reported occupancy and average rate against market data and city tourism statistics, investigating outliers
Recalculate royalties and marketing levies for a sample of franchisees from their reported figures
For the related-party franchisee, obtain PMS data directly or visit the site and recompute room nights
Review the franchise agreements for audit rights and consider exercising them at the under-performing sites
Confirm royalty payable balances with all franchisees
procedures.trap_explanation: Franchisee confirmations of their own declared balances would corroborate the self-reported figures; the flagged risk is that those figures are incomplete, so confirmation is the wrong direction and the wrong source.

scenarios.client_context: The maintenance stores hold 40,000 part numbers, many dedicated to ageing aircraft types being retired by the customer base. The provisioning model buys to historical consumption, but the customer's retirement schedule (published last quarter) cuts demand for two engine families by 70%. Obsolescence reviews are run annually by the same planner who places the purchase orders.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Demand collapsing for two engine families means carrying amounts for dedicated parts are unlikely recoverable; the planner placing orders is conflicted when reviewing obsolescence.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Annual review of 40,000 SKUs by one conflicted person means write-downs may be incomplete.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate consumption for engine-family parts against the retirement schedule and identify stock exceeding forecast demand
Independently review the obsolescence methodology and re-perform the calculation for a risk-weighted sample of parts
Inspect physical condition and storage segregation of dedicated parts during count attendance
Review the disclosure of the inventory valuation judgement and sensitivity of write-downs
Trace a sample of parts to purchase orders to check the provisioning model reacted to the retirement announcement
procedures.trap_explanation: Purchase-order tracing tests whether buying followed the model, but the flagged risks are recoverability of stock already held and completeness of write-downs; purchasing behaviour does not measure the carrying amount.

scenarios.line_item: Construction work in progress (rail safety programme)
scenarios.client_context: A multi-year signalling renewal is capitalized monthly from contractor applications for payment. The contractor submitted a December application including January-planned works, and the programme office approved it to use up remaining budget before year-end. Commissioning tests for one section passed in October but the section is not yet handed to operations, so costs stay in CWIP and depreciation has not started.

assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Approving a December application covering January works pulls future costs into the year-end asset.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Depreciation should begin when the section is available for use, not at handover; holding costs in CWIP overstates the asset and understates expense.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Applications are capitalized without measurement certification of works completed.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the December application against the contractor's works schedule and surveyor valuations to identify January-scope costs
Test whether depreciation started when commissioning was achieved in October, recalculation from the available-for-use date
Agree capitalized amounts to independent quantity surveyor certificates for a sample of months
Review the programme office's approval controls and budget-driven approval patterns
Physically observe the commissioned section in operation
procedures.trap_explanation: Seeing the section running evidences it exists, but the flagged risks are capitalizing January costs and the depreciation start date; the asset's physical presence was never in doubt.

scenarios.client_context: A conglomerate acquired a cosmetics company and allocated EUR 70m of the price to the flagship brand using the relief-from-royalty method, with a royalty rate of 8% estimated by the CFO with no external support. Since acquisition, a viral safety complaint about the brand's flagship product went viral, and sales fell 30% in the final quarter. No impairment indicator was recorded in the impairment review, which the CFO also prepared.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: An internally estimated 8% royalty rate with no corroboration biases the brand's fair value at acquisition, and the post-acquisition sales collapse triggers a genuine impairment indicator the CFO's own review missed.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: The impairment review may have omitted the brand's own recent performance data as an indicator.

procedures.procedure: Benchmark the 8% royalty rate against published brand licensing transactions and independent valuation studies
Evaluate whether the fourth-quarter sales collapse is an impairment indicator and reperform the impairment test with updated cash flows
Assess the CFO's role in both the valuation and the impairment review and the adequacy of independent challenge
Review the intangibles and impairment disclosures including estimation uncertainty
Confirm the acquisition's legal completion date with the purchaser's lawyers
procedures.trap_explanation: Completion date confirms the transaction timing, but the flagged risks are the biased brand valuation and a missed impairment indicator — measurement issues for which a legal date is irrelevant.

scenarios.client_context: The group capitalizes internal development using a rule of thumb: engineers' logged time tagged 'dev' is capitalized, everything else expensed. The mobile app rebuild runs in agile sprints mixing research, design and coding; the head of engineering tags whole teams' time to 'dev' during high-pressure quarters, and amortization begins 'on product launch' — but the app launched incrementally to 5%, then 50% of users months apart.

assertions_high_risk.classification: Blanket 'dev' tagging capitalizes research and design time that should be expensed, and sprint mixing makes separation judgemental.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Amortization starting at 'launch' ignores the phased rollout; costs are available for use before full launch, so the amortization period is misallocated.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Capitalized time may include bench time or non-project activity given whole-team tagging.

procedures.procedure: Sample sprint records and re-perform the split between research, design and development phases against capitalization criteria
Vouch a sample of capitalized time to sprint boards, tickets and release records evidencing development activity
Recalculate amortization start dates from the incremental availability of the app's features to each user cohort
Review IT access to time-tagging and whether whole-team tagging overrides were approved
Inspect the disclosure of the capitalization policy, amounts and amortization approach
Confirm capitalized payroll cost to the HR system's payroll register
procedures.trap_explanation: Agreeing capitalized time to the payroll register verifies the rates paid, but the flagged risks are which activities qualify and when amortization starts; a payroll tie-out says nothing about the nature of the work performed.

scenarios.client_context: Anchor tenants pay base rent plus 12% of sales above a threshold; sales figures are self-reported through an online portal. Two tenants under-reported sales in prior years and settled when challenged. The lease liability for variable payments is estimated by the finance team using budgeted tenant sales, which were prepared before two new competing centres opened nearby.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Estimating variable lease income and related measurement using pre-competition budgets overstates the expected turnover component.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Self-reported sales with a history of under-reporting mean variable payments due may not be fully invoiced or estimated.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate variable lease amounts for a sample of tenants using independently obtained sales evidence, such as footfall and card data
Challenge the budgeted sales assumptions against post-opening actual sales trends in the centre
Review the portal's edit history for post-submission changes to reported sales and who can make them
For tenants with prior under-reporting, reperform the sales verification and settlement process on current-year figures
Confirm reported tenant sales with the tenants directly
procedures.trap_explanation: Tenant confirmation merely repeats their own portal submission; with under-reporting the flagged risk, the confirmation adds no independent evidence and can lend false comfort to the very figures in doubt.

scenarios.client_context: During lease renegotiations, two landlords granted a three-month rent holiday and reduced fixed rents by 10% for two years. The accountant treated the holiday as a variable payment exclusion and the rent reduction as a lease modification, remeasuring the liability with an unchanged discount rate. The original leases contain a discount-rate-on-remeasurement clause referencing the rate implicit at modification, currently higher than the original rate.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Using the original rather than revised discount rate on remeasurement misstates the liability, and the treatment of the holiday as an exclusion versus negative variable payment affects the measurement.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Whether the concession is a modification or a separate agreement changes both the accounting route and the liability's carrying amount.

procedures.procedure: Read the renegotiation agreements and determine whether the concessions are modifications, applying the revised discount rate where required, and recompute the liability
Compare the accountant's discount rate to the lease's own rate-reference clause and current borrowing evidence
Evaluate whether the rent holiday should reduce the liability and remeasurement gain or loss recognition
Inspect the lease liability note for the concession's treatment and modification effects
Confirm the revised rent schedule with each landlord
procedures.trap_explanation: Landlord confirmation of the agreed schedule evidences the deal exists, but the flagged risks are the remeasurement mechanics — discount rate and modification classification — which are accounting judgements the landlord cannot confirm.

scenarios.line_item: Borrowing costs on a tunnel project
scenarios.client_context: The company capitalized all borrowing costs of a EUR 300m facility to the tunnel project, including a period of six months when excavation was suspended after a geological dispute with the contractor, and including facility-arrangement fees paid two years before works started. The finance team's capitalization spreadsheet applies the rate to the full drawn balance each month.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Capitalizing during the six-month suspension and pre-commencement fees violates the activity periods, and the spreadsheet's full-balance approach may not adjust rates or drawdown timing.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Arrangement fees belong in the borrowing's effective-interest calculation, not directly in capitalized project cost at payment.

procedures.procedure: Reconstruct the project timeline and recalculate capitalizable borrowing costs, excluding the suspension period and pre-commencement fees
Test the spreadsheet's logic for rate application against facility drawdown schedules
Agree the suspension period to contractor correspondence and the dispute log
Recalculate the effective interest cost of arrangement fees and their capitalization route
Confirm facility terms and drawn balances with the lender
Observe tunnel construction progress on site
procedures.trap_explanation: Site observation confirms works are under way, but the flagged risks are the accounting periods and mechanics of capitalizing borrowing costs; whether the tunnel physically progresses does not test the spreadsheet's math or the suspension cut-off.

scenarios.client_context: The group issued a EUR 200m convertible bond with a conversion price 40% above the share price at issue. The accountant classified the entire instrument as debt because 'conversion is unlikely', using the coupon rate of 2% as the effective rate instead of the market rate for equivalent non-convertible debt of 7%. The conversion feature is also excluded from the diluted EPS calculation.

assertions_high_risk.classification: A convertible bond generally requires separating the liability and equity components; classifying it entirely as debt misclassifies the equity element.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Using the 2% coupon instead of the 7% market rate misstates the liability component's initial measurement and subsequent interest.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Interest expense computed on the wrong effective rate is understated each period.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate the split of the bond into liability and equity components using the 7% market rate for equivalent straight debt
Recompute periodic interest on the corrected effective rate and quantify the understatement
Review the terms for features — resets, puts, contingent conversion — that affect the split analysis
Test the diluted EPS computation for inclusion of the conversion feature and the assumed conversion method
Confirm the bond's issue proceeds and coupon payments with the trustee
Enquire of management why conversion is deemed unlikely and whether that view changed with share price movements
procedures.trap_explanation: Likelihood of conversion is irrelevant to the required split accounting of the instrument at inception; management's view is not the criterion, and the enquiry does not test the misstated measurement.

scenarios.client_context: A wholly-owned subsidiary has accumulated losses of EUR 40m and recognizes a DTA in full, supported by a group cash-flow forecast showing the subsidiary returning to profit — a forecast the group CFO signs, and which assumes a new contract with the group's largest customer that has not yet been tendered. The subsidiary has no history of profits and its market is shrinking.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Recognizing a DTA on losses whose recovery depends on an untendered contract, in a shrinking market with no profit history, is not supported by convincing evidence; the forecast's optimism overstates the asset.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The DTA's reliance on forecasts and its sensitivity require disclosure of the judgement.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the forecast's assumptions — contract win probability, market size, margins — against external market data and tender status
Recompute the DTA using probability-weighted scenarios of taxable profits, including a no-recovery scenario
Review the history of forecast versus actual for this subsidiary over the past three years to test predictive reliability
Assess whether the recoverability judgement and its sensitivity are disclosed
Confirm the loss carryforward amounts with the tax authority
procedures.trap_explanation: The losses' existence is not in dispute; the risk is whether they can ever be used. Confirming the loss amount does not test recoverability, which depends on future profits.

scenarios.client_context: The company announced a buyback of up to 100m shares and began purchasing through a broker in the final quarter. Purchases were recorded directly against retained earnings, at a price above the announced cap for two blocks executed in the last week, and the treasury shares are presented as an asset in one subsidiary's standalone accounts. The CFO's bonus is tied to ROE, which the buyback mechanically improves.

assertions_high_risk.classification: Treasury shares must be deducted from equity, not charged to retained earnings or held as an asset; both treatments are present.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Purchases above the announced cap raise whether authorization limits were breached or trades recorded outside the programme.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The programme's scope, limits and treasury share movements require disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Agree all purchase settlements to broker confirmations and the board authorization, investigating the above-cap blocks
Evaluate the presentation of treasury shares in both group and subsidiary accounts against equity deduction requirements
Recalculate average cost and reconcile treasury share movements to the share register
Review the equity note and buyback disclosures for limits, progress and holdings
Confirm the brokerage account balance with the broker
procedures.trap_explanation: Broker balance confirmation verifies settlement cash, but the flagged risks are authorization breaches and equity classification; a balance confirmation cannot speak to either.

scenarios.client_context: The chain is closing 12 of 60 stores; six are loss-making with no reversal expected, and leases have 5 years to run with no break rights. Management recognized a provision for the six loss-making stores but sized it as one year's losses only, on the argument that performance might improve. Two stores were sublet at below-lease rates, and the sublease income was ignored in the provision build.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A one-year-loss size for five-year unavoidable leases understates the provision, and ignoring sublease income overstates it in the opposite direction — the build must capture both.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Stores on the closure list but not yet loss-making may still meet the onerous test; the population may be incomplete.

procedures.procedure: Recompute the provision for each store over the full remaining lease term, including unavoidable costs net of sublease income
Test the onerous criteria for all 12 closure-list stores, not only those currently loss-making
Agree the sublease terms and rates to executed sublease agreements and verify inclusion in the model
Review the disclosures of the provision's nature, build-up and expected timing
Confirm lease terms and remaining durations with the landlords
procedures.trap_explanation: Landlord confirmation verifies the leases exist, but the flagged risks are the size of the onerous provision and completeness of the store population; the lease terms are inputs already known, not the disputed measurement.

scenarios.client_context: Each of the four sibling-owned group companies guarantees the bank facilities of the others. The group presents only company-level accounts, and the notes list guarantees given for the company's own facility but not the guarantees of siblings' facilities. One sibling company's facility was recently restructured after covenant stress, and its bank has reserved rights against guarantors.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Cross-guarantees of siblings' facilities are omitted from the note, so the disclosed contingent liability population is incomplete.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The stressed sibling's facility makes the guarantee exposure probable enough that non-disclosure would mislead users of the company-level accounts.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the facility agreements of all four sibling companies for guarantee clauses and reconcile against the disclosed note
Read the restructuring correspondence with the stressed sibling's bank for reservation-of-rights language against guarantors
Obtain a listing of all guarantees given and received and test it for completeness against legal files and board minutes
Evaluate whether the probability of call and the amounts require disclosure or recognition in the company-level accounts
Enquire of the group's bankers whether any further cross-collateral arrangements exist
Confirm the company's own facility balance with its bank
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirming the company's own loan tests its recorded borrowings; the flagged risk is undisclosed guarantees of other entities' facilities, which the company's own bank confirmation does not cover.

scenarios.client_context: The company deducts 5% employee pension contributions from wages and pays them over monthly with the employer's 3% match. The payroll-to-provider file is keyed by a part-time clerk; 2% of employees were mapped to the wrong scheme in a mid-year provider migration, and the provider reports unallocated receipts in a suspense account that has been growing for four months.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The migration mapping error means contributions for mis-mapped employees are calculated and routed wrongly.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Growing provider suspense balances indicate deductions that never reached employees' pots — amounts deducted but not allocated.

procedures.procedure: Reconcile total deductions per payroll to provider allocations, quantifying the suspense account's growth by month
Trace a sample of mis-mapped employees from payroll to provider records and recompute their contributions
Obtain the provider's mapping-file change log for the migration and review approvals
Confirm the year-end contributions payable and suspense balance directly with the pension provider
Recalculate the employer 3% match for a payroll sample
Confirm employees' pot balances with a sample of scheme members
procedures.trap_explanation: Member pot confirmations verify recorded member balances, but the flagged risks are routing errors and unallocated suspense; members cannot see suspense, and confirming pots presumes the allocation worked.

scenarios.client_context: Brokers earn 20% commission on new business and 5% on renewals, paid one month after policy inception. The monthly accrual is computed by the broker team leads in a shared spreadsheet. Two teams have been splitting policies into multiple mid-term adjustments that each attract new-business commission, and the claims run-off on one large scheme suggests some policies were bound to hit a quarterly contest deadline and cancelled within the free-look period.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Policies bound for contest deadlines then cancelled within the free-look period generate commission on business that never became effective.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Splitting policies into adjustments to re-trigger new-business rates overstates the accrual.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The spreadsheet accrual does not appear to reverse commissions on cancelled policies.

procedures.procedure: Match commission accruals to policies and identify those cancelled within the free-look period, testing whether commissions were reversed
Recompute commission on a sample of split-adjustment policies against the scheme's contractual rate table
Analyse new-business commission spikes around contest deadlines and the subsequent cancellation pattern
Review the spreadsheet's reversal logic and access rights of team leads
Confirm commission statements with the two largest insurers
Confirm accrued commission balances with a sample of brokers
procedures.trap_explanation: Brokers are the parties who benefit from the accrual; their confirmation of their own commission cannot test splitting abuse or un-reversed cancellations — the flagged risks.

scenarios.line_item: Net investment in a foreign operation
scenarios.client_context: The group's currency position includes a long-term EUR loan from the parent to its US subsidiary, designated as a net investment hedge in a memo spreadsheet. The designation memo was written two years ago and never updated; meanwhile the subsidiary also borrowed locally in USD, changing the hedgeable net investment. Translation differences on the loan are parked in a hedging reserve even though designation documentation is stale.

assertions_high_risk.classification: A stale designation that no longer matches the actual net investment may fail hedge criteria, moving translation differences to profit or loss instead of equity.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Net investment hedge disclosures must reflect the actual designated amounts and the hedge's effect; the memo's staleness makes them misleading.

procedures.procedure: Recompute the hedgeable net investment amount including the subsidiary's new local borrowing and test the designation's continued validity
Review the designation memo's terms against the actual loan and net investment at each reporting date
Trace translation differences on the loan to equity or P&L according to hedge qualification, and quantify any misrouting
Evaluate the net investment hedge disclosures for designated amounts and effectiveness
Confirm the loan balance with the subsidiary's bank
procedures.trap_explanation: The loan's existence is agreed between parent and subsidiary; the flagged risks are hedge designation validity and the routing of translation differences — accounting judgements a bank cannot confirm.

scenarios.client_context: A government subsidy covers 40% of the cost of electric buses, payable on proof of delivery and 12 months' operating data. The operator recognized the full subsidy at delivery of all 60 buses, but 8 buses delivered in the last month have no operating data yet, and 5 buses from the first tranche were reassigned to a non-subsidized charter route, which the subsidy terms prohibit for 24 months.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Recognizing subsidy income for buses whose conditions — operating data, route restrictions — are not yet met books income before the qualifying events occur.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The amounts for reassigned buses may need to be repaid; the recognized income may be overstated.

procedures.procedure: Read the subsidy agreement's conditions and map each condition to evidence at year-end for all 60 buses
Recalculate recognizable subsidy for buses meeting conditions, isolating the 8 without operating data
Inspect route logs for the 5 reassigned buses and evaluate repayment or clawback exposure
Review whether the clawback risk is disclosed as a condition or contingency
Confirm amounts received and conditions status with the transport authority
Physically inspect the fleet and verify bus identification numbers
procedures.trap_explanation: Seeing the buses confirms delivery — an agreed fact — but the flagged risks are unmet operating conditions and route breaches; a physical count cannot test compliance conditions.

scenarios.client_context: The subsidiary breached its own leverage test and its 12-month forecast shows cash exhaustion in month seven. The parent provided a support letter in January stating it 'intends to maintain support', but the letter is unsigned by the parent's board, expires in six months, and the parent itself has covenant headroom of only 4%. The draft accounts note the letter as sufficient without describing its limits.

assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: An unsigned, expiring letter from a covenant-tight parent does not remove the material uncertainty, and describing it as sufficient without limits misleads.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: On a break-up basis, the subsidiary's assets may be overstated; the going concern judgement rests on weak support.
assertions_high_risk.classification: If the going concern basis fails, current/non-current reclassification of the whole balance sheet follows.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the support letter's signatories, expiry and conditions, and evaluate whether the parent's board has authorized it
Assess the parent's own covenant headroom and forecast to test its ability to honour the support
Evaluate the disclosure of the conditions and expiry of the support in the subsidiary's draft accounts
Consider the break-up value implications if the basis is inappropriate and the reclassification effects
Obtain a written representation from management on its assessment and knowledge of the parent's intentions
Confirm the subsidiary's year-end bank balances with the bank
procedures.trap_explanation: Cash confirmation verifies a present balance while the dispute is about future support; the letter's validity and the parent's capacity are the evidence needed, not today's bank balance.

scenarios.client_context: The firm holds client balances in a client account reconciled monthly by the finance manager, who also transfers funds between client and office accounts when fees fall due. Two property transactions completed in December left residual balances unreturned, one for 11 months. The regulator's inspection is due next quarter, and office-account overdraft is serviced from client account surpluses in busy months.

assertions_high_risk.rights_and_obligations: Client money used to cover office overdrafts breaches segregation rules and misstates who owns the balance.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Residual unreturned balances may not all be identified in the ledger, especially from older completions.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Client ledger balances in the accounting system may not reflect actual bank-held client money after inter-account transfers.

procedures.procedure: Reconcile the client bank account to the total of client ledger balances and investigate reconciling items
Review all client-to-office transfers in the year and test whether each was for properly invoiced fees for that client
Age client balances and test the identification and return process for residuals over six months
Confirm the client account balance with the bank and confirm terms with the regulator's guidance on segregation
Inspect disclosures of client money holdings and the regulatory breach risk in the financial statements
Vouch a sample of office account fee receipts to client invoices
procedures.trap_explanation: Fee receipt vouching tests the firm's own revenue, but the flagged risks are segregation and existence of client money; the office account's income trail says nothing about whose money sits in the client account.

scenarios.client_context: The group participates in a scheme where customers buy vouchers at 70% of face value, the government tops up the rest. The group recognized the full face value of all vouchers sold as revenue at sale date. Redemption tracking is manual; the scheme's terms require unclaimed balances after 18 months to be repaid, and 30% of last year's vouchers remain unredeemed.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Recognizing voucher face value at sale books revenue before meals are served.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The revenue per redeemed voucher is the discounted sale price plus top-up only when conditions are met; unredeemed balances create a repayment liability rather than income.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Manual redemption tracking makes the split of redemptions across the period-end uncertain.

procedures.procedure: Recompute revenue as vouchers redeemed at the correct amount and compare to the recognized figure, quantifying the misstatement
Trace redemption reports for December and January to the booking system and test the period allocation
Assess the repayment liability for vouchers approaching the 18-month expiry using redemption curves
Reconcile voucher sales, redemptions and balances to the government scheme administrator's data
Confirm the group's scheme settlement balance with the scheme administrator
Observe meal service at one restaurant for an evening
procedures.trap_explanation: Watching service proves meals are served — an undisputed fact — while the flagged risks are the recognition timing and measurement of unredeemed vouchers; observation is irrelevant to the accounting build-up.

scenarios.line_item: Goodwill impairment testing against management's budget
scenarios.client_context: The group's CGU carrying value includes goodwill from a fibre-network acquisition. The impairment model uses a five-year cash-flow forecast built on the board-approved budget, which assumes market share recovers from 18% to 30% and ARPU grows 6% annually despite three consecutive years of decline. The recoverable amount exceeds carrying value by 4%, and head-office bonus pools are tied to the fibre CGU's reported results.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The approved budget's aggressive share and ARPU assumptions may lack support and materially inflate the recoverable amount, leaving a 4% headroom that conceals impairment.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Key assumptions, sensitivity, and the thin headroom may not be adequately disclosed.

procedures.procedure: Compare budget assumptions (market share, ARPU, churn, capex) to external market data, regulator statistics, and prior-year actuals to evaluate whether they are reasonable and supportable
Perform retrospective review of prior-year budgets against actual outcomes to assess management's forecasting bias
Recalculate the discounted cash-flow model, independently evaluating the discount rate and terminal growth rate against market evidence
Perform sensitivity analysis on the key assumptions to determine whether reasonably possible changes eliminate the 4% headroom, and assess whether sensitivity and headroom are adequately disclosed
Confirm with the group CFO that the fibre CGU is not impaired and obtain a management representation letter covering the goodwill balance
procedures.trap_explanation: A representation and the CFO's assertion confirm management's opinion but provide no audit evidence about the reasonableness of the budget assumptions or the model's inputs, which are the identified valuation risks.

scenarios.line_item: Goodwill arising on a bargain-purchase business combination
scenarios.client_context: The client acquired a competing retail chain out of insolvency for EUR 40 million when the fair value of identifiable net assets was measured at EUR 55 million, generating negative goodwill (gain) of EUR 15 million recognized in P&L. The identifiable-asset valuations were prepared by the client's own finance team, with store property fair values based on pre-insolvency appraisals and inventory marked at the acquirer's normal retail margin rather than the forced-sale prices paid.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Understating the fair value of acquired assets (stale property appraisals, retail-margin inventory) inflates the bargain-purchase gain; the measurement of acquired assets drives the P&L gain.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The EUR 15 million gain calculation depends on precise net-asset measurement; errors in the purchase-price allocation flow directly into the gain.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The nature of the gain and the basis of asset fair values must be disclosed; a gain from an insolvency purchase may be misrepresented.
