procedures.procedure: Evaluate the competence, capability, and objectivity of those involved in asset fair-value measurement, and consider engaging an auditor's expert to re-perform property and inventory valuations
Vouch the acquisition agreement, insolvency filings, and completion accounts to confirm the consideration paid of EUR 40 million and the occurrence of the transaction
Recalculate the fair-value schedule of identifiable net assets, testing inventory to forced-sale/exit pricing and property to current market evidence at the acquisition date
Inspect whether the gain is presented as a bargain-purchase gain and that valuation bases and the nature of the acquisition are disclosed
Review board minutes for the period after acquisition to understand management's plans for the acquired stores
procedures.trap_explanation: Board minutes about future plans may reveal strategy but do not audit the acquisition-date fair values of the acquired assets; the risk is that stale appraisals and retail-margin inventory pricing understate net assets and overstate the gain, which minutes cannot address.

scenarios.line_item: Level 2 corporate bond portfolio valued using broker quotes
scenarios.client_context: A EUR 9 billion corporate bond portfolio is classified as level 2 within the fair-value hierarchy. Valuations are produced by a vendor system sourcing broker quotes; audit sampling last year found 30% of quotes were stale (older than 30 days) for illiquid subordinated financial-sector paper that trades rarely. This year the same vendor is used, and a new performance bonus for the investment desk depends on reported portfolio returns exceeding a benchmark.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Stale broker quotes for illiquid bonds may not represent exit prices at the reporting date, and vendor-model adjustments could be biased toward the bonus benchmark.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Data feed errors in coupon, rating, or quote-mapping may cause pricing inaccuracies across the portfolio.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Bonds valued with stale or adjusted quotes may still be labelled level 2 when observable inputs are unavailable, misstating the hierarchy disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Test the design and implementation of controls over quote staleness, including the vendor's exception reports for quotes older than the defined threshold
Independently price a risk-based sample of illiquid bonds using pricing sources not used by management (e.g., matrix pricing or an auditor's pricing tool) and investigate differences beyond tolerance
Assess whether bonds with stale or unobservable inputs should be classified as level 3, and test the fair-value hierarchy disclosure and sensitivity disclosures
Evaluate the objectivity of the vendor as a management expert and of desk personnel given the return-based bonus, and test any management overrides of vendor prices
Send year-end confirmation requests to the custodian bank asking it to confirm the bonds held and their market values
procedures.trap_explanation: Custodian confirmations verify holdings (existence) but a custodian does not independently attest to fair values, and certainly not to the staleness of broker quotes or bonus-related bias — the actual valuation and accuracy risks.

scenarios.line_item: Embedded derivative in convertible bonds issued in foreign currency
scenarios.client_context: The client issued USD-denominated convertible bonds. Treasury separated an embedded equity-conversion derivative and, because the bonds are USD and functional currency is EUR, did not bifurcate a second embedded FX derivative, treating all FX movement in the conversion feature's value. The derivative's year-end valuation uses management's own volatility assumption of 25% when implied volatility for comparable listed options is 35%, and the liability grows with each remeasurement.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Management's 25% volatility assumption, unsupported by market-implied volatility, may understate the derivative liability.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Failure to identify and separately account for the embedded FX derivative misclassifies FX movements between derivative P&L, equity, and translation reserves.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The bifurcation and valuation calculations involve complex option-pricing models prone to computational error.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Separation of embedded derivatives, valuation inputs, and sensitivity must be disclosed.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the terms of the convertible instrument with reference to the accounting framework to identify all embedded derivatives (conversion option and FX feature) and test whether separation and classification are appropriate
Engage or use an auditor's expert to evaluate the option-pricing model, and benchmark management's 25% volatility against implied volatility from comparable listed instruments
Recalculate the derivative valuation model and its FX component, including testing the completeness of year-end remeasurement entries
Inspect whether embedded derivative accounting, key inputs, and FX classification are adequately disclosed
Review the bond trustee's annual report for confirmation of the total principal outstanding at year end
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirming principal outstanding verifies the debt balance but does not address the identified risks: bifurcation of the FX derivative, the unsupported volatility assumption, or model accuracy — the derivative's valuation and classification are untouched.

scenarios.line_item: Loss component under the premium allocation approach (IFRS 17)
scenarios.client_context: For short-duration motor policies the client applies the premium allocation approach. At year end the model carries a loss component on a cohort of policies sold with underpriced premiums after a pricing error. The actuarial team calculates the loss component from ultimate claims estimates; the claims development pattern for the affected cohort was changed this year from 18 to 9 months with no documented rationale, which reduces the measured loss component. The pricing error was discovered by management in November but the remediation memo is dated after year end.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The shortened claims development pattern, without rationale, reduces the loss component; measurement depends on subjective development assumptions.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: The loss component may not cover all in-scope cohorts affected by the pricing error, and late-identified onerous groups may be omitted.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: IFRS 17 requires disclosure of the loss component, basis of preparation, and changes in estimates.

procedures.procedure: Involve an auditor's actuarial expert to evaluate the rationale for and effect of the shortened claims development pattern, benchmarking against historical development of comparable cohorts
Test the completeness of the loss component by reconciling the affected-policy population from the pricing-error investigation to the cohorts modelled
Recalculate the loss component for a sample of cohorts, tracing premium, ultimate claims, and development inputs to source data
Review post-year-end remediation documentation and assess whether it constitutes evidence of conditions existing at year end requiring adjustment or disclosure of the pricing error and loss component
Inspect the insurance contract liability note to confirm the number of motor policies in force at year end
procedures.trap_explanation: Verifying policy counts confirms scale of the portfolio but does not test the loss component's measurement, the completeness of affected cohorts, or the disclosure of the pricing error and changed development pattern — the identified risks.

scenarios.line_item: Carried interest and fee income of a private equity fund manager
scenarios.client_context: The manager consolidates a PE fund it controls and recognizes carried interest entitlement when the fund's cumulative returns pass the 8% preferred return hurdle. Full realizations are years away; carried interest is recognized on a cumulative-catch-up basis following a recent upward revaluation of the two largest portfolio companies. The valuations use EBITDA multiples provided by the deal partner who negotiated the investments, and the fund agreement allows clawback of carried interest if later realizations underperform.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Deal-partner EBITDA multiples are not independent and may overstate portfolio valuations, driving premature carried-interest recognition.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Recognizing carried interest on unrealized revaluations may not represent income that has occurred per the fund's terms and realization-based hurdle mechanics.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The basis of carried-interest recognition and clawback exposure may not be adequately disclosed.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the fund's limited partnership agreement to confirm hurdle, catch-up, and clawback mechanics and evaluate whether the revenue recognition policy complies with the framework
Evaluate the objectivity of valuation inputs; benchmark the deal partner's EBITDA multiples against comparable-transaction evidence and independent market data for the portfolio companies' sectors
Recalculate the cumulative catch-up computation from the waterfall, tracing performance data to custodian and capital-account statements
Assess whether the clawback obligation is measured and the recognition basis, valuation inputs, and clawback exposure are disclosed
Confirm year-end capital-account balances with the fund's limited partners
procedures.trap_explanation: LP confirmations verify capital balances and commitments but not whether carried interest should have been recognized on unrealized revaluations or whether the deal partner's multiples are supportable — the flagged occurrence and valuation risks are untested.

scenarios.line_item: Derecognition of auto-loan receivables transferred to a securitization vehicle
scenarios.client_context: The client transfers EUR 2 billion of auto loans to a securitization SPV quarterly, derecognizing them and recognizing a gain or loss on sale. The servicing sub-fee gives the client the power to direct the SPV's relevant activities, and the client also holds 8% of the tranched notes issued by the SPV, retained in a first-loss position. The SPV's board consists of the client's treasury employees. Group statements present the SPV off balance sheet, while the standalone statutory accounts of the SPV are audited by another firm.

assertions_high_risk.rights_and_obligations: Power over the SPV's relevant activities plus exposure to variable returns may require consolidation; derecognition may misstate the group's rights and obligations over the transferred assets.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Failed derecognition or required consolidation could mislead users if transfers, retained interests, and continuing involvement are not disclosed.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The gain-on-sale calculation depends on the fair value of retained interests, which are valued by treasury using internal prepayment and loss assumptions.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the SPV's governance, decision-making over relevant activities, and returns exposure against the control framework to conclude on consolidation in the group statements
Inspect transfer agreements, note purchase documents, and first-loss tranche holdings to determine retained interests and continuing involvement
Evaluate the fair-value measurement of retained interests, benchmarking prepayment and loss assumptions against external evidence
Assess whether transfers of receivables, retained interests, and servicing are disclosed, and reconcile transfer disclosures to the group structure chart
Obtain confirmation from the SPV's administrator of the principal balances of loans held by the SPV at year end
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirming the SPV's loan balances verifies assets the group may not even own; the flagged risks are whether derecognition/consolidation is appropriate and whether retained-interest valuation is supportable — balance confirmations do not address control analysis or fair value.

scenarios.line_item: Repossessed residential properties held as collateral assets
scenarios.client_context: A prolonged housing downturn doubled repossessions: 240 properties taken into possession are held at the lower of cost and estimated fair value less costs to sell. The valuation comes from internal mortgage advisers who originally sold the properties' loans; 15 properties have been unsold for over 18 months despite two asking-price reductions, and a government rent-control scheme announced post year end affects the rental yield used in two valuations. Management concluded no impairment is needed, using an internal index of asking prices rather than transaction prices.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Valuations by advisers with conflicting interests, unsold listings, and asking-price indices may overstate recoverable amounts and omit impairment.
assertions_high_risk.rights_and_obligations: Legal title transfer on repossession must be complete before assets are recognized, and pending borrower redemption rights may affect ownership.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Collateral-held assets and the post-year-end rent-control scheme may require disclosure under events after the reporting period.

procedures.procedure: For a risk-based sample of repossessed properties, independently value using external evidence (land registry transaction prices, independent agents), focusing on the 18-month-old listings
Inspect legal title documentation and possession orders to confirm the client's rights at the reporting date, and enquire about borrower redemption claims
Evaluate the post-year-end rent-control announcement as an adjusting or disclosing event, including its effect on the two yield-based valuations
Assess the objectivity and competence of the internal mortgage advisers performing valuations, and test controls over review of their work
Physically inspect a sample of repossessed properties to verify their existence and condition
procedures.trap_explanation: Physical inspection confirms the properties exist and their state, but the flagged risks concern biased valuations, incomplete legal title, and disclosure of the post-year-end scheme — none of which presence at the site resolves.

scenarios.line_item: Net investment hedge of a USD subsidiary using cross-currency swaps
scenarios.client_context: The group hedges its net investment in a USD operation using cross-currency swaps designated as a net investment hedge, expecting hedge gains to remain in the FX translation reserve. Mid-year the USD operation was partially disposed of, reducing the net investment, but the hedge notional was unchanged; hedge accounting continues, and management reallocated a portion of the swap gains from the reserve to P&L using an internally documented policy that the external auditor has not previously reviewed. Year-end swap valuation is performed by a treasury system whose FX-forward curve feed failed in December and was manually patched.

assertions_high_risk.classification: After partial disposal the hedge may exceed the net investment, forcing discontinued hedge accounting; reclassifying reserve amounts to P&L may misclassify FXOCI amounts.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The manually patched FX curve may misstate swap valuations at year end.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Manual patch entries and hedge-effectiveness recalculations are error-prone.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Hedge designation, discontinued hedge accounting, and amounts reclassified from OCI must be disclosed.

procedures.procedure: Recompute the net investment in the USD operation after the partial disposal and test whether the hedged amount continues to qualify; evaluate where discontinued amounts were recorded
Independently value the cross-currency swaps at year end using external FX and interest-rate curves, and investigate differences against the treasury system's patched output
Review management's reallocation policy and recalculate amounts transferred from the FX translation reserve to P&L for compliance with the framework
Test whether hedge relationships, discontinued designations, and OCI reclassifications are adequately disclosed
Confirm the notional amounts and maturity dates of the cross-currency swaps with the counterparty banks at year end
procedures.trap_explanation: Swap confirmations verify contractual terms but not the flagged risks: post-disposal hedge accounting qualification, the patched valuation curve, or the propriety of OCI reallocations — confirmations cannot test classification and measurement judgements.

scenarios.line_item: Pillar Two top-up tax provision and disclosure
scenarios.client_context: The group operates in 14 jurisdictions and applies the OECD Pillar Two rules. The tax team computes a top-up tax provision of EUR 22 million using a spreadsheet with 14 tabs, manual data feeds from local statutory accounts, and a single analyst who understands the model. Two jurisdictions with low effective tax rates changed local incentives mid-year, and the safe-harbour election for one jurisdiction depends on qualified CbCR data that the group has never before prepared. Disclosure of the expected top-up tax in the coming year was drafted by the tax manager but omits one jurisdiction.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Manual spreadsheet inputs risk omitting jurisdictions or entities from the 15% minimum-tax computation, particularly where local incentives changed.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Single-analyst spreadsheet models without independent review are prone to formula and data-mapping errors.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Safe-harbour qualification depends on qualified CbCR data whose preparation controls are untested; misstatement affects the provision's measurement.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The draft disclosure omits a jurisdiction and may be incomplete.

procedures.procedure: Reconcile the entity and jurisdiction population in the Pillar Two model to the group structure, statutory filings, and the consolidation system to test completeness
Recalculate a sample of jurisdiction computations, tracing income, covered taxes, and incentive inputs to local statutory accounts and tax returns; test spreadsheet formula integrity
Evaluate whether the safe-harbour election is supported, including the preparation process and data quality of the qualified CbCR data
Review the top-up tax disclosure against the computation, confirming all jurisdictions, expected future charges, and timing are disclosed
Discuss the group's transfer-pricing policy with the head of tax and obtain a signed representation confirming the top-up tax figure
procedures.trap_explanation: A management representation is not audit evidence of the computation itself; the flagged risks — omitted jurisdictions, spreadsheet errors, untested safe-harbour data, and incomplete disclosure — require substantive testing, not assurance from the responsible manager.

scenarios.line_item: Pension plan surplus restricted by the asset ceiling
scenarios.client_context: A strong asset performance moved the client's defined benefit plan into a surplus of EUR 60 million. The net asset was recognized in full, but plan amendments allow refunds or reduced future contributions only via a 5-year contribution holiday capped at EUR 40 million. The actuarial report is issued by the plan actuary who has advised the trustees for 15 years. A proposed union agreement, signed after year end but negotiated before, would restore contributions and remove any refund access. The airline's own published guidance emphasizes 'balance-sheet strength' to aircraft lessors.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Recognizing a EUR 60 million asset exceeds the EUR 40 million economic benefit available through the contribution holiday; the asset ceiling may be misapplied given the post-year-end union agreement.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The ceiling computation and actuarial data flows are error-prone.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The asset ceiling restriction, surplus nature, and the union agreement's effect may not be disclosed.

procedures.procedure: Inspect plan documents and trust deeds to determine the forms and amounts of economic benefit available (refund or contribution reduction), and recalculate the asset ceiling against the EUR 40 million cap
Evaluate the union agreement as an adjusting or non-adjusting post-year-end event and assess its effect on refund access and the asset ceiling
Assess the competence, capability, and objectivity of the plan actuary, and evaluate the actuarial valuation's key assumptions (discount rate, mortality) against market evidence
Test whether the asset-ceiling restriction, the surplus, and the union agreement are disclosed in the pension note
Vouch contributions paid and refunds received to bank statements during the year and reconcile to the pension ledger
procedures.trap_explanation: Reconciling cash movements to the pension ledger verifies historical contributions but not the flagged risks: whether the recognized net asset respects the asset ceiling and whether the post-year-end agreement removes refund access — measurement and disclosure judgements that cash testing cannot reach.

scenarios.line_item: Inventory destroyed in a warehouse fire after the reporting date
scenarios.client_context: On 15 January, three weeks after the 31 December year end, a fire destroyed a regional warehouse holding EUR 18 million of inventory carried at cost. The insurance claim may recover only 60% of value and settlement is expected to take 18 months. Inventory was counted on 27 December and no adjustment was made; management asserts the fire is a non-adjusting event requiring only disclosure, while the draft disclosure omits the expected insurance shortfall. A prior audit noted the client's tendency to defer loss recognition after adverse events.

assertions_high_risk.existence: Whether inventory recognized at year end physically existed — the fire shows the warehouse's stock may have been misstated even at 31 December if counts or cut-off were misapplied.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Inventory loss allowance may need to reflect conditions existing at year end, including NRV and insurance-recovery measurement.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The non-adjusting event disclosure omits the insurance shortfall and financial effect.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the count records for the destroyed warehouse, including 27 December count sheets, and reconcile the last recorded inventory to fire-loss listings compiled for the insurance claim
Investigate the fire's cause and timeline with fire-service and expert reports to determine whether any condition (e.g., electrical fault, earlier incident) existed at year end
Obtain the insurance policy and broker correspondence; evaluate whether the claim, expected recovery, and timing are appropriately measured and whether recoveries are recognized per the framework
Review subsequent-event procedures and test that the disclosure states the event's nature and estimated financial effect, including the EUR 7 million uninsured shortfall
Extend year-end inventory count testing at other warehouses to obtain broader assurance over the inventory balance
procedures.trap_explanation: Counting other warehouses tests stock elsewhere, but the flagged risks concern the destroyed warehouse's year-end balance, its valuation, and the incomplete disclosure — extending testing at unaffected sites does not respond to them.

scenarios.line_item: Classification of interest paid within the cash flow statement
scenarios.client_context: The draft cash flow statement classifies EUR 120 million of interest paid on vessel loans as investing outflows alongside newbuild capex, while interest received on surplus cash is within operating. The classification changed last year from operating without disclosure of the change or its effect, and the group's covenant package defines 'cash flow from operations' excluding interest. The FD states the change better reflects the business, and analysts' models the group benchmarks against assume interest is operating.

assertions_high_risk.classification: Interest paid may not meet the criteria for investing classification under the framework; the prior-year change may misclassify operating cash flows and flatter covenant metrics.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The change in classification, its comparability effect, and the covenant definition's divergence are undisclosed.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Reclassification affects subtotal arithmetic and comparative figures.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the client's policy for interest classification against the framework's requirements and the cash-generating purpose of the vessel loans
Recast the cash flow statement subtotals on a consistent basis, recalculating the operating and investing subtotals and the comparatives
Test whether the change in classification, its amount, and comparability effects are disclosed; evaluate the covenant definition against the presented 'cash flow from operations' subtotal
Vouch interest paid to loan statements and bank records to confirm the EUR 120 million and its allocation between loans
Inspect the newbuild vessel purchase invoices to verify the capex amounts included in investing activities
procedures.trap_explanation: Vouching capex invoices verifies investing outflows exist, but the flagged risks are the interest classification, undisclosed policy change, and covenant interaction — verifying vessel purchases does not address where interest paid belongs.

scenarios.line_item: Receivables sold under a factoring arrangement with recourse
scenarios.client_context: The client sells roughly 40% of receivables to a factoring bank, derecognizing them and booking a loss on sale each month. The agreement allows the factor full recourse for credit losses, with a quarterly true-up based on actual collections; last year's true-ups consistently produced refunds from the client exceeding the original loss booked by 25%. The sales ledger team applies a pre-computation of the expected recourse obligation using a 12-month default table that has not been updated for the current economic environment (customer defaults rising). Derecognition is approved by the treasury manager, who reports a KPI on 'working capital released'.

assertions_high_risk.rights_and_obligations: With full recourse, substantially all risks and rewards may be retained, so derecognition may be inappropriate and the receivables should remain on balance sheet.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The expected recourse obligation uses an outdated default table and may be understated, misstating any continuing involvement or provision.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: The recourse obligation may not capture all true-up settlements, given persistent refunds exceeding estimates.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Monthly loss-on-sale and true-up computations are error-prone.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the factoring agreement to evaluate transfer of risks and rewards (recourse terms, true-up mechanics) and conclude on derecognition appropriateness
Recalculate the expected recourse obligation using current-environment default data, and reconcile historical true-up refunds to the estimates to test adequacy
Trace a sample of factored invoices to bank credit advices and the sales ledger to test accuracy of transferred balances and loss-on-sale computations

Evaluate whether continuing involvement, recourse obligations, and the working-capital KPI's effect on management incentives are considered in the risk assessment, and test disclosure of the arrangement
Send direct confirmations to a sample of factored customers at year end asking them to confirm the receivable balances
procedures.trap_explanation: Customer confirmations address receivables existence, but the flagged risks are derecognition under full recourse, the understated recourse obligation, and completeness of true-ups — debts that were sold and may not even belong to the client; confirmation cannot resolve transfer-of-rights or measurement issues.

scenarios.line_item: Non-controlling interest put option valued as a financial liability
scenarios.client_context: A minority shareholder in the group's largest wind-farm subsidiary holds a long-dated put option requiring the group to repurchase its 25% stake at fair value. The put is valued using a DCF of the subsidiary, with the model prepared by the group's own development team whose bonuses depend on the group's reported net assets. Wind-farm valuations are acutely sensitive to power-price curves; the team uses the forward curve for only two years and a flat price of EUR 85/MWh for years 3-25 while current long-dated market products imply EUR 60. The put's fair value is 60% of consolidated net assets and grows each year.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The EUR 85/MWh flat long-term price, unsupported by market evidence and set by interested personnel, likely overstates subsidiary value and the liability understated or overstated depending on direction; power-price curve selection is the critical judgement.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Complex long-dated DCF computations are error-prone.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Other obligations to the minority holder (preferential distributions, guaranteed returns) may not be included in the liability.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The basis of the put's valuation and its sensitivity to power prices may not be disclosed.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the competence, objectivity, and incentives of the development team, and benchmark the EUR 85/MWh flat price and two-year forward-curve approach against independent long-dated market data and expert analysis

Consider using an auditor's expert to independently evaluate and recalculate the DCF model's discount rate, long-dated price curve, and terminal assumptions, tracing production and tariff data to independent engineering reports
Inspect the shareholders' agreement and put option deed to identify all components of the obligation, including preferential returns or guarantees, and test completeness of the liability
Test that the valuation methodology and power-price sensitivity of the put liability are disclosed
Review board minutes for approval of the subsidiary's annual budget
procedures.trap_explanation: Board approval of the budget evidences internal sign-off but not the fairness of the EUR 85/MWh long-term price, the completeness of obligations to the minority shareholder, or model accuracy — the identified valuation risks remain untested.

scenarios.client_context: Revenue is invoiced monthly when support tickets are closed in the ticketing system; a consultant closes tickets manually and there is no automated link to the billing module. December billings were 30% above the monthly average after a year-end push tied to the consultants' utilization bonuses, and 15 tickets invoiced in December were reopened by clients in January.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Manual ticket closure with a utilization bonus creates an incentive to close and bill tickets for work not performed.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Tickets closed after year end may be billed in December to inflate billings, and reopened tickets suggest work was not complete at closure.

procedures.procedure: Vouch a sample of December invoices to the underlying tickets, client sign-off or resolution notes evidencing the work was performed
Test that tickets reopened in January were not billed in December unless evidence supports completion at year end
Trace a sample of closed tickets through to the billing module and recalculate the invoiced amount against the contracted hourly rates
Confirm year-end receivable balances with the largest clients
procedures.trap_explanation: Receivable confirmations address whether debts exist, but the flagged risks are whether closed tickets represent work actually performed and whether closure cut-off is correct — balance confirmation does not evidence ticket-level work or timing.

scenarios.line_item: Store cash sweeps from point-of-sale terminals
scenarios.client_context: Each store's POS system is configured to sweep daily takings into the group bank account overnight, but 12 of 90 stores show unreconciled differences between POS takings and bank deposits for the last two weeks of the year, and three stores' daily sweep reports were manually edited by store managers before upload.

assertions_high_risk.existence: Edited sweep reports may conceal cash taken before it reached the bank, so recorded cash sweeps may not exist at the reported amount.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Differences between POS takings and bank deposits may indicate takings never swept or recorded, understating cash.

procedures.procedure: Reconcile daily POS takings to bank deposit records for a sample of stores, focusing on the 12 stores with unreconciled differences
Compare the population of registered terminal IDs to terminals with recorded sweeps to test that all stores' takings are captured
For the stores with edited reports, obtain the original system-generated report from the POS provider and investigate each edit
Obtain bank statements for January and review deposits received after year end
procedures.trap_explanation: Reviewing January deposits tests the timing of subsequent receipts, but the flagged risks are whether year-end sweep records are complete and unmanipulated — later deposits do not evidence whether the December sweeps were edited or missing.

scenarios.line_item: Trade payables and supplier statement reconciliations
scenarios.client_context: The purchase ledger runs on a legacy system where invoices are matched to goods-received notes manually. Two major suppliers stopped issuing monthly statements this year after a portal migration, and a sample during the interim audit found three unrecorded invoices for goods received in December that were only entered in February.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Manual matching plus missing supplier statements create a risk that December goods-received invoices are unrecorded, understating payables.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Without supplier statements, duplicated or fictitious supplier balances are harder to detect.

procedures.procedure: Search unmatched goods-received notes at year end and trace the corresponding supplier invoices into the purchase ledger after year end
Reconcile supplier portal balances for the two largest suppliers to the ledger, and obtain direct supplier confirmations where portal data is unavailable
Vouch a sample of recorded payables to subsequent payment and the supplier invoice to confirm the balance is genuine and accurately recorded
Vouch a sample of payments made after year end to supporting invoices
procedures.trap_explanation: Vouching subsequent payments tests whether recorded payables existed (existence direction), but the flagged risk is understatement — invoices received and goods delivered before year end that never entered the ledger — which payment testing cannot detect because unpaid unrecorded liabilities leave no payment trail.

scenarios.client_context: Employees submit T&E claims through an app with photos of receipts; claims under EUR 75 need no manager approval. Entertainment of clients is commissionable to brokers as a marketing support credit, and one team's claims doubled in the final quarter while the company travel bookings remained flat.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: The sub-EUR 75 no-approval threshold and credit-linked incentive create an incentive and opportunity for fictitious or personal claims.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Client entertainment may be misclassified as staff travel to avoid entertainment tax rules and disclosure, or personal expenses claimed as business.

procedures.procedure: Vouch a risk-based sample of small unapproved claims to the receipt images and business purpose described, focusing on the team with doubled claims
Analyse claims by employee, category and month against company travel bookings to identify unusual patterns
Test that client entertainment is coded to the correct expense line and the marketing support credit, and not to staff travel
Inspect the T&E policy manual to confirm it requires receipts for all claims
procedures.trap_explanation: Reading the policy manual shows what the rules say, not whether employees complied; the flagged risks are fictitious claims and misclassification of entertainment, which require testing of actual claims, not of the written policy.

scenarios.line_item: Trade receivables and the provision matrix
scenarios.client_context: The group applies a matrix provision of 1% (current), 5% (1-90 days) and 20% (over 90 days). A top-ten customer, 4% of receivables, is over 120 days past due and in a payment plan after its own plant shutdown; the ledger still applies the 20% matrix rate with no specific provision, and currency devaluation affects two export-heavy customers.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The matrix rate of 20% for the distressed top-ten customer may materially understate the required allowance given its shutdown and payment plan.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Long-overdue export balances raise the risk that disputed or non-existent balances remain on the ledger.

procedures.procedure: Send positive confirmations to the top-ten customers, including the distressed customer, and investigate differences
Assess the recoverability of the distressed customer's balance against its payment plan performance and any security held, and evaluate whether a specific provision is required
Recalculate the matrix provision by aging bucket and test that the ledger applies the percentages correctly
Review the sales ledger for invoices issued in the first week of the new year
procedures.trap_explanation: Inspecting post-year-end invoices tests revenue cut-off, but the flagged risks are the adequacy of the provision for the distressed customer and whether aged balances exist — next-year invoicing says nothing about either.

scenarios.client_context: The fleet grew from 140 to 190 vans this year. The workshop supervisor, who approves his own purchase orders since a control redesign, capitalizes all workshop invoices over EUR 5,000; this year EUR 380,000 of engine rebuilds, resprays and tyre packages across the older vans were capitalized alongside the new van purchases.

assertions_high_risk.classification: Repairs and maintenance wrongly capitalized as additions overstate PPE and understate opex.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Self-approved purchase orders create a risk that recorded additions are not genuine assets.

procedures.procedure: Vouch a sample of capitalized additions to purchase invoices and vehicle registration documents, tracing into the fixed asset register
Inspect the nature of workshop invoices over the capitalization threshold and evaluate whether each is an asset or a repair
Physically sight a sample of new vans against registration plates at a depot visit
Review the depreciation rates for vans in the fixed asset register
procedures.trap_explanation: Reviewing depreciation rates tests the ongoing depreciation charge, but the flagged risks are fictitious or misclassified additions — whether engine rebuilds were capitalized as new vehicles — which the depreciation rate setting does not address.

scenarios.line_item: Perpetual inventory records between physical counts
scenarios.client_context: Stores perform one annual count each, spread across the year, with the system updated by head-office journal whenever a count differs. Shrinkage in the 12 stores counted in December averaged 3% versus 1% elsewhere, and the journals posting count adjustments are prepared by the same retail operations team whose bonuses are tied to store profitability.

assertions_high_risk.existence: High December shrinkage suggests recorded quantities exceed goods actually on shelves at count date.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Manually prepared adjustment journals by a bonus-incentivized team create a risk adjustments are manipulated or misposted.

procedures.procedure: Observe counts at a risk-based sample of stores not yet counted and compare results to the perpetual records at that date
Test a sample of count adjustment journals, agreeing the posted quantity to the count documentation and the preparer/reviewer sign-off
Perform roll-forward testing from the December counts to year end using purchase and sales movements
Confirm the group's stock insurance policy covers inventory at cost
procedures.trap_explanation: Insurance cover confirms the client can insure its goods but provides no evidence that recorded quantities exist or that adjustment journals are accurate — the flagged shrinkage and manipulation risks are untouched.

scenarios.client_context: The agency prepays annual SaaS subscriptions for 40 tools; the prepayment schedule is maintained in a spreadsheet updated by whoever raises the purchase. Several tools were replaced mid-year but their prepaid balances remain, and a EUR 96,000 three-year design platform contract was fully expensed at inception in the prior year but is being used this year.

assertions_high_risk.existence: Balances for tools no longer in use may remain on the spreadsheet with no rights to future service.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: The fully expensed three-year platform means a genuine future benefit is not on the balance sheet, understating prepayments.

procedures.procedure: Vouch a sample of prepaid balances to subscription invoices and confirm the service period spans year end
Reconcile the spreadsheet to the list of tools in active use, investigating balances for replaced tools
For the design platform contract, evaluate the accounting for the three-year prepayment and whether the future benefit is recognized
Inspect the approved supplier list to confirm all SaaS vendors are authorized
procedures.trap_explanation: Vendor authorization shows the vendors are legitimate suppliers, not that prepaid balances exist or are amortized correctly; the flagged risks of stale balances and omitted prepayments are about the balances themselves, not vendor approval.

scenarios.client_context: Electricity, gas and water are accrued monthly by taking the prior month's actual cost plus 5%, a shortcut adopted two years ago. Utilities are now 40% higher year on year, meter readings are submitted quarterly, and January's actual invoices received after year end exceeded the December accrual by 28%.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The prior-month-plus-5% shortcut significantly understates the accrual when costs are rising 40% year on year.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Quarterly meter readings mean some properties' consumption since the last reading may never be accrued.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate the December accrual per property using consumption since the last meter reading and current tariff rates
Reconcile utility invoices received in January and February to the December accrual and investigate unaccrued consumption
Perform analytical procedures comparing utility cost per occupied room night across properties and to prior year
Vouch utility payments made during the year to bank statements
procedures.trap_explanation: Vouching year payments confirms cash paid for utilities, but the flagged risks are whether the year-end accrual is complete and measured correctly — historical payments do not measure consumption between the last invoice and year end.

scenarios.client_context: Gift cards are sold through third-party platforms and in store; redemption data from the platforms is imported weekly via a spreadsheet, and one platform changed its export format in October, halving recorded redemptions since then. Breakage revenue is recognized based on a three-year historical redemption curve of 88%, but card terms now expire balances after two years.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: The broken platform export means actual redemptions since October may be significantly under-recorded, distorting the breakage curve and the liability.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The 88% curve based on three-year expiry may not represent redemption behaviour under the new two-year expiry, misstating breakage revenue.

procedures.procedure: Obtain redemption data directly from the affected platform for October to December and reconcile to the imported spreadsheet
Reperform the breakage estimate using redemption curves aligned to the two-year expiry, benchmarking against the platform's raw data
Test redemptions recorded in the first week of January to confirm they were not recorded in December
Physically inspect the stock of unsold gift cards at the flagship store
procedures.trap_explanation: Counting unsold cards tests card stock, not revenue: the flagged risks are the broken redemption import and the breakage estimate — neither unsold cards nor their physical presence evidences redemptions or the estimate's accuracy.

scenarios.line_item: Dividends declared and the statement of changes in equity
scenarios.client_context: The company declared an interim dividend in August and a final dividend in December, both approved by the board, but the final dividend exceeded accumulated profits available per the December draft accounts and was paid to the founding shareholder in January. The statement of changes in equity shows only the interim dividend, and the final dividend was recorded as a trade payable.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: The final dividend is omitted from the SOCIE, so equity movements are incomplete.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Recording the dividend as a trade payable misclassifies a distribution against equity.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Non-compliance with distribution rules and the misclassification may require disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Inspect board minutes and shareholder resolutions for both dividends and trace their recognition into the ledger
Evaluate the accounting classification of the final dividend, testing whether it was charged against equity rather than recorded as a payable
Recalculate distributable reserves at the declaration date and evaluate whether the final dividend complied with distribution rules
Confirm the January dividend payment appears on the bank statement
procedures.trap_explanation: Verifying the cash payment shows the dividend was paid, but the flagged risks are completeness and classification in equity — whether the SOCIE captures both dividends and whether the distribution was properly charged to reserves — neither of which the bank record resolves.

scenarios.client_context: VAT returns are prepared by the bookkeeper from the general ledger using a spreadsheet mapping; 40% of sales are zero-rated tractor parts and 60% standard-rated, but the mapping template has not been updated since the parts catalogue was restructured in April, and the final return's output tax ratio to sales has drifted from prior periods.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The stale spreadsheet mapping may charge the wrong VAT rate to restructured parts, misstating output tax.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Product codes missing from the mapping may drop out of the return altogether, understating output VAT.

procedures.procedure: Reperform the VAT return for a sample period, tracing sales and purchase ledger data through the spreadsheet mapping to the filed return
Obtain the full parts catalogue after the April restructure and reconcile its VAT rate flags to the spreadsheet mapping table
Perform analytical procedures on the ratio of output tax to standard-rated sales by period and investigate the drift
Enquire of the bookkeeper whether any VAT returns were filed late in the year
procedures.trap_explanation: Asking about filing timeliness addresses compliance deadlines, not whether the returns' figures are complete and accurate under a stale mapping — the flagged misstatement risks are about the content of the returns, not their punctuality.

scenarios.client_context: Twenty departments hold petty cash floats between EUR 200 and EUR 1,500 for field-trip costs and workshop supplies. The last surprise count was four years ago, one department's float record shows a persistent EUR 400 shortfall 'to be recovered', and float custodians in three departments changed this year without any handover documentation.

assertions_high_risk.existence: The persistent unrecovered shortfall suggests recorded float balances include cash that no longer exists.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Custodian handovers without documentation increase the risk that float records are misstated or unreconciled.

procedures.procedure: Perform surprise counts of all department floats, reconciling cash on hand to the float records
Inspect the float records for the department with the persistent shortfall, including vouchers supporting expenditures and reimbursement requests
Review the handover documentation for the three departments with new custodians and enquire of the outgoing custodians
Review the university's petty cash policy for maximum float sizes
procedures.trap_explanation: The policy's float limits are a rule, not evidence; the flagged risks are missing cash and undocumented handovers, which only physical counts and record inspection can address — policy limits do not verify any balance.

scenarios.client_context: The shared services centre recharges IT, HR and finance costs to member firms quarterly using headcount as the only driver. A new case-management platform consumed primarily by the largest member firm was recharged evenly, and EUR 1.2 million of costs relating to the group's own rebranding project were recharged in the December quarter with no supporting allocation basis shared with member firms.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Headcount-only allocation of a platform used mainly by one firm misstates each member's recharge.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Rebranding costs with no allocation basis may be recharges for services member firms never received.

procedures.procedure: Vouch a sample of December quarter recharge lines to the underlying cost records and the allocation basis issued to member firms
Evaluate the appropriateness of the headcount driver for the case-management platform against actual usage data
Test whether member-firm invoiced recharges agree to the group's recharge schedules and are recorded consistently by both parties
Confirm the group's rebranding budget was approved by the board
procedures.trap_explanation: Board approval of the rebranding budget shows the group sanctioned its own project, but the flagged risk is whether member firms received any service for the recharged costs — approval of the group's spending is not evidence of a valid recharge.

scenarios.client_context: The brand team commits media spend through insertion orders approved up to EUR 50,000 by the marketing director. December spend was 60% of the annual budget after a campaign was pulled forward, and EUR 900,000 of invoices arrived in January for media that ran in December; the accrual account has been untouched since the interim audit despite the pull-forward.

assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Media run in December but invoiced in January risks being recorded in the wrong period given the stale accrual.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: The untouched accrual for pulled-forward campaigns means December services may be unrecorded.

procedures.procedure: Obtain media flight reports for November to January campaigns and test that services delivered by year end are accrued
Trace the January invoices for December media into the accounting records as accruals, not new-year expenses
Vouch a sample of December expenses to approved insertion orders and proof of performance from media platforms
Analyse monthly marketing spend against budget to identify the December spike and its recording
procedures.trap_explanation: Budget-to-actual analysis shows spending patterns but does not verify which period the media ran in or whether all December services are recorded — the cut-off and completeness risks need flight reports and invoice tracing, not variance review.

scenarios.client_context: All laptops are depreciated over four years regardless of condition. This year 300 laptops were replaced after 20 months following a hardware fault settlement with the vendor; the old laptops were written off on disposal, but their remaining carrying value of EUR 210,000 was recorded as accelerated depreciation within the annual depreciation charge rather than as a disposal loss line.

assertions_high_risk.classification: Disposal losses presented within depreciation misclassify the nature of the expense and distort the depreciation line used in forecasts.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The write-off computation and the ongoing depreciation of retained laptops need recalculation, including the shortened replacement cycle.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate depreciation for a sample of laptops on the register, testing cost, useful life and accumulated amounts
Trace the disposal of the 300 replaced laptops to the vendor settlement and the write-off computation, testing the disposal loss amount
Test that the disposal loss is presented separately from the depreciation charge and evaluate whether the four-year life remains appropriate given the 20-month replacement
Physically inspect a sample of laptops issued to staff to confirm they are in use
procedures.trap_explanation: Inspecting laptops confirms the assets exist, but the flagged risks are computational accuracy and the classification of disposal losses — whether a laptop is on a desk says nothing about how its depreciation was calculated or presented.

scenarios.client_context: A hospital chain ordered EUR 4 million of imaging consumables in December with delivery scheduled across Q1; the client invoiced and recognized revenue on 28 December when goods were segregated in its warehouse under a bill-and-hold arrangement. The contract lacks explicit customer acceptance of the hold terms, storage is in a general racking area, and the sales director's bonus depends on hitting the annual target, which this deal clinches exactly.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Revenue may have been recognized without control transferring — segregated but not separately identified goods with unproven customer acceptance may not be a genuine sale.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Recognition in December for goods delivered in Q1 risks misstating the period of revenue.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Storage fees charged to the customer in the arrangement may be misapplied in the transaction price.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the contract for bill-and-hold terms, customer acceptance, and reasons for the arrangement, and evaluate whether control criteria are met
Observe the segregated inventory area, verifying the goods are separately identified and not available for other customers
Trace the actual dispatches in Q1 to despatch documents and test the timing of revenue recognition against transfer of control
Recalculate the transaction price including the storage charge and test whether the arrangement's economics are appropriately reflected
Confirm the year-end receivable balance with the hospital chain
procedures.trap_explanation: A receivable confirmation shows the customer acknowledges a debt, but the flagged risks are whether control of the goods transferred in December and whether recognition was premature — customers confirming balances do not validate bill-and-hold criteria, and the sales director's bonus incentive makes management assertion insufficient.

scenarios.line_item: Marketplace commission revenue — principal vs agent
scenarios.client_context: The marketplace lists third-party sellers' goods, takes a 15% commission, and recognizes total selling price as revenue with the sellers' share as cost of sales. The platform holds inventory in its own fulfilment centres, handles returns and refunds, and its terms state the customer's contract for defective goods is with the seller. Total GMV grew to EUR 300 million this year.

assertions_high_risk.classification: Holding inventory, handling returns and facing refund exposure may indicate principal status, making net commission presentation a misclassification that overstates revenue 6-fold.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Computation of the sellers' share, refunds and fees across EUR 300 million GMV is error-prone.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Revenue disaggregation and the basis of presentation must reflect the correct principal or agent conclusion.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the contract terms against control indicators (inventory, returns, pricing, credit risk) and conclude on principal versus agent classification
Recalculate gross revenue, commission and seller share for a sample of orders, tracing to platform transaction logs
Test that refunds and returns are recorded consistently with the party bearing the exposure
Inspect the revenue note's disaggregation and policy wording against the concluded classification
Enquire of the CFO why gross presentation was chosen and document management's rationale
procedures.trap_explanation: Management's rationale explains the policy choice but is not evidence it is correct; the flagged risk is misclassification driven by the platform's own exposure to returns and inventory — that requires evaluation of contract terms and control indicators, not the CFO's justification.

scenarios.line_item: Standard costing variances in cost of sales
scenarios.client_context: Finished-goods cost of sales is relieved at standard cost, with purchase-price, usage and volume variances swept to P&L quarterly. Timber prices rose 35% during the year but the standard was only updated in October, and EUR 2.8 million of unfavourable purchase-price variances sits in the variance account with a EUR 1.9 million favourable volume variance netted against it — awaiting the plant manager's sign-off, whose bonus depends on plant margin over standard.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Stale standards plus gross-netting of variances may misstate both cost of sales and closing inventory valuation; sweeping variances entirely to P&L when some belong in inventory distorts margins.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Netting purchase-price variances against volume variances misclassifies the nature of the differences, obscuring over/under-recovery.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Variances pending the interested plant manager's sign-off may include posting errors or unsupported adjustments.

procedures.procedure: Test the standard-setting process, evaluating whether the October update reflects actual timber input prices and reasonable usage rates
Recalculate the variance sweep for each quarter and evaluate whether variances should be allocated between cost of sales and closing inventory
Trace a sample of variance postings to production orders, goods-received notes and invoice prices to verify the variances are genuine
Test the cut-off of the Q4 variance postings and whether the pending net position was resolved before year end
Physically inspect timber stock in the yard and compare quantities to the perpetual records
procedures.trap_explanation: Counting timber verifies inventory quantities, but the flagged risks concern variance computation, allocation between P&L and inventory, and classification — physical counts do not address how variances were calculated or where they were swept.

scenarios.line_item: Consignment inventory held at customer sites
scenarios.client_context: Draft beer kegs worth EUR 6 million sit at bars and stadiums under consignment: title passes on tap connection. Reconciliation relies on field sales teams' quarterly counts recorded in a mobile app; two regions' Q4 counts were not performed after a sales-manager dispute, and the app has no edit-logging, so prior counts can be silently revised.

assertions_high_risk.existence: Unperformed Q4 counts in two regions mean recorded consignment balances may not physically exist, and without edit-logging prior counts could be manipulated.
assertions_high_risk.rights_and_obligations: Kegs already tapped by customers may have passed title but remain recorded as the client's inventory.

procedures.procedure: Perform or observe independent counts at a risk-based sample of customer sites in the two uncounted regions and reconcile to the app records
Inspect the consignment agreements' title-passing terms and test whether tapped kegs remain in the inventory system
Obtain the app's back-end data extract and test for revisions to prior-period counts where edit-logging is absent
For slow-moving kegs at stadiums, evaluate NRV given keg freshness limits and seasonal demand
Send confirmations to the largest bars requesting confirmation of quantities of the client's branded kegs held
Review the production records for kegs filled during the year
procedures.trap_explanation: Production volumes show what was filled, not what remains at customer sites; the flagged risks are existence of uncounted kegs and title having passed on tapped stock — neither is addressed by reviewing brewery output.

scenarios.client_context: Broiler flocks are valued at fair value less costs to sell based on an internal model of average live weight per bird and market price per kilo. Feed-conversion rates deteriorated 12% after a disease challenge in the autumn, so birds are reaching target weight a week later; the model still assumes the historical 38-day cycle, and year-end slaughter-house price lists dropped 8% post year end.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The model's stale 38-day cycle assumption overstates average weight, and the post-year-end price drop may be an adjusting event for the fair-value measurement.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Disease challenges raise the risk that bird mortality is understated and recorded flock numbers exceed live birds.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Biological asset movements and valuation methodology require disclosure, including the effect of the disease challenge.

procedures.procedure: Observe flock counts at a sample of houses, reconciling to the internal model's bird population and mortality records
Involve an auditor's expert to reperform the fair-value computation using actual post-disease growth rates and current market prices per kilo
Evaluate the post-year-end slaughter price lists as evidence of fair value at the reporting date and test the measurement and any related disclosure
Test the completeness of flock records for newly placed houses, tracing chick placements to hatchery invoices
Confirm feed purchases and quantities with the feed supplier
procedures.trap_explanation: Feed confirmations verify purchase volumes, but the flagged risks are the fair value of live birds under a stale growth model, whether flock numbers are real after disease losses, and price-based disclosure — feed tonnage does not measure any of these.

scenarios.client_context: The chain added 30 leased store locations, capitalizing lease payments over the term using a single 6% incremental borrowing rate for all stores. Ten leases include six rent-free months and EUR 400,000 of leasehold improvements funded by the chain that revert to the lessor at term end; the lease tracker spreadsheet was built by a trainee and the 6% rate was taken from a competitor's annual report rather than the chain's own borrowing terms.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A borrowed competitor discount rate, unadjusted rent-free periods, and omitted lessor-reverting improvements may misstate RoU asset measurement.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Leases missing from the trainee's spreadsheet would omit RoU assets entirely.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Initial measurement computations across 30 leases in a spreadsheet are error-prone.

procedures.procedure: Independently derive the incremental borrowing rate from the chain's own financing terms and reperform the initial measurement for a sample of leases
Test the rent-free periods' effect on the payment schedule and whether leasehold improvements that revert to lessors are included in the RoU asset or depreciated separately
Reconcile the lease tracker to signed lease agreements held by legal, testing for leases omitted from the tracker
Test spreadsheet integrity for formula errors and input links for the 30 new locations
Visit a sample of the new stores to confirm the premises are occupied and trading
procedures.trap_explanation: Visiting stores confirms the leases are real, but the flagged risks concern measurement — the discount rate, rent-free periods, and improvements — and completeness of the tracker; a store being open says nothing about whether its RoU asset was measured correctly.

scenarios.client_context: As lessor, the REIT charges tenants base rent plus 8% of turnover above a threshold. Two anchor tenants' reported turnover declined 15-20% this year, reducing variable receipts, while a third moved to an audited-sales clause requiring certified statements. Tenant sales data arrives via PDF emails keyed into the ledger by one analyst, and the December quarter's variable income estimate was booked at the analyst's forecast rather than from tenants' certified statements.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: PDF-based, manually keyed sales statements risk tenants' turnover being understated or never submitted, understating variable lease income.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Forecast-based December recognition instead of tenant-certified statements may misstate the quarter's variable income.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The anchor tenants' declining sales and any lease modifications need evaluation for impairment of lease income streams.

procedures.procedure: Trace a sample of tenants' certified sales statements into the ledger, and for non-certifying tenants reconcile reported turnover to footfall and other independent indicators
Test the December quarter estimate against the certified statements received after year end and evaluate whether the estimate was reasonable and appropriately revised
Evaluate whether the anchors' declining sales trigger lease modifications or impairment of the associated income streams and receivables
Reconcile the tenant population in the sales-clause schedule to the executed lease population to test completeness of tenants subject to turnover rent
Inspect the shopping centres' common-area maintenance expense invoices
procedures.trap_explanation: Inspecting operating expense invoices is unrelated to the flagged risks: understated tenant turnover, forecast-based variable income, and impairment of income streams — none of which is addressed by verifying property opex.

scenarios.client_context: The client migrated to a new HR system mid-year; guards' shift and wage data were imported by the vendor, and legacy employee records with no leaver flag were also migrated. Monthly payroll runs 4,500 employees paid per shift logs; the new system lets the operations manager add 'casual' employees without HR review, and an anonymous tip-off alleges two regional offices pay guards who left months ago. The year-end payroll reconciliation to the general ledger has a persistent 2% difference the payroll team cannot explain.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Migrated legacy records and unreviewed casual additions create a ghost-employee risk — payroll expense for people who perform no shifts.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The unexplained 2% ledger reconciliation difference suggests processing errors across the migrated data.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: The unexplained difference could also indicate payroll costs omitted from the ledger.

procedures.procedure: Test the HR system migration: reconcile employee master data before and after cutover, and identify migrated legacy records lacking active flags
For a sample of casual employees added by the operations manager, trace shift logs, site sign-in records, and bank account details distinct from other employees
Investigate the 2% payroll-to-ledger reconciliation difference by recomputing the payroll journal for two months
Compare active employee lists to site deployment rosters for the two flagged regions and enquire of site supervisors independent of the operations manager
Test that December payroll is recorded in the correct period by tracing the payment run dates to bank debits
Enquire of the payroll manager whether the migration was successful and whether she considers the payroll reliable
procedures.trap_explanation: The payroll manager's opinion is a management assertion, not evidence; the flagged risks — ghost employees, an unexplained 2% difference, and unreviewed casual additions — require substantive testing of master data, shift logs, and the reconciliation, especially as the tip-off implies management-level involvement.

scenarios.client_context: Employees receive RSUs vesting over four years subject to continued service; the valuation and expense model is maintained by the CFO's office using a Black-Scholes estimate updated annually. This year the company repriced underwater awards for the second time, granted a special tranche to the founding team with performance conditions tied to 'sustained product engagement', and the model still uses the pre-repricing volatility from the 2021 IPO year.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Stale IPO-era volatility and unmodelled repricing effects may misstate the fair value of awards and the expense.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: The founding team's vague performance condition may not meet the definition of a vesting condition, and 'engagement' is defined by the same executives receiving the awards.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Late grants and the repriced tranches may not all be captured in the expense model.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the grant and repricing approvals, testing the population of awards in the model against the cap table and board minutes
Evaluate the model's inputs — volatility, expected life, and the effect of the two repricings — against current market evidence for comparable listed SaaS companies
Assess whether 'sustained product engagement' is a properly defined performance or service condition, and how the founders' tranche was valued and expensed
Recalculate the quarterly expense for a sample of employee groups, testing vesting schedules and forfeiture estimates against leaver data
Test that the equity-settled awards are not classified as cash-settled in the expense note
Confirm the total share capital and number of shares issued with the company registrar at year end
procedures.trap_explanation: The registrar confirms issued shares, but the flagged risks are the expense computation — stale volatility, repricing effects, ill-defined performance conditions — and completeness of awards in the model; the share register says nothing about expense measurement.

scenarios.client_context: Maintenance contracts are billed annually in advance; the deferred income schedule releases revenue evenly over 12 months from each invoice. Mid-year the standard contract changed to include two safety inspections at fixed months, and a sales campaign in December billed 18-month contracts at a discount while the schedule continues to release on a 12-month straight-line basis.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Releasing 18-month billings over 12 months front-loads revenue and understates the deferred income balance at year end.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Discounted contracts with distinct inspection services may need revenue allocated between the service obligation and inspections, changing the release pattern.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: December billings entered late may never reach the deferred income schedule.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate the deferred income release for a sample of December and 18-month contracts, testing the release basis against the service period
Evaluate whether the bundled inspections are distinct services and whether the transaction price should be allocated between them, including the discount
Reconcile the December billing run to the deferred income schedule to test all billed contracts are deferred
Trace a sample of invoices to contract start dates and confirm the release begins in the correct month
Send confirmations to a sample of building owners confirming their annual maintenance billing
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirming billings with customers verifies amounts invoiced, but the flagged risks are the internal release pattern — 18-month contracts on a 12-month basis — and the completeness of the schedule; customer confirmations cannot test how the client amortizes what it billed.

scenarios.client_context: The holding company wrote off EUR 5 million of shareholder loans to the founder's son's hospitality venture this year, recorded as an investment impairment with no tax effect computed. The loans had no fixed repayment terms, the venture's only asset is a hotel under construction with development land, and the write-off was approved by the founder alone at a board meeting with no independent directors. No related-party disclosure was drafted.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The impairment measure relies on the venture's recoverable value; the under-construction hotel and land may support partial recovery, and a full write-off may be excessive or premature.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The related-party nature of the loans and their write-off require disclosure, which was not drafted.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Writing off shareholder loans as investment impairment may misclassify the loss, including any concealed distribution character.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the loan agreements, board minutes, and the venture's financials, and evaluate whether the full write-off is supported by recoverable value evidence
Evaluate the classification of the write-off — impairment, related-party credit loss, or constructive distribution — and its accounting treatment
Test the completeness of related-party disclosures against the register of related parties, including the son's venture and any other family entities
Assess the tax treatment of the write-off and whether the omitted tax effect is material
Obtain a management representation that all related-party relationships are disclosed
procedures.trap_explanation: A representation about related-party completeness is insufficient on its own where the founder alone approved the write-off and controls the information environment; the flagged risks — valuation of the loans and full disclosure — require substantive inspection of agreements and independent identification of family entities, not assurance from the interested party's representative.

scenarios.line_item: Revenue processed through a migrated ERP system
scenarios.client_context: The client migrated its ERP mid-year; order-to-cash data was converted by the vendor in a phased cutover with parallel running for six weeks. After parallel running ended, a mapping error caused credits for volume rebates to post to the wrong customer accounts, and the year-end system-generated revenue report was built by IT using an undocumented query. December revenue grew 18% month-on-month, partly attributed to order backlog release after the migration stabilized.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The rebate mapping error and the undocumented revenue report query may misstate revenue data across the period after cutover.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Backlog released after migration may include duplicated or corrupted orders converted twice during the phased cutover.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Orders stuck in the migration queue may never have reached the revenue ledger.

procedures.procedure: Test the migration cutover: reconcile order and invoice totals before, during, and after parallel running, investigating duplicated or dropped records
Reperform the year-end revenue report using an independently built query and reconcile to the general ledger
Trace the volume-rebate credits to correct customer accounts and assess whether misposting affected revenue recognition
Test December and January despatch dates around year end for orders released from the migration backlog to confirm correct cut-off
Confirm year-end receivable balances with the largest customers
procedures.trap_explanation: Customer balance confirmations verify receivables exist, but the flagged risks are inside the ERP — mapping errors, duplicated converted orders, and an undocumented report query — none of which is addressed by customers agreeing their statements.

scenarios.line_item: Trade receivables recorded in a cloud billing system
scenarios.client_context: All customer billing runs on a third-party cloud platform that also bills on the client's behalf; the client has no direct access to the underlying database. The platform's SOC 1 Type II report covers the year to October but the client's year end is December, leaving a two-month period with no assurance report, and the platform had a rate-table change in November affecting processing fees billed. The client's receivables grew 45% with the platform's new merchant onboarding.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The November rate-table change during the uncovered two-month period may misstate the billed fees and receivables.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Without direct database access, the client relies entirely on the platform's processing; fictitious or duplicated merchant balances would be difficult to detect.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Rapid merchant onboarding with no assurance over the uncovered period raises allowance adequacy questions.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the SOC 1 Type II report's scope, period, and control deficiencies, and test the client's complementary user entity controls
For the uncovered November-December period, perform direct substantive procedures: reconcile billing extracts to bank settlements and merchant statements
Test the November rate-table change: recalculate a sample of billed fees before and after the change
Test the allowance for newly onboarded merchants against settlement default experience
Review the platform's marketing materials describing its billing accuracy guarantees
procedures.trap_explanation: The provider's marketing claims are not audit evidence; the flagged risks — billing accuracy through the uncovered rate-change period and the existence of rapidly onboarded merchant balances — require substantive testing and the SOC 1 evaluation, not vendor assurances about its own service.

scenarios.line_item: Financial guarantee issued to a joint venture lender
scenarios.client_context: To secure the JV's EUR 30 million project facility, the client issued a guarantee covering 60% of the balance plus a first-demand undertaking for the first EUR 3 million. No liability was recognized; the finance director argues the guarantee was issued 'in the ordinary course' because parent companies routinely support JVs.
