The JV missed two milestone payments in Q4, its project is 30% over budget, and the lender has made informal enquiries about the EUR 3 million undertaking.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: The guarantee may meet the definition of a financial guarantee liability requiring initial recognition at fair value; no liability was recorded.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The JV's over-budget project and missed milestones increase the likelihood of a call, requiring the liability to be measured at the higher of loss allowance and initial fair value less amortization.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Contingent guarantee terms, the undertaking, and the lender's enquiries require disclosure as a contingent liability or provision.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the guarantee and undertaking documents and evaluate whether they meet the liability recognition definition rather than remaining a mere contingency
Evaluate measurement of the guarantee liability, considering the JV's budget overrun, missed milestones, and the lender's enquiries as loss evidence
Discuss with the client's lawyers the enforceability of the first-demand undertaking and the probability of calls
Test whether the guarantee, its maximum exposure, and the JV's difficulties are disclosed
Review minutes of JV board meetings for the year
procedures.trap_explanation: JV minutes may reveal project context, but the flagged risks are the client's own liability recognition, its measurement, and disclosure — legal conclusions about the guarantee documents and the lender's demand probability are not addressed by reading the JV's meeting minutes.

scenarios.line_item: Expected credit loss overlays on lease receivables
scenarios.client_context: The lessor's ECL model for its EUR 200 million lease book uses PD curves by asset class with a single macroeconomic scenario (base case). The credit committee applies quarterly management overlays 'for rounding' without documentation; this year overlays totalled EUR 4.2 million releases, mostly reversing earlier overlays. Two sectors in the book — construction and haulage — deteriorated sharply in H2, but the model's PD curves were last refreshed two years ago.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Stale PD curves, a single scenario, and undocumented overlay releases may understate ECL for deteriorating sectors.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Undocumented overlays reversing prior provisions distort the model's arithmetic and comparability.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Overlay movements and methodology changes require disclosure in the credit-risk note.

procedures.procedure: Test the overlay governance: inspect credit committee minutes and documentation supporting each quarterly overlay and its release
Involve an auditor's expert to evaluate the PD curves and single-scenario approach against current macroeconomic forecasts for construction and haulage
Perform retrospective review comparing previously modelled losses against actual write-offs to assess model bias
Test whether overlay movements, the two-year-old PD refresh, and scenario methodology are disclosed
Send confirmations to a sample of lessees confirming lease balances outstanding
procedures.trap_explanation: Lessee confirmations verify recorded receivable balances exist, but the flagged risks are measurement of expected losses — stale curves, undocumented overlay releases — and disclosure; agreeing balances with lessees does not test the loss model.

scenarios.line_item: Warranty provision classified by an AI complaint tool
scenarios.client_context: Warranty costs are provided using historical claim rates, but this year a machine-learning model was deployed to auto-classify customer complaints into 'warranty-eligible' versus 'user-error', feeding the provision's claims data. The model was trained on two years of old product lines and has never been validated against a new smart-appliance range that already shows 3x the complaint rate; claims rejected by the model are never reviewed, and the provision fell 20% despite the rising complaints.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Claims auto-rejected as user-error without review may omit genuine warranty obligations, understating the provision.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A model trained on old product lines may systematically under-estimate the new range's 3x claim rate.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Use of the AI classification and its effect on the provision estimate may need disclosure as a significant estimate.

procedures.procedure: Validate the model's classification: manually re-classify a risk-based sample of auto-rejected complaints for the smart range and quantify misclassification
Compare the model's implied claim rates for the new range against actual service-centre claim volumes and engineer job reports
Evaluate the model's training data vintage and design, including whether product-line shifts require retraining or expert involvement
Test whether the provision movement reconciles to claims data and whether the AI-driven estimate is disclosed
Inspect the appliance assembly line quality-control records for the year
procedures.trap_explanation: Factory quality records show production-line defect controls, but the flagged risks are in the claims classification — rejected complaints and stale training data — and the resulting provision measurement; production QC inspection does not test whether warranty claims were correctly classified or provided for.

scenarios.line_item: Onerous lease on an exited flagship store
scenarios.client_context: The brand exited its flagship store two years into a ten-year lease with 4.5 years remaining at EUR 2.4 million per annum, recognizing a provision for unavoidable lease costs less expected sublease income. The agent's sublease marketing report quotes 'headline' rents while actual lettings on the street have signed at 40% below headline, and the provision has not been updated since the exit despite two failed sublease negotiations and a repair obligation to restore the premises before handover.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Using headline rather than achievable rents overstates sublease income and understates the onerous lease provision, and restoration costs may be omitted.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: The failed negotiations suggest additional unavoidable costs not in the provision's scope.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Changes in the provision and the basis of the sublease assumption require disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate the provision using market evidence of actual lettings on the street, evaluating the achievability of the agent's headline-rent assumption
Evaluate the effect of the two failed negotiations on expected sublease timing and income, testing whether the provision reflects current conditions
Inspect the lease's dilapidation and restoration clauses and test whether restoration costs are included in the provision
Assess the objectivity of the leasing agent's report, given their interest in marketing the property, and obtain independent letting comparables
Visit the exited store to confirm it is vacant and available for subletting
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirming the store is empty verifies the facts of the exit, but the flagged risks are the provision's measurement — optimistic headline rents and omitted restoration costs — which a site visit cannot test.

scenarios.client_context: An IP-owning subsidiary charges a 3% revenue royalty to all group entities using its extraction patents, adjusted quarterly via top-side journals booked by group tax. Two operating subsidiaries recorded the royalty in cost of sales while others recorded it in operating expenses, one subsidiary disputed its liability and has not paid for three quarters, and the arm's-length benchmarking study supporting the 3% rate is five years old while patent coverage now differs substantially across entities.

assertions_high_risk.classification: Inconsistent classification between cost of sales and operating expenses distorts comparability and segment gross margins.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: A stale benchmarking study may no longer support the 3% rate as arm's length, with tax adjustment risk.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: The disputed subsidiary's unpaid quarters raise whether the charge reflects actual IP usage by each entity.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the intercompany licence agreements and map patent usage by entity to the royalty base, testing the disputed subsidiary's usage
Evaluate whether the five-year-old benchmarking study still supports the 3% rate, engaging a transfer-pricing specialist for updates
Test the consistency of royalty classification across entities and the elimination of the charge in consolidation
Test the quarterly top-side journal computation: recalculate 3% against each entity's reported revenue and confirm correct cut-off at year end
Confirm intercompany balances with the IP subsidiary's counterparties
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirming intercompany balances verifies what each side recorded, but the flagged risks are the royalty rate's arm's-length support, classification consistency, and whether charges reflect actual patent usage — none of which balance confirmation resolves.

scenarios.client_context: The company capitalized EUR 3.8 million of costs for 'building the brand': agency fees, a festival sponsorship, and an in-house creative team's salaries, alongside genuine packaging design costs. The finance team has no project-by-project ledger, so capitalized amounts are tracked in a spreadsheet reconciled only annually, and the marketing director — whose budget is praised for capitalization reducing opex — approves what is capitalized.

assertions_high_risk.classification: Sponsorship and promotion costs may not qualify for capitalization as intangible brand assets, and salaries of staff on general marketing activities may be misclassified.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Without a project ledger, capitalized costs may include items with no identifiable asset.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Amortization of capitalized brand costs with uncertain useful lives may be misstated.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the accounting framework's criteria for brand capitalization and test each capitalized cost type — agency fees, sponsorship, salaries, packaging design — against those criteria
Vouch a sample of capitalized costs to invoices, timesheets, and project documentation identifying the specific asset created
Reconcile the capitalization spreadsheet to the general ledger and test the completeness and arithmetic of the amortization computation
Evaluate the marketing director's approval role and the incentive created by capitalization for classifying costs
Test that genuine design costs are amortized over the correct period by inspecting the useful life assessment
Confirm the sponsorship fee paid to the festival organizer
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirming the sponsorship was genuinely paid verifies a payment occurred, but the flagged risks are whether that payment qualifies for capitalization at all and the accuracy of the spreadsheet tracking it — a payment confirmation does not make promotion spend an intangible asset.

scenarios.client_context: The group claimed government wage subsidies for staff furloughed during restrictions, recognizing EUR 2.9 million of subsidy income when claims were submitted. Auditors of the scheme publish error-rate statistics; the group's claims were prepared by an outsourced payroll bureau using estimated rather than actual furlough hours, the group kept staff rostered for delivery services during the claimed periods, and the scheme's clawback window is open with compliance audits randomly selecting claimants.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Claims based on estimated hours for staff actually rostered may not qualify, so recognized income may not have occurred.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Estimate-based claims need later truing to actual hours; the difference has not been computed.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Government grant accounting and the clawback exposure require disclosure, including conditions attached.

procedures.procedure: Recompute a sample of claims using actual furlough records and rosters, testing whether rostered delivery staff were wrongly claimed
Inspect the scheme's conditions and the group's evidence of compliance, including the bureau's claim files and the group's own rosters and timesheets
Evaluate whether claims recognized on submission comply with the framework's conditions-based recognition or should follow the grant's assurance requirements
Assess the clawback exposure quantitatively and test whether contingency disclosure is made
Review the payroll bureau's service organization report for the period
Confirm total payroll costs with the group's bank for the subsidy periods
procedures.trap_explanation: Bank-verified payroll totals confirm what staff cost, but the flagged risks are whether the claimed furlough hours were genuine and whether the claims qualify — cash paid to rostered staff proves nothing about which hours were subsidized.

scenarios.client_context: Fee earners log time to WIP daily; unbilled amounts transfer to revenue only on invoice. Year-end unbilled WIP is EUR 12 million, up 40%, concentrated in a litigation practice where the fee arrangement is 'no win, no fee' for a major case set for trial next year. Partners review their own WIP for recoverability, and the firm's profitability metric — reported to the bank covenant — includes unbilled revenue growth.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Conditional-fee litigation WIP may not be recoverable at full value; partner self-review of their own WIP is not an objective recoverability assessment.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Time logged for the no-win-no-fee case may never convert to revenue, so recognized unbilled amounts may not be genuine income.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: The covenant link to unbilled growth creates an incentive to omit WIP write-downs, while late time entries may be missing.

procedures.procedure: For the litigation practice, evaluate the conditional fee arrangement and assess WIP recoverability against outcome probability, using counsel's opinion where appropriate
Test a sample of unbilled time entries to fee-earner time records, engagement letters, and evidence of work performed
Evaluate the firm's WIP review control given partners review their own balances, and test whether write-down decisions are documented and challenged
Perform cut-off testing on time entries recorded after year end for work performed before it, and test that December's recorded revenue includes all recoverable WIP
Discuss with the firm's bank the covenant calculation basis
procedures.trap_explanation: Talking to the bank clarifies covenant definitions but provides no evidence about WIP recoverability or whether logged time represents real work; the flagged risks lie in the firm's own estimates and records, not the lender's interpretation.

scenarios.line_item: Carbon credits held for voluntary offset programme
scenarios.client_context: The airline buys voluntary carbon credits to market 'carbon-neutral fares', capitalizing them as intangible assets at cost. This year it bought EUR 6 million of credits from two reforestation projects; one project was suspended from the registry in November over permanence doubts, and no impairment was recognized because 'the trees still exist'. Credits are revalued to market via a broker's indicative price list that the airline's sustainability team negotiates with the same broker selling new credits.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Registry suspension questions the suspended project's credits' value; broker-negotiated 'market prices' from an interested counterparty may not be fair value.
assertions_high_risk.rights_and_obligations: Suspended registry status may mean the client no longer holds transferable, enforceable rights to the credits.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Claims of carbon-neutral fares depend on credit quality, creating a reputational disclosure dimension.

procedures.procedure: Confirm credit ownership and registry status for both projects, including whether the suspended project's credits remain transferable
Evaluate impairment of the suspended project's credits, considering registry findings, permanence doubts, and recoverable value evidence from independent sources
Assess the objectivity of the broker's price list given the broker also sells new credits, and benchmark against independent carbon-credit trading platforms
Test whether credit holdings, the suspension, and the neutrality claim's basis are disclosed
Physically inspect the reforested areas via satellite imagery or site visit for a sample of projects
procedures.trap_explanation: Trees being visible verifies planting occurred, but the flagged risks are the credits' registry status, value, and ownership rights — a suspended project's standing forest may still hold impaired or non-transferable credits.

scenarios.client_context: The exchange holds customers' bitcoin and ether in a mix of its own hot wallets and a custodian's cold storage, recording a custody asset and matching liability at cost per token. Two platform outages in December prevented customer withdrawals, an internal wallet reconciliation showed a 40-token shortfall 'under investigation' since October, and the exchange switched its proof-of-reserves auditor. Token prices fell 55% during the year while the balance sheet still carries cost.

assertions_high_risk.existence: The unexplained 40-token shortfall suggests recorded custody assets may not exist in full.
assertions_high_risk.rights_and_obligations: Customer segregation and whether the exchange holds assets on trust affects the balance sheet gross-up and ownership risk disclosure.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Carrying tokens at cost during a 55% price fall may misstate the asset and liability measurement basis required by the framework.

procedures.procedure: Obtain on-chain evidence: agree recorded token holdings to blockchain addresses and the custodian's confirmation, including the shortfall investigation
Evaluate the accounting policy for custody assets and liabilities — measurement basis, segregation, and gross-up — against the framework
Investigate the December outages and the shortfall, including management's response and whether customer assets were rehypothecated
Assess the reason for the proof-of-reserves auditor change and the adequacy of reserve disclosures
Recalculate the customer liability from the order ledger to the token inventory
Confirm the exchange's bank balances used for fiat customer segregation
procedures.trap_explanation: Bank confirmations verify segregated fiat, but the flagged risks concern token holdings on-chain, the measurement of crypto assets in a 55% price fall, and ownership rights over customers' digital assets — fiat balances say nothing about whether the tokens exist or how they are accounted for.

scenarios.client_context: The bank's EUR 1.1 billion SME book provisions on a collective model with PD/LGD parameters last validated three years ago. This year the portfolio mix shifted toward collateral-light working-capital facilities, arrears rose from 2% to 4.5%, and the credit department booked a EUR 3.5 million 'model recalcibration' release in December without documentation. Two large hospitality borrowers restructured their loans in November and were returned to 'performing' without the restructure being modelled.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Stale PD/LGD parameters, a portfolio shift, and restructured loans treated as performing may understate collective provisions.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The undocumented December release lacks support and reverses provisions without an evidential basis.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Provision movements, the release, and forbearance treatment require disclosure, including staged classification.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the PD/LGD parameter vintage against the portfolio's changed mix and current arrears experience, involving a credit-risk expert
Inspect support for the December release, testing who approved it and the evidence for 'recalibration'
Test the two restructured hospitality exposures: evaluate the classification of 'cured' loans against the restructuring terms and forbearance disclosure
Perform retrospective model review of prior-year collective provisions against actual loss experience
Test that provision movements, the release, and forbearance are disclosed in the credit risk note
Confirm loan balances outstanding with a sample of SME borrowers
procedures.trap_explanation: Borrower confirmations verify principal balances exist, but the flagged risks are the loss model — stale parameters, an undocumented release, and restructures treated as performing — none of which balance confirmation addresses.

scenarios.line_item: Supplier finance arrangement and trade payables presentation
scenarios.client_context: The client joined a bank-led reverse factoring programme: the bank pays approved supplier invoices early and the client repays the bank on the suppliers' original due dates. EUR 90 million of programme payables remain inside trade payables with no disclosure of the arrangement's terms, carrying amounts, and liquidity risk. The largest participating supplier renegotiated its invoice pricing when it joined, and one bank in the programme signalled it may withdraw its facility next year.

assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Supplier finance arrangements' terms, carrying amounts, and liquidity concentration require disclosure; the EUR 90 million omission misleads analysts assessing working capital.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Whether the arrangement modifies the payable's nature (borrowing vs trade payable) affects classification and covenant definitions of leverage.
assertions_high_risk.rights_and_obligations: The withdrawal signal creates a refinancing/liquidity obligation that may need presentation as a liability or disclosed risk.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the programme agreements to identify terms, approved-invoice mechanics, and the accounting implications for classification
Test whether the arrangement's existence, carrying amounts, range of terms, and concentration risk are disclosed
Reconcile programme payables to bank statements of settlement and the repayment schedule, testing completeness of the disclosed amounts
Evaluate the effect of the bank's withdrawal signal on liquidity risk, covenant classification, and going concern support
Confirm programme payables balances directly with participating suppliers
procedures.trap_explanation: Supplier confirmations verify invoices exist, but the flagged risks are disclosure of the programme's terms, classification of the payables, and liquidity consequences of the bank's withdrawal — which confirming balances with suppliers does not address.

scenarios.line_item: Workers' compensation claims reserves — inflation assumption
scenarios.client_context: The insurer's claims reserves apply a claims-inflation factor of 4% per annum, unchanged for three years while wage inflation — the indexation basis for compensation payments — ran at 7-9%. The reserving actuary joined the company six months ago and has not yet performed a full reserve review; a portfolio of legacy claims from a construction book shows court awards trending above the factor, and the reserve note still describes the factor as 'consistent with recent experience'.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The outdated 4% inflation factor likely understates reserves, particularly for long-tail construction claims with wage-linked awards.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Reserve computations inheriting the factor misstate the technical provisions across the book.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The reserve note's description of inflation assumptions is inconsistent with actual experience and requires correction.

procedures.procedure: Involve an auditor's actuarial expert to independently assess the inflation factor against wage index data and court award trends, quantifying the shortfall
Perform retrospective review of prior-year reserves against actual claim settlements to test the adequacy and bias of assumptions
Test the reserving computation for a sample of construction-book claims, tracing payment histories and applying updated indexation
Evaluate the new actuary's review status and management's process for updating assumptions between full reviews
Test that the inflation assumption disclosed in the reserve note reflects the actual indexation basis and recent experience
Confirm reinsurance recoverable balances with the reinsurer
procedures.trap_explanation: Reinsurer confirmations verify recoverable balances exist, but the flagged risks are the understated gross reserves from a stale inflation factor and the misleading disclosure — recoverables are a separate balance and do not address the reserve measurement.

scenarios.line_item: Disposal group classified as held for sale
scenarios.client_context: The group committed in October to sell its rail-technology division for EUR 480 million, classified as held for sale with a EUR 35 million impairment on classification. The buyer can walk away if EU merger clearance is not obtained within nine months, and the competition authority has signalled concerns given the parties' combined market share. At year end the sale is 'highly probable' per management, but completion now also depends on the buyer raising financing that has not yet been underwritten. Divisional management, whose LTIP vests on completion, control the disposal-cost estimates.

assertions_high_risk.classification: Whether the sale remains highly probable given merger-clearance risk and ununderwritten buyer financing may require declassification back to held-and-used, reversing impairment and reinstating depreciation.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The EUR 35 million impairment on classification and disposal-cost estimates prepared by completion-incentivized divisional management may misstate the disposal group's carrying amount.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Held-for-sale presentation, the conditions to sale, and the completion dependency require disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the held-for-sale criteria at year end: inspect the sale agreement's conditions, merger-clearance status, and buyer financing evidence, and conclude on continued classification
Test the impairment computation on classification, including fair value less costs to sell, and challenge disposal-cost estimates prepared by incentivized divisional management
Obtain external legal opinion on the probability and timing of merger clearance and evaluate whether it affects classification or disclosure
Test that depreciation ceased appropriately on classification and that disclosures present the division's assets, liabilities, and the sale's conditions
Confirm the rail division's bank balances and facilities at year end with its banks
procedures.trap_explanation: Bank confirmations verify the division's cash and borrowings exist, but the flagged risks are whether held-for-sale classification survives the clearance and financing conditions and whether the impairment is properly measured — balance confirmations cannot address classification or impairment.

scenarios.line_item: Reinsurance recoverable on retroceded long-tail liability
scenarios.client_context: The cedant retrocedes a quota share of its long-tail disability book to three retrocessionaires, recognizing a EUR 210 million recoverable. One retro, rated A two years ago, was downgraded to BB in November and now disputes claim interpretations on the largest ceded treaty; the cedant estimates the recoverable on a 'treaty wording' basis the retro rejects. A collateral trust securing the BB retro's share fell 30% in value with the year's market fall, and no loss allowance was recorded because 'retros always pay eventually'.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The downgraded retro's ability to pay, the disputed claim interpretation, and the depleted collateral trust may require a material loss allowance on the recoverable.
assertions_high_risk.rights_and_obligations: The treaty-interpretation dispute questions whether the cedant holds enforceable rights to the amounts recorded.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Counterparty credit concentration, the dispute, and the collateral shortfall require disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Involve an auditor's expert to evaluate the recoverable's measurement, including the treaty-interpretation dispute's merits and probable outcomes
Assess the BB-rated retro's ability to pay: financial condition, regulatory status, and payment history since the downgrade, and evaluate the need for a loss allowance
Confirm the collateral trust's composition and market value at year end and test whether the shortfall is accounted for and disclosed
Obtain the reinsurer's confirmations of balances and reconcile to the cedant's treaty records, including the disputed interpretation
Test the credit-risk concentration and dispute disclosures in the reinsurance note
Vouch premium ceded to the retrocessionaires during the year to bank records
procedures.trap_explanation: Vouching premium payments shows the treaties were paid for, but the flagged risks are the recoverable's recoverability from a downgraded, disputing counterparty and the depleted collateral — past premium transfers do not evidence future claim payments.

scenarios.line_item: Recycling of foreign-currency translation gains from OCI on disposal
scenarios.client_context: The group sold its Latin American generics subsidiary, releasing EUR 120 million of accumulated FX translation losses from the translation reserve through P&L on recycling. Half the subsidiary's operations were transferred to the retained regional services entity before sale, whose functional currency the group also reassessed from USD to the parent's euro this year — moving EUR 40 million between reserves. The reserve movements are computed by group finance in a spreadsheet with no independent review, and the P&L release flatters EPS against the LTIP hurdle that would otherwise be missed.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The split of operations between sold and retained entities determines how much of the EUR 120 million belongs in recycling; the EUR 40 million functional-currency reassessment complicates the computation, and the unreviewed spreadsheet heightens error risk.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Whether the release should run through P&L, or partly remain in equity for the retained operations, is a classification risk with EPS consequences tied to the LTIP hurdle.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Reserve movements, the reassessment, and the recycling basis require clear disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the transfer of operations to the retained entity and determine the correct split of accumulated translation amounts between recycling on disposal and amounts retained in equity
Evaluate the functional-currency reassessment of the retained entity, testing whether the evidence genuinely supports the change and its EUR 40 million reserve effect
Recalculate the recycling computation from the reserve's opening balance, disposal documentation, and the spreadsheet's inputs, testing its integrity independently
Assess the LTIP hurdle proximity and management incentive for the release's timing and classification, performing additional procedures over reserve journals
Test that the reserve movements, the reassessment, and the disposal's recycling are disclosed and reconciled to the statement of changes in equity
Confirm the disposal proceeds received from the buyer's bank
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirming sale proceeds verifies the disposal's cash, but the flagged risks are how the EUR 120 million was split on recycling, the functional-currency reassessment, and spreadsheet accuracy — the amount received says nothing about the reserve mechanics.

scenarios.line_item: Lease modification: fixed payments renegotiated to variable
scenarios.client_context: Post-pandemic footfall left the group renegotiating all 60 of its leases. Two flagship leases were modified mid-year from fixed rent to base rent plus 5% of box-office takings — previously variable payments were negligible. The group treated the modifications as separate leases under the 'adding a right' logic because the landlord also granted signage rights, and continued the old measurement without remeasuring the lease liabilities. Box office is running 30% below the attendance assumptions used in the old liability measurement, and the landlord confirmed in writing the renegotiation 'replaces the existing rent structure entirely'.

assertions_high_risk.classification: Whether the modifications add a separate right (signage) or modify existing leases determines whether remeasurement is required — the 'replaces entirely' wording suggests a modification requiring liability remeasurement, not a new lease.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: If remeasurement applies, the discount rate and the new fixed-plus-variable structure must be re-measured; retaining stale attendance-based payments overstates or misstates the liability.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Remeasurement computations across 60 renegotiated leases are error-prone.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the modification agreements, including the signage rights and the 'replaces entirely' confirmation, and evaluate against the framework's modification-versus-separate-lease criteria
If modification accounting applies, reperform the remeasurement for the two flagships: revised payment structure, revised discount rate, and updated liability and RoU asset
Test the remaining renegotiated leases for correct treatment, sampling modification documents and the payment schedule updates
Evaluate box-office performance against the payment assumptions and assess whether the variable structure changes impairment analysis of the RoU assets
Test that lease modification accounting and the revised terms are disclosed
Confirm the annual fixed rent paid to the two flagship landlords
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirming rent paid verifies cash amounts, but the flagged risks are the classification of the modifications and the lease liabilities' remeasurement — a year's rent payment does not test whether the liability should have been remeasured under a new structure.

scenarios.line_item: Sovereign bond portfolio expected credit losses
scenarios.client_context: The bank holds EUR 3 billion of emerging-market sovereign bonds, at amortized cost in the banking book, with ECL modelled at stage 1 (12-month losses) using country PDs from a vendor model. In December the IMF published a debt-sustainability downgrade for the largest exposure country, its bond prices fell 35% year-to-date, and two rating agencies moved it to selective default watch. The bank's credit committee minute says 'prices are illiquid and noisy; fundamental analysis supports no stage transfer', written by the sovereign desk head whose bonus is tied to banking-book marks.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Objective default-likelihood evidence (rating watch, IMF downgrade, price collapse) may require significant-increase-in-risk assessment and stage 2 transfer, materially raising lifetime ECL.
assertions_high_risk.classification: The stage classification drives the ECL horizon; management's contrary conclusion from an incentivized desk head is a classification risk.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Sovereign concentration, staging, and the use of conflicting evidence require disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the staging assessment against objective default indicators — rating actions, IMF downgrade, and market prices — independent of the desk's view
Involve an auditor's credit expert to reperform sovereign PDs and quantify ECL under stage 2 lifetime measurement for the downgraded country
Assess the desk head's involvement and incentive, performing procedures over the credit committee's evidential support for 'noisy price' conclusions
Test whether bond prices used were observable and consistent across sources, and recalculate the portfolio's ECL computation
Test sovereign concentration, staging movements, and methodology disclosures in the credit-risk note
Confirm the bank's holdings of the sovereign bonds with the central securities depository
procedures.trap_explanation: CSD confirmation verifies the bonds are held, but the flagged risks are staging classification and ECL measurement amid default-likelihood evidence — confirming custody says nothing about whether the loss allowance is adequate.

scenarios.line_item: Equity-method investment with a different financial year-end
scenarios.client_context: The group holds 40% of a wind-farm JV, accounted for using the equity method. The JV reports to 30 September while the group's year end is 31 December; group finance rolls forward the JV's September results using a budget-based spread that last year captured 70% of the JV's actual Q4 profit. This year the JV commissioned a new farm in Q4 with grid-connection delays, and its CFO (seconded from the group) indicated informally that Q4 was 'below plan'. The carrying value equals 85% of the group's consolidated market capitalization, and no impairment indicators were documented in the group's year-end review.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The budget-based Q4 roll-forward with known below-plan performance may overstate share of profit and the carrying value; impairment indicators were not documented despite the investment's dominance of the group's market cap.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The roll-forward mechanics (last year capturing 70% of actuals) suggest systematic estimation error in the group's share.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Q4 events at the JV — commissioning and delays — must be reflected in the group's year-end accounts.

procedures.procedure: Obtain the JV's Q4 management accounts and supporting detail, and reperform the roll-forward from 30 September to 31 December, testing the budget-spread mechanism against actuals
Evaluate the group's Q4 share of JV profit against the grid-connection delays and below-plan indication, testing management's estimates
Perform impairment assessment of the equity-method carrying value, benchmarking against market capitalization and testing management's impairment-indicator review
Inspect the JV's audited 30 September financials, the auditor's report, and the shareholders' agreement for the group's rights, and evaluate consolidation-scope conclusions
Test the associate disclosures: year-end difference, roll-forward basis, and carrying-value reconciliation
Confirm the group's shareholding in the JV with the corporate registry
procedures.trap_explanation: The registry confirms the 40% holding exists, but the flagged risks are the Q4 roll-forward's accuracy, share-of-profit estimation, and impairment — the ownership percentage was never in doubt, so confirmation adds nothing to the flagged risks.

scenarios.line_item: Provision for a historical operational risk event
scenarios.client_context: In the prior year the bank's payment-processing platform misapplied FX spreads to 2 million retail transactions. Litigation is ongoing in two jurisdictions; the bank recognized EUR 15 million in the prior year and added nothing this year despite the lead regulator's draft decision in November quantifying redress at EUR 28-40 million, the class action expanding to business customers, and external counsel — engaged on a capped-fee basis — advising 'defensible but uncertain'. The CFO told the board that provision increases 'prejudge the litigation'.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The regulator's draft decision range of EUR 28-40 million against a EUR 15 million provision suggests material under-measurement; the duty to update estimates is not prejudiced by litigation.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: The expanded class (business customers) may create additional obligations outside the provision's scope.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Contingent liabilities, the draft decision, and sensitivity of the estimate require disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the regulator's draft decision, counsel's advice (assessing independence given the capped-fee engagement), and litigation filings to reassess the obligating event and measurement range
Recalculate the exposure using the regulator's range, the expanded claimant population, and remediation costs, comparing to the recognized provision
Test that the draft decision, the litigation's status, and the range of possible outcomes are disclosed, including contingent liabilities beyond the provision
Evaluate management's 'prejudice' rationale and assess whether the estimate reflects current evidence, documenting the effect of the CFO's position
Review the bank's operational-risk event register for other unprovisioned processing failures
Confirm the bank's legal fee accruals with the external counsel firm
procedures.trap_explanation: Counsel confirmations verify fee balances, but the flagged risks are the redress provision's measurement against the regulator's range and the completeness of the expanded claimant population — legal fee accounting is immaterial to whether the EUR 15 million is adequate.

scenarios.line_item: Revenue on modified enterprise shipping contracts
scenarios.client_context: During the freight-rate collapse the group renegotiated 200 enterprise contracts, converting fixed annual minimums into rate-per-TEU plus service credits for missed performance. Accounting treated each renegotiation as a contract modification 'accounted for as part of the existing contract', keeping original transaction-price allocations. For 30 contracts the negotiated outcome was economically a new pricing regime with added services (customs brokerage), and service credits issued in Q4 were netted against revenue rather than presented as separate fulfilment costs, understating both revenue and cost lines ahead of a debt covenant test on reported revenue.

assertions_high_risk.classification: Modifications that add distinct services at standalone pricing may require prospective treatment as separate contracts; netting service credits against revenue misclassifies fulfilment costs.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Retained original transaction-price allocations after renegotiation misstate revenue for the modified periods.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The covenant relevance of revenue and the netting presentation increase disclosure and fraud-risk considerations.

procedures.procedure: Inspect a sample of renegotiated contracts against modification criteria: whether customs brokerage is distinct and whether pricing reflects standalone selling prices, determining separate versus prospective treatment
Recompute revenue for the 30 affected contracts under the correct modification treatment and quantify the misstatement
Test the Q4 service credits: trace to issued credit notes, evaluate whether they are fulfilment costs presented gross, and test their completeness
Perform revenue cut-off testing around year end for modified contracts, tracing sailings and service completion to the recognition period
Evaluate the covenant pressure on reported revenue as a fraud-risk factor and test journal entries around the modification accounting
Confirm container volumes shipped under the 30 contracts with the enterprise customers
procedures.trap_explanation: Customer volume confirmations verify sailings occurred, but the flagged risks are the modification accounting treatment and the gross-versus-net presentation of service credits — volumes shipped do not resolve how a renegotiated contract should be accounted for.

scenarios.line_item: Client money segregation at a broker-dealer
scenarios.client_context: The broker holds client money in pooled trust accounts, reconciled to client ledgers daily by the operations team. This year the reconciliation template excluded a newly launched derivatives margin account, so EUR 18 million of client balances sat unsegregated in the firm's own account for four months; the breach was discovered in December and corrected pre-year-end, but two days of the reconciliation were performed by the firm's treasurer who also managed the firm's own-prop account, and the regulatory report of the breach has not yet been drafted.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: The excluded margin account shows client money populations can be incomplete in the reconciliation; other exclusions may exist.
assertions_high_risk.rights_and_obligations: Unsegregated client money mixed with the firm's own funds breaches trust obligations; the treasurer's dual role heightens misuse risk.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Whether the trust accounts contain client money at reported amounts requires evidence, given the breach history.

procedures.procedure: Obtain trust-account bank confirmations directly and reconcile to the client ledger at year end, testing for any remaining unsegregated balances
Test the completeness of the reconciliation population: map every client-money source account to the reconciliation template, investigating the margin exclusion's origin and any others
Test the December reconciliations performed by the treasurer: reperform them and trace movements between the trust and prop accounts during the breach window
Inspect the breach correction and evaluate whether the regulatory reporting obligation and the event require disclosure in the financial statements
Evaluate the segregation structure and daily reconciliation controls, including reviewer independence from the prop desk
Confirm trade receivable balances with a sample of institutional clients
procedures.trap_explanation: Institutional receivable confirmations verify trading debts owed to the firm, but the flagged risks are client money's segregation, completeness of reconciliations, and the trust breach — receivable balances are the firm's own assets and say nothing about client money custody.

scenarios.line_item: Dividend received from a hyperinflationary subsidiary
scenarios.client_context: The group's Turkish subsidiary declared a dividend equivalent to EUR 60 million, recognized as investment income in December. Türkiye is designated hyperinflationary, so the subsidiary's results are restated using the index and translated at closing rate — but the dividend was measured using the transaction-date spot rate applied to un-indexed local amounts. Currency controls mean dividends can only be paid into a blocked-currency account, two tranches are pending central-bank approval, and the group's income statement benefit offsets the hyperinflation restatement loss that would otherwise breach a net-interest covenant.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Using spot-at-transaction on un-indexed amounts in a hyperinflationary economy misstates the dividend's translated amount.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: The pending central-bank approval means part of the dividend may not be receivable — income for dividends that may never be distributable.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The currency-control restrictions, blocked funds, and covenant interplay require disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Recompute the dividend's translated amount under hyperinflationary accounting: indexed subsidiary amounts, closing-rate translation, and comparison to the recorded EUR 60 million
Inspect the subsidiary's distribution resolution and the central-bank approval status for each tranche, assessing recognition of pending tranches
Evaluate the blocked-currency account's transferability, enforceability of the group's rights, and any impairment of the trapped funds
Test the covenant computation's treatment of the hyperinflation loss and the dividend, and assess the incentive effect on recognition timing
Obtain confirmation of the blocked-currency account balances from the Turkish bank
Review the subsidiary's local statutory accounts for the prior year
procedures.trap_explanation: Reviewing prior-year statutory accounts shows historical performance, but the flagged risks are the dividend's translation under hyperinflationary rules, pending central-bank approvals, and the covenant effect — last year's local accounts do not address any of them.

scenarios.client_context: Four years ago the company signed a ten-year take-or-pay supply contract for specialty gases at fixed prices indexed to energy costs. Energy indexation has driven contract prices 60% above the current spot market, the fab's output is running at 55% of the contracted volumes assumed in the purchasing model, and a competitor's new plant has collapsed spot prices further. Purchasing maintains a spreadsheet quantifying the expected loss at EUR 4 million over the remaining term, but the model still assumes the original demand forecast, and the company negotiated a volume-reduction amendment in November that legal says does not release it from the take-or-pay minimums.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The loss computation based on stale demand forecasts understates the onerous commitment provision; contract prices above spot for six more years imply a much larger unavoidable loss.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: The November amendment's failure to release minimums means the full commitment remains, and any other onerous contracts may not be identified.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The nature, timing, and amount of the commitment and sensitivity of the estimate require disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the supply contract and the November amendment with external legal opinion on the enforceability of take-or-pay minimums
Reperform the loss computation using current fab utilization, demand forecasts, and forward energy and spot-price curves, benchmarking against independent market data
Test the completeness of onerous-contract screening across all long-term purchase agreements, reconciling the commitment register to signed contracts
Evaluate disclosure of the commitment's amount, remaining term, indexation exposure, and the amendment's effect
Test spreadsheet integrity and the sourcing of demand assumptions, challenging the purchasing team's inputs against the operations plan
Confirm the volumes of gases delivered during the year with the supplier
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirming deliveries verifies contract activity, but the flagged risks are the future loss on the unavoidable minimums, the completeness of onerous-contract screening, and disclosure — past deliveries do not measure the six remaining loss-making years.

scenarios.line_item: Segment reporting after an operating-model reorganization
scenarios.client_context: In July the group reorganized from three geographic divisions into two global product segments, with segment P&Ls rebuilt monthly on a new allocation model. The chief operating decision maker is now the executive committee; segment disclosures for the year were prepared on the old geographic basis 'for comparability' using a reconciliation with unexplained balancing figures of EUR 14 million. Inter-segment sales are reported at the old transfer prices, though the reorganization introduced a new cost-plus transfer regime mid-year, and one new segment combines a profitable services business with a loss-making legacy product line whose combined 'adjusted segment margin' is cited in the CEO's letter.

assertions_high_risk.classification: Reporting on the superseded geographic basis instead of the new reportable segments misclassifies the segment structure the CODM actually uses.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The EUR 14 million unexplained reconciliation differences and mixed transfer-pricing regimes undermine the segment measures' accuracy.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Unexplained 'adjusted segment margin' measures in the CEO letter risk non-compliant or misleading segment disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Identify the actual CODM and the segments used in internal reporting post-reorganization by inspecting executive committee packs and management accounts, and evaluate the reported segment basis against them
Reperform the reconciliation between the old geographic basis and the new segment basis, investigating the EUR 14 million balancing figures to their source
Test the inter-segment transfer pricing: old versus new cost-plus regime application, and whether the basis of inter-segment measurement is disclosed and consistent
Evaluate the completeness of segment disclosures: segment assets, expenses, and the reconciliation to consolidated totals under the new structure
Assess whether the 'adjusted segment margin' in the CEO letter is a compliant segment measure or requires reconciliation and relabeling
Confirm external revenue for a sample of major customers within each segment
procedures.trap_explanation: Customer revenue confirmations verify sales occurred, but the flagged risks are the segment structure reported, the reconciliation's unexplained differences, and disclosure quality — confirming external sales says nothing about which segment they belong to or how measures are defined.
